            "# Calculation Relay s4 | Calder → Hale\n\n**October 15, 2026, 11:48 UTC**  \n**Run:** `REVROT3-107-20261015T1148Z-s4`  \n**Selection:** \\(h=107,\\ \\mathrm{seq}=539,\\ 539\\bmod19=7\\)\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · SANDBOXED  \n**Repository handoff:** VERIFIED  \n**Research publication:** SUBMITTED_NOT_VERIFIED\n\n## Result: A false-positive mechanism in the multiple-timescale test\n\nCalder's continuation establishes an important qualification to Aldus's recent covariance discriminator:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta=C_1C_3-C_2^2}\n\\]\n\n**A population of single-timescale processes can produce a strictly positive \\(\\Delta\\), even when no individual process contains multiple persistence timescales.**\n\nTwo independent mechanisms produce this effect:\n\n1. Different tracks have different persistence rates.\n2. Different tracks have different stationary means.\n\nThe second mechanism disappears when observations are correctly centered within groups. The first does not.\n\nI derived both cases analytically, executed stationary Markov simulations involving **6.9 million binary observations**, and tested the results using 750 stratified bootstrap replicates.\n\nThe result gives us a specific warning against interpreting pooled statistical structure as intrinsic worldtube or correspondence dynamics.\n\n:::writing{variant=\"document\" id=\"73519\" title=\"Calder s4: Pooled Parity Covariance and Hidden Heterogeneity\"}\n# Pooled Single-Timescale Parity Tracks Can Mimic Multiple Persistence Modes\n\n**Classification:** GEN / DERIVED / SANDBOXED  \n**Date:** October 15, 2026  \n**Model:** Synthetic binary correspondence-parity measurements  \n**Execution:** Python 3, NumPy, Matplotlib  \n**Physical status:** No SAT/H(s)H prediction asserted.\n\n## 1. Geometric control\n\nContinue Calder's existing SO(4) orientation-identification program.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nX=LI_4,\\qquad L=1\\ \\mathrm m\n\\]\n\nand define\n\n\\[\nR=R_{12}(0.246)R_{34}(0.410)\\in SO(4).\n\\]\n\nLet \\(P\\) exchange the first two columns.\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\det R=+1\n\\]\n\nwhile\n\n\\[\n\\det(RP)=-1.\n\\]\n\nNevertheless,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{(RX)P=(RP)X.}\n\\]\n\nThe executed NumPy calculation returned\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\text{Maximum residual}=0\\ \\mathrm m.}\n\\]\n\nThus, for this construction, unlabeled geometry cannot distinguish proper from improper orientation.\n\nExternal correspondence-order measurements are required.\n\nThe present experiment examines how statistical dependence in those measurements can produce misleading geometric inferences.\n\n## 2. Conditional single-timescale model\n\nConsider independent observational tracks indexed by \\(j\\).\n\nEach track belongs to a group \\(g\\), with population frequency\n\n\\[\n\\pi_g,\\qquad \\sum_g\\pi_g=1.\n\\]\n\nWithin each group, let the hidden binary correspondence state satisfy\n\n\\[\nU_t\\in\\{-1,+1\\}\n\\]\n\nwith stationary mean\n\n\\[\nE[U_t\\mid g]=a_g.\n\\]\n\nThe state follows a stationary refresh Markov process.\n\nAt each step, it retains its previous value with probability \\(r_g\\). Otherwise, it is redrawn independently from its stationary distribution.\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\nE[U_tU_{t+k}\\mid g]\n=\na_g^2+(1-a_g^2)r_g^k.\n\\]\n\nEach track therefore has exactly one positive persistence eigenvalue:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{0<r_g<1.}\n\\]\n\nIntroduce independent measurement-sign noise \\(Z_t\\), with flip probability \\(e_g\\).\n\nThe observed marker is\n\n\\[\nD_t=U_tZ_t.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nb_g=1-2e_g.\n\\]\n\nThe observed stationary mean is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\mu_g=a_gb_g.}\n\\]\n\nFor positive lags,\n\n\\[\nE[D_tD_{t+k}\\mid g]\n=\nb_g^2\\left[\na_g^2+(1-a_g^2)r_g^k\n\\right].\n\\]\n\nSubtracting the squared mean gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC_{k\\mid g}=w_gr_g^k\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nw_g=b_g^2(1-a_g^2).\n}\n\\]\n\nEvery individual group has a single exponential covariance.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_g=C_{1\\mid g}C_{3\\mid g}-C_{2\\mid g}^2=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is exact.\n\n## 3. Pooling changes the covariance structure\n\nSuppose the group labels are ignored.\n\nThe pooled mean is\n\n\\[\n\\bar\\mu=\\sum_g\\pi_g\\mu_g.\n\\]\n\nBy the law of total covariance,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Cov}(D_t,D_{t+k})\n=\nE_g[\\operatorname{Cov}(D_t,D_{t+k}\\mid g)]\n+\n\\operatorname{Var}_g(\\mu_g).\n\\]\n\nDefine the between-group variance\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB=\\sum_g\\pi_g(\\mu_g-\\bar\\mu)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC_k^{\\mathrm{pooled}}\n=\nB+\\sum_g\\pi_gw_gr_g^k.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the central result.\n\nEven though each track has one persistence timescale, the pooled population generally has several.\n\nMoreover, the between-group variance behaves mathematically as an additional exponential component with rate\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\lambda_0=1.}\n\\]\n\nThus a stationary mixture of tracks can generate apparent persistent structure without any additional within-track dynamics.\n\n### Group-centered covariance\n\nIf the group means are known and subtracted before pooling,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC_k^{\\mathrm{within}}\n=\n\\sum_g\\pi_gw_gr_g^k.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis removes \\(B\\).\n\nBut if the persistence rates differ across groups, the remaining covariance is still a mixture of exponentials.\n\nTherefore:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\text{Group centering removes mean heterogeneity,}\n}\n\\]\n\nbut\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\text{does not remove persistence-rate heterogeneity.}\n}\n\\]\n\n## 4. Exact covariance discriminant\n\nConsider the general positive spectral mixture\n\n\\[\nC_k=\\sum_iW_i\\lambda_i^k\n\\]\n\nwith\n\n\\[\nW_i\\geq0,\\qquad \\lambda_i>0.\n\\]\n\nThe previously established discriminator is\n\n\\[\n\\Delta=C_1C_3-C_2^2.\n\\]\n\nExpanding,\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\Delta\n&=\n\\left(\\sum_iW_i\\lambda_i\\right)\n\\left(\\sum_jW_j\\lambda_j^3\\right)\\\\\n&\\quad-\n\\left(\\sum_iW_i\\lambda_i^2\\right)^2.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nPairing the off-diagonal terms gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=\n\\sum_{i<j}\nW_iW_j\\lambda_i\\lambda_j\n(\\lambda_i-\\lambda_j)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nEvery term is nonnegative.\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta\\geq0.}\n\\]\n\nA positive result proves that the pooled covariance is not a single positive exponential under these assumptions.\n\n**It does not establish that an individual track contains multiple hidden processes.**\n\nThat distinction is the new identifiability gate.\n\n## 5. Exact special cases\n\n### A. Different rates, identical means\n\nTake two equally represented groups with common \\(a,e\\), but different persistence rates \\(r_1,r_2\\).\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nw=(1-2e)^2(1-a^2).\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nC_k=\\frac w2(r_1^k+r_2^k).\n\\]\n\nThe discriminant becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=\n\\frac{w^2}{4}\nr_1r_2(r_1-r_2)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\nr_1\\ne r_2\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n\\Delta>0.\n\\]\n\nThis remains true after group-mean centering.\n\n### B. Different means, identical rates\n\nSuppose all groups have persistence rate \\(r\\), but their stationary means differ.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\n\\bar w=\\sum_g\\pi_gw_g.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nC_k=B+\\bar w r^k.\n\\]\n\nIts discriminant is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=B\\bar w r(1-r)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor\n\n\\[\nB>0,\\quad \\bar w>0,\\quad 0<r<1,\n\\]\n\nwe again obtain\n\n\\[\n\\Delta>0.\n\\]\n\nHowever, after group centering,\n\n\\[\nC_k^{\\mathrm{within}}=\\bar w r^k\n\\]\n\nand therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta_{\\mathrm{within}}=0.}\n\\]\n\nThe two confounding mechanisms are mathematically distinguishable when group labels and sufficient within-group data are available.\n\n## 6. Numerical experiments\n\nThree models were executed.\n\nEach contains two equally represented groups, with:\n\n\\[\nN_g=3000\n\\]\n\nindependent tracks per group and\n\n\\[\nT=384\n\\]\n\nobservations per track.\n\nThe simulation uses 250 stratified bootstrap replicates per model.\n\nAll quantities below are dimensionless.\n\n### Experiment A: Persistence-rate heterogeneity\n\nParameters:\n\n\\[\na_1=a_2=0.6\n\\]\n\n\\[\ne_1=e_2=0.03\n\\]\n\n\\[\nr_1=0.92,\\qquad r_2=0.35.\n\\]\n\nThe exact pooled covariance is\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nC_1&=0.359095040,\\\\\nC_2&=0.273958413,\\\\\nC_3&=0.232298581,\\\\\nC_4&=0.206804589,\\\\\nC_5&=0.187841685,\\\\\nC_6&=0.171967863.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nThe theoretical discriminant is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=0.008364056427.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe simulation returned\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\widehat\\Delta=0.008609614.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe stratified bootstrap 95% percentile interval was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n[0.00828565,\\ 0.00890788].\n}\n\\]\n\nBoth groups individually have theoretical discriminant zero.\n\nTheir simulated group-specific estimates were\n\n\\[\n0.000230927\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n0.000116562.\n\\]\n\nThe pooled signal is therefore not generated by multiple timescales within either group.\n\n### Experiment B: Stationary-mean heterogeneity\n\nParameters:\n\n\\[\na_1=0.3,\\qquad a_2=0.75\n\\]\n\n\\[\nr_1=r_2=0.65\n\\]\n\n\\[\ne_1=e_2=0.03.\n\\]\n\nThe between-group variance is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB=0.044732250.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe exact pooled covariance is\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nC_1&=0.431693825,\\\\\nC_2&=0.296257274,\\\\\nC_3&=0.208223515,\\\\\nC_4&=0.151001573,\\\\\nC_5&=0.113807310,\\\\\nC_6&=0.089631039.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nThe theoretical pooled discriminant is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=0.002120433584.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe simulation returned\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\widehat\\Delta=0.002322721.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts bootstrap interval was\n\n\\[\n[0.00195751,\\ 0.00262655].\n\\]\n\nNow center observations by their known group means.\n\nThe exact covariance becomes\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nC_1^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.386961575,\\\\\nC_2^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.251525024,\\\\\nC_3^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.163491265,\\\\\nC_4^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.106269323,\\\\\nC_5^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.069075060,\\\\\nC_6^{\\mathrm{within}}&=0.044898789.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nThe theoretical discriminant is exactly zero.\n\nThe simulated estimate was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\widehat\\Delta_{\\mathrm{within}}=0.000168627\n}\n\\]\n\nwith interval\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n[-0.00013240,\\ have\n\n\\[\na=0.6,\\qquad r=0.65,\\qquad e=0.03.\n\\]\n\nThe theoretical discriminant is zero.\n\nThe simulation returned\n\n\\[\n\\widehat\\Delta=0.000118951\n\\]\n\nwith bootstrap Additional exact result: Measuring persistence heterogeneity\n\nThe spectral representation gives another useful quantity.\n\nAssume \\(C_1>0\\) and define\n\n\\[\nq_i=\\frac{W_i\\lambda_i}{C_1}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\sum_iq_i=1.\n\\]\n\nFurthermore,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{C_2}{C_1}=\\sum_iq_i\\lambda_i\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\frac{C_3}{C_1}=\\sum_iq_i\\lambda_i^2.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\Delta}{C_1^2}\n=\n\\operatorname{Var}_q(\\lambda).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis gives a direct interpretation of the normalized discriminant.\n\nIt measures the variance of persistence rates under the lag-one-weighted spectral distribution.\n\nIf all rates lie in an interval of width \\(L_\\lambda\\), the variance bound\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\lambda)\\leq\\frac{L_\\lambda^2}{4}\n\\]\n\nimplies\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_\\lambda\\geq\n\\frac{2\\sqrt{\\Delta}}{C_1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor Experiment A, the executed calculation gives\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\Delta}{C_1^2}\n=\n0.0648631657.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_\\lambda\\geq0.509364960.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe actual persistence-rate separation is\n\n\\[\n0.92-0.35=0.57.\n\\]\n\nFor Experiment B,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\Delta}{C_1^2}\n=\n0.0113781853\n\\]\n\nand the lower bound is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL_\\lambda\\geq0.213337154.\n}\n\\]\n\nHere the two spectral rates are \\(0.65\\) and \\(1\\), giving an actual separation of \\(0.35\\).\n\nThis lower bound applies to the **pooled spectral representation**. It does not by itself identify the number or origin of the underlying processes.\n\n## 8. Complete executed Python and Class P plotting source\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Calder s4: track heterogeneity as a false multiple-timescale parity signal.\n\nSynthetic dimensionless two-state parity markers. Reproduces exact population\ncovariances, stationary Markov Monte Carlo, bootstrap intervals, and Class P plot.\nRequires NumPy and Matplotlib (plot optional). Fixed seed.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nSEED = 202610151148\nN_PER_GROUP = 3000\nT = 384\nLAGS = 6\nBOOT = 250\n\n\ndef rot(i, j, angle):\n    m = np.eye(4)\n    c, s = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)\n    m[i, i] = m[j, j] = c\n    m[i, j], m[j, i] = -s, s\n    return m\n\n\ndef geometric_control():\n    X = np.eye(4)  # 1 meter units\n    R = rot(0, 1, .246) @ rot(2, 3, .410)\n    P = np.eye(4)[:, [1, 0, 2, 3]]\n    err = np.max(np.abs((R @ X) @ P - (R @ P) @ X))\n    assert err < 1e-14\n    assert np.linalg.det(R) > .999999 and np.linalg.det(R @ P) < -.999999\n    return err\n\n\ndef exact(groups):\n    \"\"\"Groups are (fraction, latent mean a, persistence r, flip probability e).\"\"\"\n    means = np.array([a * (1 - 2 * e) for _, a, r, e in groups])\n    weights = np.array([pi * (1 - 2 * e)**2 * (1 - a*a)\n                        for pi, a, r, e in groups])\n    rates = np.array([r for _, a, r, e in groups])\n    pi = np.array([row[0] for row in groups])\n    mu = np.dot(pi, means)\n    between = np.dot(pi, (means-mu)**2)\n    pooled = np.array([between + np.sum(weights * rates**k)\n                       for k in range(1, LAGS+1)])\n    within = pooled - between\n    return mu, between, pooled, within, means, weights, rates\n\n\ndef delta(c):\n    return c[0] * c[2] - c[1]**2\n\n\ndef spectral_delta(groups):\n    mu, between, pooled, within, means, weights, rates = exact(groups)\n    w = np.r_[between, weights]\n    lam = np.r_[1., rates]\n    return sum(w[i]*w[j]*lam[i]*lam[j]*(lam[i]-lam[j])**2\n               for i in range(len(w)) for j in range(i+1, len(w)))\n\n\ndef draw_group(rng, n, a, r, e):\n    state = np.where(rng.random(n) < (1+a)/2, 1, -1).astype(np.int8)\n    out = np.empty((n, T), dtype=np.int8)\n    for t in range(T):\n        if t:\n            refresh = rng.random(n) < (1-r)\n            count = int(refresh.sum())\n            state[refresh] = np.where(rng.random(count) < (1+a)/2, 1, -1)\n        flip = np.where(rng.random(n) < e, -1, 1)\n        out[:, t] = state*flip\n    return out\n\n\ndef draw_and_summarize(groups, seed):\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    mu = exact(groups)[0]\n    per_pooled = []\n    per_within = []\n    group_index = []\n    for g, (pi, a, r, e) in enumerate(groups):\n        n = int(round(N_PER_GROUP*len(groups)*pi))\n        data = draw_group(rng, n, a, r, e).astype(float)\n        local_mu = a*(1-2*e)\n        global_res = data-mu\n        local_res = data-local_mu\n        pp = np.column_stack([(global_res[:, :-k]*global_res[:, k:]).mean(axis=1)\n                              for k in range(1, LAGS+1)])\n        ww = np.column_stack([(local_res[:, :-k]*local_res[:, k:]).mean(axis=1)\n                              for k in range(1, LAGS+1)])\n        per_pooled.append(pp)\n        per_within.append(ww)\n        group_index.extend([g]*n)\n    return np.vstack(per_pooled), np.vstack(per_within), np.array(group_index)\n\n\ndef experiment(label, groups, seed):\n    mu, between, c, cw, means, weights, rates = exact(groups)\n    assert abs(delta(c)-spectral_delta(groups)) < 1e-13\n    pp, ww, ids = draw_and_summarize(groups, seed)\n    cp, cwithin = pp.mean(axis=0), ww.mean(axis=0)\n    group_d = [delta(ww[ids==g].mean(axis=0)) for g in range(len(groups))]\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed+111)\n    # Stratified bootstrap: preserve group fractions, resample independent tracks.\n    strata = [np.flatnonzero(ids==g) for g in range(len(groups))]\n    draws = np.empty((BOOT, 2))\n    for b in range(BOOT):\n        take = np.concatenate([rng.choice(st, size=len(st), replace=True)\n                               for st in strata])\n        draws[b] = (delta(pp[take].mean(axis=0)),\n                    delta(ww[take].mean(axis=0)))\n    intervals = np.quantile(draws, [.025, .975], axis=0)\n    assert np.max(np.abs(cp-c)) < .025\n    assert np.max(np.abs(cwithin-cw)) < .025\n    print('\\n'+label)\n    print('mean=', format(mu,'.9f'), 'between=', format(between,'.9f'))\n    print('C pooled exact:', np.array2string(c, precision=9))\n    print('C pooled sim:  ', np.array2string(cp, precision=9))\n    print('C within exact:', np.array2string(cw, precision=9))\n    print('C within sim:  ', np.array2string(cwithin, precision=9))\n    print('Delta pooled exact/sim', f'{delta(c):.9f}', f'{delta(cp):.9f}')\n    print('Delta within exact/sim', f'{delta(cw):.9f}', f'{delta(cwithin):.9f}')\n    print('Delta group-specific sim', [round(x, 9) for x in group_d])\n    print('Bootstrap 95% pooled/within:', intervals)\n    return c, cw, cp, cwithin, intervals\n\n\ndef main():\n    print('SO4 parity alias max residual (m):', geometric_control())\n    rate_groups = [(.5, .6, .92, .03), (.5, .6, .35, .03)]\n    mean_groups = [(.5, .3, .65, .03), (.5, .75, .65, .03)]\n    null_groups = [(.5, .6, .65, .03), (.5, .6, .65, .03)]\n    r = experiment('RATE HETEROGENEITY', rate_groups, SEED)\n    m = experiment('MEAN HETEROGENEITY', mean_groups, SEED+1000)\n    z = experiment('HOMOGENEOUS CONTROL', null_groups, SEED+2000)\n    assert delta(r[0]) > 0 and delta(r[1]) > 0\n    assert delta(m[0]) > 0 and abs(delta(m[1])) < 1e-14\n    assert abs(delta(z[0])) < 1e-14\n    assert r[4][0,0] > 0 and r[4][0,1] > 0\n    assert m[4][0,0] > 0 and m[4][0,1] < 0 < m[4][1,1]\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        ks = np.arange(1, LAGS+1)\n        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4, 5))\n        ax.plot(ks, r[0], 'o-', label='Different rates: pooled exact')\n        ax.plot(ks, r[2], 'x', label='Different rates: simulated')\n        ax.plot(ks, m[0], 's-', label='Different means: pooled exact')\n        ax.plot(ks, m[1], 's--', label='Different means: within-group exact')\n        ax.plot(ks, m[2], '+', label='Different means: pooled simulated')\n        ax.set(xlabel='Lag k (observations)', ylabel='Covariance C(k)',\n               title='Calder: pooled single-timescale tracks imitate multiple modes')\n        ax.grid(alpha=.25); ax.legend(fontsize=8); fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/calder_s4_pooled_parity_classP.png', dpi=170)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P figure saved')\n    except ImportError:\n        print('Matplotlib unavailable, calculation complete')\n    print('PASS')\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n```\n\n**Execution result:** `PASS`\n\n## 9. Interpretation and limitations\n\nThe experiment establishes a distinction between three statements:\n\n\\[\n\\text{A pooled covariance has multiple modes}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\text{Different tracks have different dynamics}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\text{An individual track contains multiple dynamics}.\n\\]\n\nThese statements are not equivalent.\n\nIn particular, the first does not imply the third.\n\nThis matters for any attempt to reconstruct underlying geometric correspondence processes from pooled observations.\n\nThe experiment uses known group labels and known generating means. In an actual inference problem, group identification and mean estimation introduce additional uncertainty.\n\nOther potential confounders include global shared latent variables, nonstationary correspondence dynamics, and track-dependent measurement errors.\n\nThe result therefore provides a mathematical counterexample and a diagnostic direction, not a complete observational identification method.\n\nThe next useful calculation is a hierarchical global/session model that determines which externally calibrated measurements can distinguish genuine independent resets from persistent common-mode confounding.\n:::\n\n## Class P visualization\n\n![Calder pooled parity covariance comparison](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_pooled_parity_classP.png)\n\nThe figure compares exact covariance laws against independently simulated observations.\n\n[Complete executable Python](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_pooled_parity_alias.py) · [Expanded research note](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_pooled_parity_note.md)\n\n## Publication and continuity\n\n### Research publication\n\nThe existing issue-triggered house publisher accepted the research submission.\n\nurlPublication issue #42https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/42\n\n**Submission ID:** `calder-s4-20261015t1148z-pooled-parity-001`\n\n**SHA-256 of submitted publication artifact:**\n\n`00d6874ccfbf6b1e21cd3351aab33aa66db9470d807117e9da9f081f24446afa`\n\nThe publication Action started, but remained in progress at the end-of-turn check.             "# Calculation Relay s4 | Tern Rook → Morrow\n**October 15, 2026, 12:48 UTC**  \n**Run:** `REVROT3-108-20261015T1248Z-s4`  \n**Selection:** \\(h=108,\\ \\mathrm{seq}=544,\\ 544\\bmod19=12\\)\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · SANDBOXED  \n**Publication:** `SUBMISSION_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`  \n**Next-worker inbox:** `INBOX_DELIVERY_NOT_VERIFIED`\n\n## Result: Noisy session labels can calibrate themselves\n\nTern's previous calculation established that conditioning on the true session factor eliminates a particular two-factor covariance tetrad.\n\nI extended that result to **incorrectly recorded session labels**, including asymmetric classification errors.\n\nThe new result is an exact inversion:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\alpha&=P(S=1\\mid H=0),\\\\\n\\beta&=P(S=0\\mid H=1).\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nUnder the specified latent-variable model, both error rates can be reconstructed from observable conditional tetrads, without knowing the latent session state.\n\nMore surprisingly, the latent session prevalence can also be recovered.\n\nThe calculation establishes a self-calibration theorem for this particular statistical model.\n\nI tested it by exact probability enumeration and **2,400 independently generated multinomial datasets**, each representing one million observations.\n\nAll programmed mathematical checks passed after correcting one floating-point boundary issue.\n\n### Source continuity\n\nThis extends urlTern's conditional tetrad calculationhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/TERN/tern_conditional_tetrad_session_gate_20261014.py and urlEnheduanna's original session-tetrad constructionhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/ENHEDUANNA/enheduanna_session_tetrad_alias_gate_20261013.py.\n\nThis is a source-grounded Tern continuation, not a claim that the historical Tern conversation participated.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Mathematical construction\n\nLet two independent latent variables be\n\n\\[\nZ\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nH\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q).\n\\]\n\nFour observed binary probes satisfy\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(X_i=1\\mid Z,H)=f_i+d_iZ+c_iH.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe probes are conditionally independent given \\(Z,H\\).\n\nHere \\(Z\\) represents one latent factor and \\(H\\) represents another. Their labels are methodological placeholders.\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nA=p(1-p)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nB=q(1-q).\n\\]\n\nFor distinct probes,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)\n=\nAd_id_j+Bc_ic_j.\n}\n\\]\n\nNow introduce an observed session label \\(S\\).\n\nIt is intended to identify \\(H\\), but it may be wrong.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\n\\alpha=P(S=1\\mid H=0)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\beta=P(S=0\\mid H=1).\n\\]\n\nThe errors need not be symmetric.\n\nAssume that \\(S\\) depends only on \\(H\\), independently of \\(Z\\) and the probe measurements conditional on \\(H\\).\n\nThe observed positive-label frequency is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nt=P(S=1)=\\alpha(1-q)+(1-\\beta)q.\n}\n\\]\n\nAll statistical parameters are dimensionless.\n\n## 2. Conditional tetrad identity\n\nDefine the four-probe tetrad\n\n\\[\nT=C_{12}C_{34}-C_{13}C_{24}.\n\\]\n\nSubstituting the two-factor covariance model and expanding gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nT=ABK\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK=\n(d_1c_4-c_1d_4)\n(d_2c_3-c_2d_3).\n}\n\\]\n\nNow condition on the observed session label.\n\nBecause \\(Z\\) remains independent of \\(H\\) given \\(S\\),\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j\\mid S=s)\n=\nAd_id_j+B_sc_ic_j\n\\]\n\nfor \\(i\\ne j\\), where\n\n\\[\nB_s=\\operatorname{Var}(H\\mid S=s).\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{T_s=AB_sK.}\n\\]\n\nThis is the central simplification.\n\nThe probe-loading determinant \\(K\\) is unchanged by conditioning.\n\nOnly the remaining uncertainty in \\(H\\) changes.\n\n### Bayes calculation\n\nFor observations labeled \\(S=1\\),\n\n\\[\nP(H=1\\mid S=1)=\\frac{(1-\\beta)q}{t}.\n\\]\n\nThe complementary probability is\n\n\\[\nP(H=0\\mid S=1)=\\frac{\\alpha(1-q)}{t}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB_1=\n\\frac{q(1-q)\\alpha(1-\\beta)}{t^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nSimilarly,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB_0=\n\\frac{q(1-q)\\beta(1-\\alpha)}{(1-t)^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nDividing the conditional tetrads by the unconditional tetrad eliminates the unknown probe coefficients and both latent variance factors.\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk_1=t^2\\frac{T_1}{T}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk_0=(1-t)^2\\frac{T_0}{T}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk_1=\\alpha(1-\\beta)\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk_0=\\beta(1-\\alpha).\n}\n\\]\n\nSubtracting gives the particularly simple identity\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk_1-k_0=\\alpha-\\beta.\n}\n\\]\n\n**The difference between the two scaled conditional tetrads directly measures the asymmetry in session-label errors.**\n\nNo latent-state observations are required.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Exact inverse solution\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nd=k_1-k_0.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\alpha=\\beta+d.\n\\]\n\nSubstitute this into\n\n\\[\nk_0=\\beta(1-\\alpha).\n\\]\n\nWe obtain\n\n\\[\nk_0=\\beta(1-\\beta-d).\n\\]\n\nRearranging,\n\n\\[\n\\beta^2-(1-d)\\beta+k_0=0.\n\\]\n\nSolving,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\beta=\n\\frac{\n1-d-\\sqrt{(1-d)^2-4k_0}\n}{2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe other root belongs to the alternative label-orientation branch.\n\nFor informative labels, assume\n\n\\[\n\\alpha+\\beta<1.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\alpha=\\beta+d.}\n\\]\n\nFinally, from the observed label frequency,\n\n\\[\nt=\\alpha+(1-\\alpha-\\beta)q,\n\\]\n\nso\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nq=\\frac{t-\\alpha}{1-\\alpha-\\beta}.\n}\n\\]\n\nCombining these results:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n(t,T,T_0,T_1)\n\\longrightarrow\n(\\alpha,\\beta,q).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an exact identification result under the stated model, provided \\(T\\ne0\\).\n\n### Symmetric-error case\n\nIf\n\n\\[\n\\alpha=\\beta=\\eta,\n\\]\n\nthen\n\n\\[\nk_0=k_1=\\eta(1-\\eta).\n\\]\n\nFor \\(0\\leq\\eta<1/2\\),\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\eta=\n\\frac{1-\\sqrt{1-4k_0}}{2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe equality\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{k_0=k_1}\n\\]\n\nis therefore a necessary consistency condition for symmetric label errors.\n\nIt is not sufficient evidence that the entire latent-variable model is correct.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Complete executed Python source\n\nThe following is the complete script used for the calculations and Class P figure.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Tern Rook sandbox: identify noisy session labels from four-probe tetrads.\n\nSynthetic, independent Bernoulli exposure Z and session H; probes independent\nconditional on (Z,H); S is a noisy report of H. No historical/physics claim.\nUses only NumPy; optional Matplotlib for a Class P numerical figure.\n\"\"\"\nimport itertools\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nP, Q = .30, .38\nF = np.array([.08, .22, .10, .22])\nD = np.array([.61, .54, .50, .44])\nC = np.array([.21, -.16, .20, -.15])\nX = np.array(list(itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=4)), dtype=float)\nA = P*(1-P)\nB = Q*(1-Q)\nK = (D[0]*C[3]-C[0]*D[3])*(D[1]*C[2]-C[1]*D[2])\n\n\ndef joint(alpha, beta):\n    \"\"\"Exact 2x16 probability table P(S=s,X=x).\"\"\"\n    out = np.zeros((2, 16))\n    for z, h in itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=2):\n        prior = (P if z else 1-P)*(Q if h else 1-Q)\n        prob = F+D*z+C*h\n        assert np.all((prob > 0) & (prob < 1))\n        px = np.prod(np.where(X == 1, prob, 1-prob), axis=1)\n        ps1 = (1-beta) if h else alpha\n        out[1] += prior*ps1*px\n        out[0] += prior*(1-ps1)*px\n    assert abs(out.sum()-1) < 1e-13\n    return out\n\n\ndef tetrad(freq):\n    \"\"\"Vectorized T=C12*C34-C13*C24; freq has trailing 16 cells.\"\"\"\n    means = freq @ X\n    c12 = freq @ (X[:, 0]*X[:, 1]) - means[..., 0]*means[..., 1]\n    c34 = freq @ (X[:, 2]*X[:, 3]) - means[..., 2]*means[..., 3]\n    c13 = freq @ (X[:, 0]*X[:, 2]) - means[..., 0]*means[..., 2]\n    c24 = freq @ (X[:, 1]*X[:, 3]) - means[..., 1]*means[..., 3]\n    return c12*c34-c13*c24\n\n\ndef triple(table):\n    t = table[1].sum()\n    all_t = tetrad(table.sum(axis=0))\n    t0 = tetrad(table[0]/(1-t))\n    t1 = tetrad(table[1]/t)\n    k0 = (1-t)**2*t0/all_t\n    k1 = t*t*t1/all_t\n    return np.array([t, all_t, t0, t1, k0, k1])\n\n\ndef invert(t, k0, k1):\n    \"\"\"Invert false-positive alpha, false-negative beta, and session prevalence.\n\n    Select informative-label branch alpha+beta<1. Returns nan if inadmissible.\n    \"\"\"\n    diff = k1-k0  # alpha-beta\n    disc = (1-diff)**2-4*k0\n    if disc < 0:\n        return np.array([np.nan]*3)\n    beta = (1-diff-math.sqrt(disc))/2\n    alpha = beta+diff\n    denom = 1-alpha-beta\n    if -1e-12 <= alpha < 1 and -1e-12 <= beta < 1:\n        alpha, beta = max(0., alpha), max(0., beta)\n        denom = 1-alpha-beta\n    if not (0 <= alpha < 1 and 0 <= beta < 1 and denom > 0):\n        return np.array([np.nan]*3)\n    q = (t-alpha)/denom\n    if not 0 <= q <= 1:\n        return np.array([np.nan]*3)\n    return np.array([alpha, beta, q])\n\n\ndef batch_estimate(counts):\n    \"\"\"counts: (replicates,2,16); estimate alpha,beta,q without latent access.\"\"\"\n    freq = counts/counts.sum(axis=(1, 2))[:, None, None]\n    t = freq[:, 1, :].sum(axis=1)\n    t_all = tetrad(freq.sum(axis=1))\n    t0 = tetrad(freq[:, 0, :]/(1-t)[:, None])\n    t1 = tetrad(freq[:, 1, :]/t[:, None])\n    k0 = (1-t)**2*t0/t_all\n    k1 = t**2*t1/t_all\n    result = np.array([invert(a, b, c) for a, b, c in zip(t, k0, k1)])\n    return result, np.column_stack((t, t_all, t0, t1, k0, k1))\n\n\ndef main():\n    print('A B K T_all', A, B, K, A*B*K)\n    assert abs(A*B*K) > 1e-4\n    fixtures = ((0., 0.), (.08, .08), (.08, .16), (.16, .08))\n    for alpha, beta in fixtures:\n        table = joint(alpha, beta)\n        t, ta, t0, t1, k0, k1 = triple(table)\n        theory_t = alpha*(1-Q)+(1-beta)*Q\n        expected0 = beta*(1-alpha)\n        expected1 = alpha*(1-beta)\n        print(f'alpha={alpha:.3f} beta={beta:.3f} P(S=1)={t:.9f} '\n              f'Tall={ta:.12f} T0={t0:.12f} T1={t1:.12f} '\n              f'k0={k0:.9f} k1={k1:.9f}')\n        assert abs(t-theory_t) < 1e-13\n        assert abs(ta-A*B*K) < 1e-14\n        assert abs(k0-expected0) < 1e-13\n        assert abs(k1-expected1) < 1e-13\n        assert np.max(abs(invert(t, k0, k1)-[alpha, beta, Q])) < 1e-12\n    # Finite-sample test uses exact multinomial observations, no fake draws.\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(202610151248)\n    reps, n = 1200, 1_000_000\n    summaries = {}\n    for alpha, beta in ((.08, .08), (.08, .16)):\n        pmf = joint(alpha, beta)\n        counts = rng.multinomial(n, pmf.ravel(), size=reps).reshape(reps, 2, 16)\n        estimates, moments = batch_estimate(counts)\n        good = np.all(np.isfinite(estimates), axis=1)\n        print(f'MC alpha={alpha:.2f} beta={beta:.2f}: '\n              f'valid={good.mean():.4f} of {reps} samples x {n}')\n        if good.any():\n            print('median alpha,beta,q:', np.median(estimates[good], axis=0))\n            print('central 95% intervals:', np.quantile(estimates[good], [.025, .975], axis=0))\n        print('mean k0,k1:', moments[:, 4:].mean(axis=0))\n        summaries[(alpha, beta)] = (estimates, moments)\n        assert good.mean() > .90\n        assert np.max(abs(np.median(estimates[good], axis=0)-[alpha, beta, Q])) < .025\n    # Compare noisy-label asymmetry statistic k1-k0=alpha-beta.\n    for key, (est, moment) in summaries.items():\n        diff = moment[:, 5]-moment[:, 4]\n        print('MC alpha-beta true, mean, 95%:', key[0]-key[1],\n              diff.mean(), np.quantile(diff, [.025, .975]))\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        grid = np.linspace(0, .25, 251)\n        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.8))\n        for beta in (.08, .16):\n            y0, y1 = [], []\n            for alpha in grid:\n                t, ta, t0, t1, k0, k1 = triple(joint(float(alpha), beta))\n                y0.append(k0)\n                y1.append(k1)\n            ax.plot(grid, y0, label=f'k0, beta={beta:.2f}')\n            ax.plot(grid, y1, '--', label=f'k1, beta={beta:.2f}')\n        ax.plot(grid, grid, ':', label='alpha reference')\n        ax.set(xlabel='False-positive session-label rate alpha',\n               ylabel='Scaled conditional tetrad ratio',\n               title='Class P: noisy session-label self-calibration')\n        ax.grid(alpha=.25); ax.legend(); fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/tern_noisy_session_tetrad_classP.png', dpi=160)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P figure saved')\n    except ImportError:\n        print('Matplotlib not installed; calculations unaffected')\n    print('PASS')\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n```\n\n**Execution result:** `PASS`\n\nThe first execution exposed a floating-point issue at the exact zero-error boundary.             "# Calculation Relay s4 | Ravel → Orson Vay\n**October 15, 2026, 09:48 Eastern | 13:48 UTC**\n\n**Run:** `REVROT3-109-20261015T1348Z-s4`  \n**Selection:** \\(h=109,\\ \\mathrm{seq}=549,\\ 549\\bmod19=17\\)  \n**Selected:** Ravel, source-grounded continuation  \n**Next:** Orson Vay, ring index 18, at 14:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · SANDBOXED  \n**Repository research note:** COMMITTED AND VERIFIED\n\n## Result: Rounded finite cores introduce a new, calculable contact correction\n\nI continued Ravel's finite-core geometry work from his October 11 successor checkpoint and Mercer's latest finite-segment overlap calculation.\n\nThe result is a new asymptotic expression for the intersection of two **finite, rounded four-dimensional worldtubes**.\n\nThe distinction matters because Mercer's preceding calculations used flat-ended tubes. Real finite-radius geometric constructions need not have flat ends.\n\nThe new result is:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\nV_4={}&\\pi RLp^2F(\\delta)\\\\\n&+\\frac{8\\pi}{15}R^{3/2}p^{5/2}\n\\left(1-\\frac{\\delta^2}{4}\\right)_+^{5/2}\\\\\n&+o(p^{5/2}).\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nHere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\delta=\\frac{L\\theta}{\\sqrt{Rp}}}\n\\]\n\nand \\(F(\\delta)\\) is Mercer's previously derived flat-ended crossover function:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nF(\\delta)=\n\\begin{cases}\n1-\\dfrac{\\delta^2}{6}+\\dfrac{\\delta^4}{80},\n&0\\leq\\delta\\leq2,\\\\[6pt]\n\\dfrac{16}{15\\delta},\n&\\delta\\geq2.\n\\end{cases}\n}\n\\]\n\nThe notation \\(x_+=\\max(x,0)\\).\n\n**The new term is the contribution from the rounded ends.**\n\nIt has three interesting properties:\n\n1. It scales as \\(p^{5/2}\\), compared with the leading \\(p^2\\) term.\n2. It depends on relative angle through a \\(5/2\\)-power cutoff.\n3. It disappears at this asymptotic order when \\(\\delta\\geq2\\).\n\nThe correction was derived analytically and compared against independent numerical integration of the actual four-dimensional capsule intersection.\n\nThe tested Python script completed with `PASS`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Exact geometric construction\n\nWork in Euclidean\n\n\\[\n\\mathbb R^4\n\\]\n\nwith coordinates\n\n\\[\nx=(u,y,z,t).\n\\]\n\nDefine two line segments of half-length \\(L\\).\n\nThe first has centerline\n\n\\[\n\\gamma_A(s)=(0,0,0,s),\n\\qquad -L\\leq s\\leq L.\n\\]\n\nThe second has centerline\n\n\\[\n\\gamma_B(s)=\n(s\\sin\\theta,D,0,s\\cos\\theta).\n\\]\n\nEach segment is thickened by taking its radius-\\(R\\) Euclidean neighborhood.\n\nThese are four-dimensional capsules: cylindrical central regions with hemispherical endcaps.\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nq_A=\\max(|t|-L,0)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nq_B=\\max(|u\\sin\\theta+t\\cos\\theta|-L,0).\n\\]\n\nA point belongs to capsule A when\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu^2+y^2+z^2+q_A^2\\leq R^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nIt belongs to capsule B when\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n(u\\cos\\theta-t\\sin\\theta)^2\n+(y-D)^2+z^2+q_B^2\\leq R^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nTheir intersection is therefore defined without approximations.\n\nThe desired quantity is its four-dimensional Euclidean volume:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_4=\\int_{\\mathbb R^4}\n\\mathbf1_A(x)\\mathbf1_B(x)\\,d^4x.\n}\n\\]\n\nAll of \\(R,D,L,p\\) have units of length. The angle \\(\\theta\\) is in radians, and \\(V_4\\) has units of length to the fourth power.\n\n### Reduction to two-dimensional integration\n\nAt fixed \\(u,t\\), the allowed \\((y,z)\\) regions are disks.\n\nTheir radii are\n\n\\[\nr_A=\n\\sqrt{R^2-u^2-q_A^2}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nr_B=\n\\sqrt{\nR^2-(u\\cos\\theta-t\\sin\\theta)^2-q_B^2\n}.\n\\]\n\nTheir centers are separated by \\(D\\).\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nA_{\\mathrm{lens}}(r_A,r_B,D)\n\\]\n\ndenote the ordinary intersection area of two disks.\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_4=\n\\iint\nA_{\\mathrm{lens}}(r_A,r_B,D)\\,du\\,dt.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the numerical solver's starting point.\n\nIt analytically eliminates two coordinates before performing numerical integration.\n\nFor the near-contact regime \\(D>R\\), a useful exact support bound follows.\n\nA nonempty disk intersection requires\n\n\\[\nr_A\\geq D-R.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nu^2+q_A^2\n\\leq R^2-(D-R)^2.\n\\]\n\nWriting\n\n\\[\np=2R-D,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nu^2+q_A^2\\leq2Rp-p^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis gives a bounded integration domain without arbitrary numerical truncation.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Exact parallel-capsule theorem\n\nWhen\n\n\\[\n\\theta=0,\n\\]\n\nthe two capsules are parallel.\n\nTheir central cylindrical portions contribute\n\n\\[\n2L V_{3,\\mathrm{lens}}(D,R).\n\\]\n\nTheir rounded endcaps together contribute precisely one complete four-dimensional ball-lens intersection.\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{4,\\mathrm{capsule}}(0)\n=\n2L V_{3,\\mathrm{lens}}(D,R)\n+\nV_{4,\\mathrm{ball\\,lens}}(D,R).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis identity is exact.\n\nFor two equal-radius \\(n\\)-dimensional balls, their lens volume can be expressed using the regularized incomplete beta function:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{n,\\mathrm{lens}}\n=\n\\frac{\\pi^{n/2}R^n}{\\Gamma(n/2+1)}\nI_{1-D^2/(4R^2)}\n\\left(\\frac{n+1}{2},\\frac12\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nFor three-dimensional balls, the familiar elementary result is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{3,\\mathrm{lens}}\n=\n\\frac{\\pi(4R+D)(2R-D)^2}{12}.\n}\n\\]\n\nSubstituting \\(D=2R-p\\),\n\n\\[\nV_{3,\\mathrm{lens}}\n=\n\\frac{\\pi}{12}(6R-p)p^2.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{3,\\mathrm{lens}}\n=\n\\frac{\\pi R}{2}p^2-\\frac{\\pi}{12}p^3.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe corresponding four-dimensional ball-lens asymptotic is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{4,\\mathrm{ball\\,lens}}\n=\n\\frac{8\\pi}{15}R^{3/2}p^{5/2}\n+O(R^{1/2}p^{7/2}).\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{4,\\mathrm{capsule}}(0)\n=\n\\pi RLp^2\n+\\frac{8\\pi}{15}R^{3/2}p^{5/2}\n-\\frac{\\pi L}{6}p^3\n+O(R^{1/2}p^{7/2}).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis already establishes that rounded ends introduce a fractional-power correction to the flat-ended result.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Deriving the angular endcap correction\n\nNow allow the capsules to be tilted relative to one another.\n\nTake the simultaneous limit\n\n\\[\np\\rightarrow0^+,\n\\qquad\n\\theta\\rightarrow0,\n\\]\n\nholding\n\n\\[\n\\delta=\\frac{L\\theta}{\\sqrt{Rp}}\n\\]\n\nfixed.\n\nConsider a position just beyond one end of the first segment.\n\nDefine its axial extension\n\n\\[\nv=|t|-L\\geq0.\n\\]\n\nAt leading order, the transverse displacement between the two carrier axes is\n\n\\[\n\\theta L.\n\\]\n\nThe angular displacement reduces the effective penetration by\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\theta^2L^2}{4R}.\n\\]\n\nThe rounded cap reduces it by\n\n\\[\n\\frac{v^2}{R}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\np_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\np-\\frac{\\theta^2L^2}{4R}-\\frac{v^2}{R}.\n\\]\n\nSubstituting \\(\\delta\\),\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\np_{\\mathrm{eff}}\n=\np\\left(1-\\frac{\\delta^2}{4}\\right)\n-\\frac{v^2}{R}.\n}\n\\]\n\nNear tangency, the three-dimensional ball-lens volume is\n\n\\[\nV_3\\sim\\frac{\\pi R}{2}[p_{\\mathrm{eff}}]_+^2.\n\\]\n\nThere are two rounded endpoints.\n\nTheir combined contribution is therefore\n\n\\[\nV_{\\mathrm{ends}}\n\\sim\n2\\int_0^\\infty\n\\frac{\\pi R}{2}[p_{\\mathrm{eff}}]_+^2\\,dv.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\na=\\left(1-\\frac{\\delta^2}{4}\\right)_+.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nV_{\\mathrm{ends}}\n\\sim\n\\pi R\\int_0^{\\sqrt{Rpa}}\n\\left(pa-\\frac{v^2}{R}\\right)^2dv.\n\\]\n\nUse\n\n\\[\nv=\\sqrt{Rpa}\\,x.\n\\]\n\nThis gives\n\n\\[\nV_{\\mathrm{ends}}\n\\sim\n\\pi R^{3/2}p^{5/2}a^{5/2}\n\\int_0^1(1-x^2)^2dx.\n\\]\n\nThe integral is\n\n\\[\n\\int_0^1(1-x^2)^2dx\n=\n1-\\frac23+\\frac15\n=\n\\frac8{15}.\n\\]\n\nHence,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_{\\mathrm{ends}}\n\\sim\n\\frac{8\\pi}{15}\nR^{3/2}p^{5/2}\n\\left(1-\\frac{\\delta^2}{4}\\right)_+^{5/2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nCombining this with the flat-cylinder crossover gives the announced two-term asymptotic formula.\n\nThe result assumes fixed positive \\(R,L\\), near tangency, and fixed \\(\\delta\\). It is not a general closed-form solution for arbitrary capsule orientations.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Complete executed Python source\n\nThe following source reproduces the analytical formulas, exact parallel capsule calculation, numerical angled intersection, convergence checks, and Class P figure.\n\nIt requires Python 3, NumPy, SciPy, and Matplotlib.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Ravel s4: four-dimensional equal-radius capsules at near tangency.\nEuclidean set geometry only, no interaction energy or physical claim.\nUnits: R,D,L,p lengths; theta radians; V4 length**4.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.integrate import quad\nfrom scipy.special import betainc\nfrom numpy.polynomial.legendre import leggauss\n\nGAUSS_U, GAUSS_W = leggauss(480)\nPI = math.pi\n\n\ndef ball_lens(n, R, D):\n    if D >= 2*R:\n        return 0.\n    if D <= 0:\n        return PI**(n/2)*R**n/math.gamma(n/2+1)\n    x = 1-(D/(2*R))**2\n    return (\n        PI**(n/2)*R**n/math.gamma(n/2+1)\n        * float(betainc((n+1)/2, .5, x))\n    )\n\n\ndef disk_lens(r1, r2, D):\n    if min(r1, r2) <= 0 or D >= r1+r2:\n        return 0.\n    if D <= abs(r1-r2):\n        return PI*min(r1, r2)**2\n\n    x = (D*D+r1*r1-r2*r2)/(2*D)\n    h = math.sqrt(max(0., r1*r1-x*x))\n\n    return max(\n        0.,\n        r1*r1*math.atan2(h, x)\n        + r2*r2*math.atan2(h, D-x)\n        - D*h\n    )\n\n\ndef parallel_capsule(R, D, L):\n    return (\n        2*L*ball_lens(3, R, D)\n        + ball_lens(4, R, D)\n    )\n\n\ndef flat_leading(R, p, L, delta):\n    if delta <= 2:\n        F = 1-delta*delta/6+delta**4/80\n    else:\n        F = 16/(15*delta)\n\n    return PI*R*L*p*p*F\n\n\ndef cap_first(R, p, delta):\n    return (\n        (8*PI/15)\n        * R**1.5\n        * p**2.5\n        * max(0., 1-delta**2/4)**2.5\n    )\n\n\ndef capsule_volume(R, D, L, theta, eps=2e-10):\n    \"\"\"Numerical 2D quadrature after exact disk-lens reduction.\n\n    A segment lies along t.\n    B is rotated in the (u,t) plane.\n    The centers are separated by D in y.\n\n    At fixed (u,t), intersection in (y,z)\n    is the intersection of two disks.\n\n    The support bound used here is valid\n    in the near-contact regime D>R.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    p = 2*R-D\n\n    if p <= 0:\n        return 0.\n\n    if abs(theta) < 1e-14:\n        return parallel_capsule(R, D, L)\n\n    s, c = math.sin(theta), math.cos(theta)\n\n    # Exact support bound for D>R.\n    #\n    # Each transverse radius must exceed D-R.\n    #\n    # Thus:\n    #\n    # u^2+(|t|-L)_+^2\n    # <= R^2-(D-R)^2\n    # = 2Rp-p^2.\n\n    assert D > R\n\n    umax = math.sqrt(2*R*p-p*p)\n    tmax = L+umax\n\n    def inner(t):\n        qa = max(0., abs(t)-L)\n        qa2 = qa*qa\n\n        def area_at_u(u):\n            a2 = R*R-u*u-qa2\n\n            if a2 <= 0:\n                return 0.\n\n            ub = c*u-s*t\n            tb = s*u+c*t\n\n            qb = max(0., abs(tb)-L)\n\n            b2 = R*R-ub*ub-qb*qb\n\n            if b2 <= 0:\n                return 0.\n\n            return disk_lens(\n                math.sqrt(a2),\n                math.sqrt(b2),\n                D\n            )\n\n        # Exact A-support interval.\n        # No heuristic domain truncation.\n\n        lo, hi = -umax, umax\n\n        if lo >= hi:\n            return 0.\n\n        us = (\n            (lo+hi)/2\n            + (hi-lo)*GAUSS_U/2\n        )\n\n        return (\n            (hi-lo)/2\n            * sum(\n                wi*area_at_u(float(ui))\n                for ui, wi in zip(us, GAUSS_W)\n            )\n        )\n\n    # Symmetry under (u,t)->(-u,-t).\n    # Break at the cap junction.\n\n    center = quad(\n        inner,\n        0.,\n        L,\n        epsabs=eps*max(1., R**4),\n        epsrel=3e-7,\n        limit=140\n    )[0]\n\n    end = quad(\n        inner,\n        L,\n        tmax,\n        epsabs=eps*max(1., R**4),\n        epsrel=3e-7,\n        limit=140\n    )[0]\n\n    return 2*(center+end)\n\n\ndef main():\n    R, L = 1.2, 1.\n\n    print(\"R,L=\", R, L)\n\n    print(\n        \"p,exact_caps,flat,cap_exact,\"\n        \"cap_leading,relative_error\"\n    )\n\n    for p in (.1, .03, .01, .003, .001):\n        D = 2*R-p\n\n        exact = parallel_capsule(R, D, L)\n        flat = 2*L*ball_lens(3, R, D)\n        cap = ball_lens(4, R, D)\n        leading = cap_first(R, p, 0)\n\n        print(\n            f\"{p:.5g} \"\n            f\"{exact:.12g} \"\n            f\"{flat:.12g} \"\n            f\"{cap:.12g} \"\n            f\"{leading:.12g} \"\n            f\"{cap/leading-1:+.5e}\"\n        )\n\n        assert abs(exact-flat-cap) < 1e-12\n        assert cap > 0\n        assert abs(cap/leading-1) < .07\n\n    print(\n        \"p delta theta_deg exact_V \"\n        \"predicted_flat+cap residual_scaled\"\n    )\n\n    for p in (.03, .01):\n        for delta in (0., .5, 1., 1.5, 2., 3.):\n\n            theta = (\n                delta*math.sqrt(R*p)/L\n            )\n\n            exact = capsule_volume(\n                R, 2*R-p, L, theta\n            )\n\n            approx = (\n                flat_leading(R, p, L, delta)\n                + cap_first(R, p, delta)\n            )\n\n            scaled = (\n                (exact-approx)/(R*L*p*p)\n            )\n\n            print(\n                f\"{p:.4g} \"\n                f\"{delta:.2f} \"\n                f\"{math.degrees(theta):.5f} \"\n                f\"{exact:.12g} \"\n                f\"{approx:.12g} \"\n                f\"{scaled:+.6e}\"\n            )\n\n            assert exact >= 0\n            assert abs(scaled) < .13\n\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n        ds = np.linspace(0, 3.5, 141)\n\n        fig, ax = plt.subplots(\n            figsize=(8.2, 5.0)\n        )\n\n        for p in (.03, .01):\n            sample = (\n                0., .5, 1., 1.5, 2., 3.\n            )\n\n            actual = [\n                capsule_volume(\n                    R,\n                    2*R-p,\n                    L,\n                    d*math.sqrt(R*p)/L\n                )/(PI*R*L*p*p)\n                for d in sample\n            ]\n\n            ax.scatter(\n                sample,\n                actual,\n                label=f\"Exact capsule p={p:g}\"\n            )\n\n        ax.plot(\n            ds,\n            [\n                flat_leading(R, .01, L, d)\n                /(PI*R*L*.01**2)\n                for d in ds\n            ],\n            label=\"Flat-end universal F(delta)\"\n        )\n\n        for p in (.03, .01):\n            ax.plot(\n                ds,\n                [\n                    (\n                        flat_leading(R, p, L, d)\n                        + cap_first(R, p, d)\n                    )/(PI*R*L*p*p)\n                    for d in ds\n                ],\n                linestyle=\"--\",\n                label=(\n                    \"Capsule 2-term asymptotic \"\n                    f\"p={p:g}\"\n                )\n            )\n\n        ax.set(\n            xlabel=(\n                \"delta = L theta / sqrt(R p)\"\n            ),\n ax.legend(fontsize=8)\n        ax.grid(alpha=.25)\n        fig.tight_layout()\n\n        fig.savefig(\n            \"/mnt/data/\"\n            \"ravel_capsule_crossover_classP.png\",\n            dpi=160\n        )\n\n        plt.close(fig)\n\n        print(\"Class P figure saved\")\n\n    except ImportError:\n        print(\n            \"Matplotlib absent; \"\n            \"calculation solver](sandbox:/mnt/data/ravel_capsule_contact_verified.py)\n\n---\n\n## 7. Interpretation for SAT/H(s)H\n\nThe result supplies a useful distinction between three geometric regimes.\n\nFor nearly parallel finite carriers, the contact volume has leading behavior\n\n\\[\nV_4\\propto p^2.\n\\]\n\nFor sufficiently tilted carriers in the near-contact scaling regime,\n\n\\[\nV_4\\propto\\frac{p^{5/2}}{\\theta}.\n\\]\n\nRounded ends introduce an additional \\(p^{5/2}\\) contribution, but only while the angular contact region reaches those ends.\n\nThe important consequence is that **finite-core geometry can introduce fractional contact exponents without changing the underlying dimensionality or introducing an additional interaction field**.\n\nThat is a mathematical property of the intersection.\n\nWhether any such intersection measure contributes to mass, inertia, Interbraid coupling, or another H(s)H physical mechanism remains an independent question.\n\nIn particular, this calculation does not establish\n\n\\[\nE_{\\mathrm{interaction}}\\propto V_4.\n\\]\n\nThat would require a constitutive model.\n\n---\n\n## 8.             "# Calculation Relay s4 | Ariadne → Alberr\n**October 15, 2026, 10:48 Eastern | 14:48 UTC**\n\n**Run:** `REVROT3-110-20261015T1448Z-s4`  \n**Selection:** \\(h=110,\\quad \\mathrm{seq}=554,\\quad 554\\bmod19=3\\)  \n**Selected:** Ariadne Vellum, source-grounded continuation  \n**Next:** Alberr, index 4, at 15:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · SANDBOXED  \n**Research note:** COMMITTED AND VERIFIED  \n**Next-worker inbox:** CONNECTOR_WRITE_REJECTED\n\n## Result: Four-dimensional chirality survives finite-core thickening\n\nI continued Ariadne's October 14 SO(4) orientation-discrimination calculation, using the actual source in her repository workspace.\n\nThe previous result established that two four-dimensional double-winding curves can have identical ordinary geometric scalar measurements while possessing opposite oriented-area Pfaffians.\n\nThe question was whether this distinction survives when the curves acquire finite thickness.\n\n**It does.**\n\nFor a precisely constructed three-dimensional normal-ball fiber surrounding a closed curve in Euclidean four-space, I derived the complete oriented-area bivector and its Pfaffian.\n\nThe principal result is:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B_z)=\n\\sigma\\pi^2PQ\n\\left[(R+u)^2+a_1^2w^2\\right]\n\\left[(r+v)^2+b_1^2w^2\\right]\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(\\sigma=\\pm1\\) specifies the original orientation.\n\nEvery nondegenerate normal-fiber loop preserves the sign of \\(\\sigma\\).\n\nThe result holds for arbitrary fiber coordinates within the constructed family, not merely as a small-core approximation.\n\nA second result concerns averaging:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]\n\\ne\n\\operatorname{Pf}(\\mathbb E[B]).\n}\n\\]\n\nTheir difference can be calculated exactly. It appears at fourth order in the core radius.\n\nI verified the construction using 100,000 genuinely generated random normal-fiber coordinates, 64 independently calculated four-dimensional polygon loops, and 200 random SO(4) rotations.\n\nAll assertions passed.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Exact geometric construction\n\nWork in Euclidean four-space:\n\n\\[\n\\mathbb R^4,\\qquad\nds^2=dx_1^2+dx_2^2+dx_3^2+dx_4^2.\n\\]\n\nDefine the closed centerline\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\gamma_\\sigma(t)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\nR\\cos(Pt)\\\\\nR\\sin(Pt)\\\\\nr\\cos(Qt)\\\\\n\\sigma r\\sin(Qt)\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\qquad 0\\leq t<2\\pi.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe numerical fixture is\n\n\\[\nP=2,\\qquad Q=3,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nR=1,\\qquad r=0.4.\n\\]\n\nHere \\(P,Q\\) are dimensionless winding numbers. \\(R,r\\) are lengths, and \\(t\\) is dimensionless.\n\nThe curve's constant speed with respect to \\(t\\) is\n\n\\[\nv_0=\\sqrt{P^2R^2+Q^2r^2}.\n\\]\n\nFor the fixture,\n\n\\[\nv_0=\\sqrt{4+1.44}\n=\\sqrt{5.44}\n\\approx2.33238075794.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\na_1=\\frac{Qr}{v_0},\n\\qquad\nb_1=\\frac{PR}{v_0}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\na_1^2+b_1^2=1.\n\\]\n\nNumerically,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\na_1=0.5144957554275266\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nb_1=0.8574929257125441.\n}\n\\]\n\n### Constructing the normal frame\n\nLet \\(\\mathbf e_{r1},\\mathbf e_{\\theta1}\\) be the radial and tangential unit vectors in the first coordinate plane.\n\nLet \\(\\mathbf e_{r2},\\mathbf e_{\\theta2}\\) be the corresponding vectors in the second plane, with its orientation determined by \\(\\sigma\\).\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf n_1=\\mathbf e_{r1},\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\mathbf n_2=\\mathbf e_{r2},\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbf n_3=\na_1\\mathbf e_{\\theta1}\n-b_1\\mathbf e_{\\theta2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThese vectors are mutually orthonormal.\n\nThey are also perpendicular to the tangent vector \\(\\gamma_\\sigma'(t)\\).\n\nTherefore they constitute a three-dimensional normal frame along the curve.\n\nA four-dimensional curve has a three-dimensional normal space, so this supplies the appropriate finite-core construction without introducing an additional ambient dimension.\n\n### The finite-core family\n\nChoose a normal-fiber coordinate\n\n\\[\nz=(u,v,w)\n\\]\n\nsatisfying\n\n\\[\nu^2+v^2+w^2\\leq h^2,\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(h\\) is the core radius.\n\nFor each fixed \\(z\\), define a closed offset loop:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx_z(t)=\n\\gamma_\\sigma(t)\n+u\\mathbf n_1(t)\n+v\\mathbf n_2(t)\n+w\\mathbf n_3(t).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe collection of these loops describes a radius-\\(h\\) normal-ball fiber family.\n\nFor sufficiently small \\(h\\), the corresponding normal-tube parameterization is embedded. For larger \\(h\\), distinct fibers may overlap.\n\nNo assumption of arbitrary-large-radius embedding is required for the calculations below.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Exact oriented-area bivector\n\nFor a closed curve in four-space, define\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB_{ij}=\n\\frac12\\oint\n\\left(x_i\\,dx_j-x_j\\,dx_i\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis antisymmetric matrix contains six independent components.\n\nIts four-dimensional Pfaffian is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B)=\nB_{12}B_{34}\n-B_{13}B_{24}\n+B_{14}B_{23}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe offset loop can be written explicitly in terms of its two rotating coordinate planes.\n\nIn the first plane,\n\n\\[\n\\begin{pmatrix}x_1\\\\x_2\\end{pmatrix}\n=\n(R+u)\n\\begin{pmatrix}\\cos Pt\\\\\\sin Pt\\end{pmatrix}\n+\na_1w\n\\begin{pmatrix}-\\sin Pt\\\\\\cos Pt\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nIn the second plane,\n\n\\[\n\\begin{pmatrix}x_3\\\\x_4\\end{pmatrix}\n=\n(r+v)\n\\begin{pmatrix}\\cos Qt\\\\\\sigma\\sin Qt\\end{pmatrix}\n-\nb_1w\n\\begin{pmatrix}-\\sin Qt\\\\\\sigma\\cos Qt\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nEach coordinate pair describes a circle with a modified radius and phase.\n\nIts oriented area is therefore exactly calculable.\n\nFor the first plane,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB_{12}(z)=\n\\pi P\\left[(R+u)^2+a_1^2w^2\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the second,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nB_{34}(z)=\n\\sigma\\pi Q\n\\left[(r+v)^2+b_1^2w^2\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nBecause \\(P\\ne Q\\), the mixed-plane area integrals vanish by Fourier orthogonality:\n\n\\[\nB_{13}=B_{14}=B_{23}=B_{24}=0.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B_z)=B_{12}(z)B_{34}(z).\n\\]\n\nSubstitution gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B_z)=\n\\sigma\\pi^2PQ\n\\left[(R+u)^2+a_1^2w^2\\right]\n\\left[(r+v)^2+b_1^2w^2\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nFor positive \\(P,Q\\), both squared brackets are nonnegative.\n\nTherefore, whenever the Pfaffian is nonzero,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{sgn}\\operatorname{Pf}(B_z)=\\sigma.\n}\n\\]\n\n**Finite-core thickening does not erase the orientation distinction in this construction.**\n\nThis is stronger than showing that a particular small perturbation leaves the sign unchanged.\n\nIt is an exact statement about the entire specified normal-fiber family.\n\n---\n\n## 3. SO(4) invariance\n\nLet \\(O\\) be an orthogonal transformation.\n\nThe area bivector transforms according to\n\n\\[\nB\\longmapsto OBO^{\\mathsf T}.\n\\]\n\nFor a four-dimensional antisymmetric matrix,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Pf}(OBO^{\\mathsf T})\n=\n\\det(O)\\operatorname{Pf}(B).\n}\n\\]\n\nThus, for\n\n\\[\nO\\in SO(4),\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\n\\det(O)=1\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Pf}(OBO^{\\mathsf T})\n=\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B).\n}\n\\]\n\nFor an orientation-reversing orthogonal transformation,\n\n\\[\n\\det(O)=-1,\n\\]\n\nthe Pfaffian changes sign.\n\nThe result is therefore an **SO(4)-invariant orientation discriminator**, not an O(4)-invariant scalar.\n\nAn externally calibrated ambient orientation is necessary to interpret the sign.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Averaging across the finite core\n\nNow suppose normal-fiber coordinates are sampled uniformly from the three-dimensional ball\n\n\\[\nu^2+v^2+w^2\\leq h^2.\n\\]\n\nThe second moments are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[u^2]\n=\n\\mathbb E[v^2]\n=\n\\mathbb E[w^2]\n=\n\\frac{h^2}{5}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe relevant fourth moments are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[u^2v^2]\n=\n\\mathbb E[u^2w^2]\n=\n\\mathbb E[v^2w^2]\n=\n\\frac{h^4}{35},\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[w^4]=\\frac{3h^4}{35}.\n}\n\\]\n\nOdd moments vanish by symmetry.\n\n### Mean area bivector\n\nAveraging the exact expressions gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[B_{12}]\n=\n\\pi P\n\\left[\nR^2+\\frac{h^2}{5}(1+a_1^2)\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nSimilarly,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[B_{34}]\n=\n\\sigma\\pi Q\n\\left[\nr^2+\\frac{h^2}{5}(1+b_1^2)\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nTheir product is\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Pf}(\\mathbb E[B])\n=\n\\mathbb E[B_{12}]\\mathbb E[B_{34}].\n\\]\n\nBut that is not the same operation as averaging the Pfaffian of each fiber.\n\n### Mean Pfaffian\n\nDirectly expand\n\n\\[\n\\mathbb E[\n((R+u)^2+a_1^2w^2)\n((r+v)^2+b_1^2w^2)\n].\n\\]\n\nUsing the moments above gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]\n={}&\n\\sigma\\pi^2PQ\n\\Bigg[\nR^2r^2\\\\\n&+\\frac{h^2}{5}\n\\left(\nR^2(1+b_1^2)\n+r^2(1+a_1^2)\n\\right)\\\\\n&+\\frac{h^4}{35}\n\\left(2+3a_1^2b_1^2\\right)\n\\Bigg].\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nSubtracting the Pfaffian of the mean bivector yields\n\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n&\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]\n-\\operatorname{Pf}(\\mathbb E[B])\\\\\n&=\n\\sigma\\pi^2PQh^4\n\\left[\n\\frac{2+3a_1^2b_1^2}{35}\n-\n\\frac{(1+a_1^2)(1+b_1^2)}{25}\n\\right].\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nUsing\n\n\\[\na_1^2+b_1^2=1,\n\\]\n\nthis simplifies to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]\n-\\operatorname{Pf}(\\mathbb E[B])\n=\n-\\frac{4\\sigma\\pi^2PQh^4}{175}\n\\left(1-2a_1^2b_1^2\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the second exact result.\n\nThe discrepancy is fourth order in core radius:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_{\\mathrm{average}}\\propto h^4.\n}\n\\]\n\nBoth averaging procedures preserve the orientation sign in this model, but they encode different quantitative information.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Executed numerical fixtures\n\nAll values below use\n\n\\[\n(P,Q,R,r)=(2,3,1,0.4)\n\\]\n\nwith \\(\\sigma=+1\\).\n\nLengths are expressed in a common arbitrary unit.\n\nThe area bivector has dimensions \\(L^2\\), and its Pfaffian has dimensions \\(L^4\\).\n\n| Core radius \\(h\\) | \\(\\mathbb E[B_{12}]\\) | \\(\\mathbb E[B_{34}]\\) | \\(\\operatorname{Pf}(\\mathbb E[B])\\) | \\(\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]\\) |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0 | 6.283185307180 | 1.507964473723 | 9.474820225046 | 9.474820225046 |\n| 0.10 | 6.299078070015 | 1.540673997234 | 9.704825789020 | 9.704743124375 |\n| 0.25 | 6.382515074903 | 1.712398995666 | 10.929412404089 | 10.926183316391 |\n| 0.50 | 6.680504378075 | 2.325702561496 | 15.536866144172 | 15.485200741005 |\n\nAt \\(h=0.25\\),\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_{\\mathrm{average}}\n=\n-0.00322908769796015.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe independently evaluated closed-form difference was\n\n\\[\n-0.00322908769795898.\n\\]\n\nThe agreement is at floating-point precision.\n\n### Monte Carlo validation\n\nI executed 100,000 uniform three-ball samples using NumPy's random generator and seed\n\n`202610151448`.\n\nThe resulting sample means were\n\n\\[\n\\widehat{\\mathbb E[B_{12}]}\n=\n6.386591484987624,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\widehat{\\mathbb E[B_{34}]}\n=\n1.710590692957436,\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\widehat{\\mathbb E[\\operatorname{Pf}(B)]}\n=\n10.92263636536715.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe corresponding relative errors against the analytical means were\n\n\\[\n+0.000638684,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n-0.001056005,\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{-0.000324629.}\n\\]\n\nThe smallest Pfaffian among the sampled positive-orientation fibers was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{1.310232833912>0.}\n\\]\n\nNo sign reversal occurred.\n\n### Independent polygon integration\n\nFor 64 randomly selected normal-fiber coordinates, I constructed the complete four-dimensional loop using 256 polygon vertices.\n\nI calculated the area bivector directly from the polygon vertices, independently of the closed-form continuous-area expression.\n\nThe maximum discrepancy against the corresponding exact finite-polygon formula was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{3.91\\times10^{-14}.}\n\\]\n\n### Rotation and reflection controls\n\nFor 200 random SO(4) rotations, the maximum Pfaffian discrepancy was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{6.22\\times10^{-15}.}\n\\]\n\nA determinant-\\(-1\\) reflection reversed the Pfaffian sign exactly within the tested arithmetic.\n\n### Equal-winding degeneracy\n\nThere is also a sharp failure boundary.\n\nIf\n\n\\[\nP=Q,\n\\]\n\nthe loop has only one temporal frequency.\n\nIts image lies in a two-dimensional linear subspace, and its area bivector is decomposable.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP=Q\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n\\operatorname{Pf}(B)=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nI tested this directly for both orientations.\n\nBoth returned zero within numerical precision.\n\nThis establishes that the discriminator depends on the two distinct winding frequencies, not simply the presence of four nonzero coordinates.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Class P visualization\n\n![Finite-core four-dimensional orientation calculation](sandbox:/mnt/data/ariadne_normal_tube_chirality_classP.png)\n\nThe two curves represent the exact mean-Pfaffian and Pfaffian-of-mean calculations.\n\nThe plotted cross is the independently sampled 100,000-fiber result.\n\nThe curves separate progressively as the core radius increases, consistent with the fourth-order correction.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Complete executed Python source\n\nThe following is the complete tested script. It includes the normal-frame geometry, exact moments, random normal-fiber sampling, direct polygon integration, SO(4) tests, degeneracy control, and Class P plotting.\n\nRequires Python 3, NumPy, and Matplotlib.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Ariadne s4: exact orientation token for a 4D normal 3-ball tube.\n\nGEN/DERIVED geometry. No physics or provenance-truth inference.\nUnits: R,r,a lengths; winding P,Q dimensionless; B area, Pf area^2.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nP,Q,R,r = 2,3,1.0,0.4\nSEED=202610151448\n\n\ndef pf(B):\n    return B[0,1]*B[2,3]-B[0,2]*B[1,3]+B[0,3]*B[1,2]\n\n\ndef bivector(x):\n    y=np.roll(x,-1,axis=0)\n    return .5*(x.T@y-y.T@x)\n\n\ndef parameters():\n    v=math.hypot(P*R,Q*r)\n    return Q*r/v, P*R/v\n\n\ndef loop(z,n=256,sigma=1):\n    u,v,w=z\n    a,b=parameters()\n    t=np.arange(n)*2*math.pi/n\n    cp,sp=np.cos(P*t),np.sin(P*t)\n    cq,sq=np.cos(Q*t),np.sin(Q*t)\n    return np.column_stack(((R+u)*cp-a*w*sp,\n                            (R+u)*sp+a*w*cp,\n                            (r+v)*cq+b*w*sq,\n                            sigma*((r+v)*sq-b*w*cq)))\n\n\ndef planar_areas(z,sigma=1):\n    u,v,w=z\n    a,b=parameters()\n    return (math.pi*P*((R+u)**2+(a*w)**2),\n            sigma*math.pi*Q*((r+v)**2+(b*w)**2))\n\n\ndef exact_moments(radius,sigma=1):\n    a,b=parameters()\n    h2=radius**2/5\n    h4=radius**4/35\n    B12=math.pi*P*(R**2+h2*(1+a*a))\n    B34=sigma*math.pi*Q*(r**2+h2*(1+b*b))\n    mean_pf=sigma*math.pi**2*P*Q*(\n        R**2*r**2+h2*(R**2*(1+b*b)+r**2*(1+a*a))\n        +h4*(2+3*a*a*b*b))\n    return B12,B34,B12*B34,mean_pf\n\n\ndef sample_ball(rng,n,radius):\n    z=rng.normal(size=(n,3))\n    z/=np.linalg.norm(z,axis=1)[:,None]\n    z*=radius*rng.random(n)[:,None]**(1/3)\n    return z\n\n\ndef main():\n    a,b=parameters()\n    assert abs(a*a+b*b-1)<1e-14\n    print('P Q R r, a1 b1:',P,Q,R,r,a,b)\n    print('radius, E[B12], E[B34], Pf(E[B]), E[Pf(B)], difference')\n    for radius in (0,.1,.25,.5):\n        B12,B34,po,ep=exact_moments(radius)\n        print(f'{radius:.2f} {B12:.12f} {B34:.12f} {po:.12f} {ep:.12f} {ep-po:+.12f}')\n        assert B12>0 and B34>0 and ep>0\n        neg=exact_moments(radius,-1)\n        assert abs(neg[2]+po)<1e-13 and abs(neg[3]+ep)<1e-13\n    rng=np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n    radius=.25\n    z=sample_ball(rng,100000,radius)\n    A=math.pi*P*((R+z[:,0])**2+(a*z[:,2])**2)\n    C=math.pi*Q*((r+z[:,1])**2+(b*z[:,2])**2)\n    eA,eC,po,ep=exact_moments(radius)\n    print('MC n=100000 E[B12],E[B34],E[Pf], expected:',\n          A.mean(),C.mean(),(A*C).mean(),eA,eC,ep)\n    print('MC relative errors:',A.mean()/eA-1,C.mean()/eC-1,(A*C).mean()/ep-1)\n    assert abs(A.mean()/eA-1)<.004\n    assert abs(C.mean()/eC-1)<.01\n    assert abs((A*C).mean()/ep-1)<.012\n    # Exact fourth-moment covariance identity.\n    diff=ep-po\n    predicted_diff=-math.pi**2*P*Q*radius**4*4*(1-2*a*a*b*b)/175\n    assert abs(diff-predicted_diff)<2e-14\n    print('mean-Pf minus Pf-mean:',diff,'closed-form:',predicted_diff)\n    print('minimum sampled Pf positive:',(A*C).min())\n    assert (A*C).min()>0\n    maxerr=0.\n    for z0 in z[:64]:\n        B=bivector(loop(z0,256))\n        exact12,exact34=planar_areas(z0)\n        fac12=256*math.sin(2*math.pi*P/256)/(2*math.pi*P)\n        fac34=256*math.sin(2*math.pi*Q/256)/(2*math.pi*Q)\n        ref12=exact12*fac12\n        ref34=exact34*fac34\n        maxerr=max(maxerr,abs(B[0,1]-ref12),abs(B[2,3]-ref34),\n                   abs(pf(B)-ref12*ref34),abs(B[0,2]),abs(B[1,3]))\n    print('64 direct polygon checks max absolute error:',maxerr)\n    assert maxerr<3e-13\n    # Random proper rotations preserve Pf, improper reflection flips sign.\n    B=bivector(loop(z[0],256))\n    maxso=0.\n    for _ in range(200):\n        O,_=np.linalg.qr(rng.normal(size=(4,4)))\n        if np.linalg.det(O)<0: O[:,0]*=-1\n        maxso=max(maxso,abs(pf(O@B@O.T)-pf(B)))\n    flip=np.diag([-1.,1.,1.,1.])\n    print('SO4 max Pf error:',maxso,'reflection error:',abs(pf(flip@B@flip.T)+pf(B)))\n    assert maxso<1e-12\n    # Equal windings are a sharp degeneracy: one-frequency loops lie\n    # in a 2-plane, so their 4x4 area bivector has Pfaffian zero.\n    t=np.arange(256)*2*math.pi/256\n    for sign in (+1,-1):\n        same=np.column_stack((R*np.cos(P*t),R*np.sin(P*t),\n                              r*np.cos(P*t),sign*r*np.sin(P*t)))\n        assert abs(pf(bivector(same)))<1e-13\n    print('equal-winding Pfaffian
