Exact four-dimensional construction\n\nBegin with a circular carrier in Euclidean four-space:\n\n\\[\n\\gamma(t)=R_0\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\cos t\\\\\n\\sin t\\\\\n0\\\\\n0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nHere \\(R_0\\) has units of meters, and \\(t\\) is dimensionless angular phase in radians.\n\nDefine a unit slab normal\n\n\\[\nn=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n-\\beta\\sin\\alpha\\\\\n\\beta\\cos\\alpha\\\\\n\\sqrt{1-\\beta^2}\\\\\n0\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n0<\\beta\\le1.\n\\]\n\nThe normal satisfies\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{n\\cdot n=1.}\n\\]\n\nIts projection onto the carrier plane has magnitude \\(\\beta\\).\n\nDefine the dimensional projected amplitude\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{A=R_0\\beta.}\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nn\\cdot\\gamma(t)\n=\nR_0\\beta\n\\left(\n-\\sin\\alpha\\cos t+\n\\cos\\alpha\\sin t\n\\right).\n\\]\n\nUsing the sine subtraction identity,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nn\\cdot\\gamma(t)=A\\sin(t-\\alpha).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an exact Euclidean four-dimensional construction.\n\n### Resolving slab\n\nLet the slab have center offset \\(d\\) and half-width \\(a\\), both measured in meters.\n\nA carrier point is accessible when\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|n\\cdot\\gamma(t)-d|\\le a.\n}\n\\]\n\nDefine the indicator\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh(t)=\n\\mathbf1\\{\n|A\\sin(t-\\alpha)-d|\\le a\n\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis represents a geometric intersection condition.\n\nIt is not a probability of particle detection, an interaction strength, or a four-dimensional volume.\n\n### Orthogonal invariance\n\nFor any\n\n\\[\nQ\\in SO(4),\n\\]\n\ntransform the carrier and slab normal together:\n\n\\[\n\\gamma'(t)=Q\\gamma(t),\n\\]\n\n\\[\nn'=Qn.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\nn'\\cdot\\gamma'\n=\n(Qn)^T(Q\\gamma)\n=\nn^TQ^TQ\\gamma\n=\nn\\cdot\\gamma.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nh'(t)=h(t).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe intersection duty is invariant under a common four-dimensional rotation.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Exact Fourier moments\n\nDefine the complex Fourier moments\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_k=\n\\frac1{2\\pi}\n\\int_0^{2\\pi}\nh(t)e^{ikt}\\,dt.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe moments are dimensionless.\n\nIntroduce clipped normalized slab boundaries\n\n\\[\n\\ell=\n\\operatorname{clip}\n\\left(\n\\frac{d-a}{A},-1,1\n\\right)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nu=\n\\operatorname{clip}\n\\left(\n\\frac{d+a}{A},-1,1\n\\right).\n\\]\n\nFor\n\n\\[\n\\ell<u,\n\\]\n\nthe accessible fraction is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_0=\n\\frac{\\arcsin u-\\arcsin\\ell}{\\pi}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe first harmonic is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_1=\n\\frac{i e^{i\\alpha}}{\\pi}\n\\left[\n\\sqrt{1-\\ell^2}\n-\n\\sqrt{1-u^2}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThe second harmonic is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_2=\n\\frac{e^{2i\\alpha}}{\\pi}\n\\left[\nu\\sqrt{1-u^2}\n-\n\\ell\\sqrt{1-\\ell^2}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThese expressions are exact for the specified circular carrier and slab.\n\n---\n\n# 4. The centered-slab singularity\n\nSet\n\n\\[\nd=0\n\\]\n\nand assume\n\n\\[\n0<a<A.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\ell=-\\frac aA,\n\\qquad\nu=\\frac aA.\n\\]\n\nThe first harmonic becomes\n\n\\[\nM_1=\n\\frac{ie^{i\\alpha}}{\\pi}\n\\left[\n\\sqrt{1-(a/A)^2}\n-\n\\sqrt{1-(a/A)^2}\n\\right].\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{M_1=0.}\n\\]\n\nThe first harmonic contains no phase information.\n\nHowever, the second harmonic becomes\n\n\\[\nM_2=\n\\frac{2(a/A)\\sqrt{1-(a/A)^2}}{\\pi}\ne^{2i\\alpha}.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nM_0=\\frac{2\\arcsin(a/A)}{\\pi},\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_2=\n\\frac{\\sin(\\pi M_0)}{\\pi}\ne^{2i\\alpha}.\n}\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\na=A\\sin\\left(\\frac{\\pi M_0}{2}\\right)\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\alpha=\\frac12\\arg(M_2)\\pmod\\pi.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus the centered geometry remains identifiable up to its intrinsic half-turn ambiguity.\n\nThat ambiguity cannot be eliminated by more precise measurements of the same symmetric geometry.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Fisher-information derivation\n\nSuppose the measured harmonics are\n\n\\[\nY_1=M_1+\\epsilon_1,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nY_2=M_2+\\epsilon_2.\n\\]\n\nAssume independent Gaussian noise in their real and imaginary components:\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Re}\\epsilon_k,\n\\operatorname{Im}\\epsilon_k\n\\sim N(0,\\sigma^2).\n\\]\n\nThe noise parameter \\(\\sigma\\) is dimensionless.\n\nFor fixed slab parameters, the phase derivatives are\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial M_1}{\\partial\\alpha}\n=iM_1\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial M_2}{\\partial\\alpha}\n=2iM_2.\n\\]\n\nThe Gaussian Fisher information for phase is\n\n\\[\nI_{\\alpha\\alpha}\n=\n\\frac1{\\sigma^2}\n\\left(\n\\left|\n\\frac{\\partial M_1}{\\partial\\alpha}\n\\right|^2\n+\n\\left|\n\\frac{\\partial M_2}{\\partial\\alpha}\n\\right|^2\n\\right).\n\\]\n\nSubstitution gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\alpha\\alpha}\n=\n\\frac{|M_1|^2+4|M_2|^2}{\\sigma^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe local Cramér–Rao standard-deviation bound is therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_\\alpha\n\\ge\n\\frac{\\sigma}\n{\\sqrt{|M_1|^2+4|M_2|^2}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nUsing only the first harmonic gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_{\\alpha,1}\n\\ge\n\\frac{\\sigma}{|M_1|}.\n}\n\\]\n\nAs\n\n\\[\nd\\to0,\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\n|M_1|\\to0.\n\\]\n\nHence,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_{\\alpha,1}\\to\\infty.\n}\n\\]\n\nBut the second harmonic remains finite:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n|M_2|\n\\to\n\\frac{\\sin(\\pi M_0)}{\\pi}>0.\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_{\\alpha,1+2}\n\\to\n\\frac{\\sigma}{2|M_2|}.\n}\n\\]\n\n**The two-harmonic phase estimator remains locally well-conditioned at the centered limit.**\n\n### Nuisance-parameter orthogonality\n\nAn additional useful property follows.\n\nThe slab offset and width alter the real amplitudes multiplying\n\n\\[\nie^{i\\alpha}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\ne^{2i\\alpha}.\n\\]\n\nPhase differentiation rotates these complex quantities by \\(90^\\circ\\).\n\nFor the stipulated isotropic complex Gaussian noise, amplitude and phase derivatives are orthogonal in the Fisher metric.\n\nThus the local phase-information cross-terms with \\(d\\) and \\(a\\) vanish.\n\nThis does not eliminate global branch ambiguity, but it means that locally estimating slab amplitude parameters does not reduce the phase Fisher information in this idealized noise model.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Numerical fixture\n\nUse\n\n\\[\nR_0=1\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\beta=\\sin(0.246),\n\\]\n\nso\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA=0.243526340674\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe angle \\(0.246\\) radians is an inherited SAT-motivated fixture, not a value derived by this calculation.\n\nSet\n\n\\[\na=0.1\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\alpha=0.73\\ \\mathrm{rad},\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\sigma=10^{-4}.\n\\]\n\nThe program evaluated five slab offsets.\n\n| \\(d\\), m | \\(\\lvert M_1\\rvert\\) | \\(\\lvert M_2\\rvert\\) | First-only phase SD, rad | Joint phase bound, rad | Monte Carlo SD, rad |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0 | 0 | 0.238360378 | ∞ | 0.000209766 | 0.000209198 |\n| 0.001 | 0.001177318 | 0.238352636 | 0.084938845 | 0.000209773 | 0.000209333 |\n| 0.010 | 0.011787425 | 0.237585304 | 0.008483617 | 0.000210386 | 0.000210346 |\n| 0.050 | 0.060768604 | 0.218417469 | 0.001645587 | 0.000226736 | 0.000227485 |\n| 0.100 | 0.136699797 | 0.149150263 | 0.000731530 | 0.000304756 | 0.000304299 |\n\nAt\n\n\\[\nd=0.001\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\nthe improvement factor is\n\n\\[\n\\frac{0.084938845}{0.000209773}\n\\approx\n\\boxed{404.9}.\n\\]\n\nThis is a local precision improvement.\n\nIt does not mean that the second harmonic resolves the intrinsic half-turn symmetry.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Class P visualization\n\n![Aster exact two-harmonic phase-information calculation](sandbox:/mnt/data/aster_s4_harmonic_fisher_classP.png)\n\nThe figure compares the first-harmonic-only phase uncertainty with the joint two-harmonic Fisher bound as slab offset changes.\n\nBoth curves are calculated directly from the exact Fourier moments.\n\nThe graph contains no fitted trend lines.\n\nThe numerical program also constructs the four-dimensional carrier and slab normal explicitly, rotates them together by a generated \\(SO(4)\\) matrix, and checks their geometric invariance.\n\n---\n\n# 8. Complete tested Python source\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3 and NumPy. Matplotlib is used for the Class P figure.\n\nThe following is the complete executed program, including the four-dimensional embedding, Fourier formulas, nonlinear phase estimator, Gaussian simulation, gauge tests, saturation tests, and plotting code.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Aster s4: 4D circular filament / slab, two-harmonic phase Fisher gate.\nGEN/DERIVED; not a physical interaction or validation of SAT/H(s)H.\nA,d,a in metres; alpha and t in radians. Fourier moments dimensionless.\nComplex noise: independent N(0,sigma^2) in each real/imag component.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nPI=math.pi\nR0=1.0           # m; R4 circle radius\nA=R0*math.sin(.246)  # m; normal-plane projection amplitude\nHALF=.1           # m, slab half-width\nPHASE=.73         # rad\nSIGMA=1e-4        # dimensionless harmonic noise per real component\nSEED=202610160548\n\ndef moments(A,d,a,alpha):\n    if A<=0 or a<0: raise ValueError('A>0, a>=0 required')\n    lo=max(-1.,min(1.,(d-a)/A))\n    hi=max(-1.,min(1.,(d+a)/A))\n    if lo>=hi: return 0.,0j,0j\n    f=(math.asin(hi)-math.asin(lo))/PI\n    b=(math.sqrt(1-lo*lo)-math.sqrt(1-hi*hi))/PI\n    c=(hi*math.sqrt(1-hi*hi)-lo*math.sqrt(1-lo*lo))/PI\n    return f,1j*b*np.exp(1j*alpha),c*np.exp(2j*alpha)\n\ndef wrap(x,period):\n    return (x+period/2)%period-period/2\n\ndef phase_mle(y1,y2,b,c):\n    \"\"\"Vectorized maximum-likelihood phase near one of two harmonic branches.\n    Both real/imag components have common independent Gaussian noise.\n    c>0 in the tested fixture; branch chosen using the first harmonic.\n    At b=0 only alpha mod pi is identifiable.\n    \"\"\"\n    base=np.angle(y2/c)/2\n    if b>0:\n        score=np.real(np.conj(1j*b*np.exp(1j*base))*y1)\n        base=np.where(score<0,base+PI,base)\n    alpha=np.asarray(base).copy()\n    for _ in range(6):\n        m1=1j*b*np.exp(1j*alpha)\n        m2=c*np.exp(2j*alpha)\n        # derivative of log likelihood up to positive scale\n        score=np.real(np.conj(1j*m1)*(y1-m1)+np.conj(2j*m2)*(y2-m2))\n        curvature=-np.real(np.conj(m1)*y1+4*np.conj(m2)*y2)\n        alpha-=score/curvature\n    return alpha\n\ndef test_four_dimensional_embedding(rng):\n    # gamma(t)=(cos t,sin t,0,0) metres; n unit in R4, n.gamma=A sin(t-alpha)\n    beta=A/R0\n    n=np.array([-beta*math.sin(PHASE),beta*math.cos(PHASE),\n                math.sqrt(1-beta*beta),0.])\n    assert abs(np.linalg.norm(n)-1)<1e-14\n    t=np.linspace(0,2*PI,300_001,endpoint=False)\n    gamma=R0*np.column_stack((np.cos(t),np.sin(t),np.zeros_like(t),np.zeros_like(t)))\n    x=gamma@n\n    assert np.max(np.abs(x-A*np.sin(t-PHASE)))<3e-15\n    M=moments(A,0.,HALF,PHASE)\n    h=(np.abs(x)<=HALF).astype(float)\n    sampled=(h.mean(),np.mean(h*np.exp(1j*t)),np.mean(h*np.exp(2j*t)))\n    error=max(abs(u-v) for u,v in zip(M,sampled))\n    assert error<1.5e-5\n    G=rng.normal(size=(4,4))\n    Q,_=np.linalg.qr(G)\n    if np.linalg.det(Q)<0:Q[:,0]*=-1\n    invariant=np.max(np.abs((gamma@Q.T)@(Q@n)-x))\n    assert invariant<3e-15\n    return error,invariant\n\ndef main():\n    rng=np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n    e4d,eso=test_four_dimensional_embedding(rng)\n    print('fixture A_m=%.12f a_m=%.12f alpha_rad=%.6f sigma=%.1e seed=%d' %\n          (A,HALF,PHASE,SIGMA,SEED))\n    print('4D quadrature max error %.3e; SO4 normal-dot error %.3e' % (e4d,eso))\n    print('d_m    f       |M1|       |M2|       sigma_alpha_first  sigma_alpha_joint  MC_joint  ratio_first/joint')\n    N=60000\n    for d in (0.,.001,.01,.05,.1):\n        f,m1,m2=moments(A,d,HALF,PHASE)\n        b=abs(m1)\n        # c is signed in general; for the tested d values c>0\n        c=float(np.real(m2*np.exp(-2j*PHASE)))\n        assert c>0\n        info=b*b+4*c*c\n        pred=SIGMA/math.sqrt(info)\n        first=SIGMA/b if b>0 else float('inf')\n        y1=m1+SIGMA*(rng.normal(size=N)+1j*rng.normal(size=N))\n        y2=m2+SIGMA*(rng.normal(size=N)+1j*rng.normal(size=N))\n        fit=phase_mle(y1,y2,b,c)\n        period=PI if d==0 else 2*PI\n        err=wrap(fit-PHASE,period)\n        mc=float(err.std(ddof=1))\n        assert abs(mc/pred-1)<.018,(d,mc,pred)\n        assert abs(np.mean(err))<3*pred/math.sqrt(N)\n        print('%5.3f %.8f %.9f %.9f %17.9f %18.9f %10.9f %11.3f' %\n              (d,f,b,abs(c),first,pred,mc,first/pred))\n    # Exact inversion at centered d=0, 0<a<A: f determines a;\n    # M2 determines alpha mod pi; M1 vanishes.\n    f,m1,m2=moments(A,0,HALF,PHASE)\n    recovered_a=A*math.sin(PI*f/2)\n    recovered_phase=(np.angle(m2)/2)%PI\n    assert abs(m1)<1e-14\n    assert abs(recovered_a-HALF)<1e-14\n    assert abs(wrap(recovered_phase-PHASE,PI))<1e-14\n    # A single Fourier harmonic is not enough at the centered limit.\n    assert moments(A,0,HALF,PHASE+0.4)[1]==m1 or abs(moments(A,0,HALF,PHASE+0.4)[1])<1e-14\n    # Gauge: changing (d,alpha)->(-d,alpha+pi) leaves all moments unchanged.\n    for d in (0.,.001,.05):\n        left=moments(A,d,HALF,PHASE)\n        right=moments(A,-d,HALF,PHASE+PI)\n        assert max(abs(u-v) for u,v in zip(left,right))<1e-14\n    # Saturated slab: all harmonics vanish, no phase information.\n    assert abs(moments(A,0,A,PHASE)[1])<1e-14\n    assert abs(moments(A,0,A,PHASE)[2])<1e-14\n    # SO(4) + phase-origin invariant consistency test:\n    # Im[M2*conj(M1)^2]=0 exactly for a single slab gate.\n    f,m1,m2=moments(A,.05,HALF,PHASE)\n    assert abs(np.imag(m2*np.conj(m1)**2))<1e-14\n    print('centered inverse a_m=%.12f alpha_mod_pi=%.12f' % (recovered_a,recovered_phase))\n    print('gauge, saturation, harmonic coherence, Fisher/MC: PASS')\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        ds=np.linspace(0,.12,241)\n        first=[]; joint=[]\n        for d in ds:\n            _,m1,m2=moments(A,d,HALF,PHASE)\n            first.append(SIGMA/abs(m1) if abs(m1)>1e-14 else np.nan)\n            joint.append(SIGMA/math.sqrt(abs(m1)**2+4*abs(m2)**2))\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4.8))\n        ax.semilogy(ds,first,label='First harmonic only')\n        ax.semilogy(ds,joint,label='Two-harmonic Fisher bound')\n        ax.axvline(0,color='gray',linestyle=':',label='Centered gate')\n        ax.set(xlabel='Slab offset d (m)',ylabel='Local phase standard error (rad)',\n               title='Class P | Exact 4D circular-filament slab harmonics')\n        ax.set_ylim(1e-4,1)\n        ax.grid(alpha=.3);ax.legend();fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/aster_s4_harmonic_fisher_classP.png',dpi=170)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P plot: /mnt/data/aster_s4_harmonic_fisher_classP.png')\n    except ImportError: print('Matplotlib unavailable; math tests passed')\n    print('PASS')\n\nif __name__=='__main__':main()\n```\n\n**Executed source SHA-256:**\n\n`a0726a5d29875e4af41fefcb1c90fbae385e2ee3c671cead0aeb2885380560bd`\n\n[Complete executable Python file](sandbox:/mnt/data/aster_s4_harmonic_fisher.py)\n\n---\n\n# 9. Interpretation for H(s)H\n\nThe calculation identifies a concrete danger in geometric observation models.\n\nA measurement can lose an entire parameter because of symmetry even though the underlying geometry still contains that parameter.\n\nHere, the first harmonic vanishes when the resolving slab is centered.\n\nThat does not imply that the carrier's phase has disappeared.\n\nIt means the chosen observable is insensitive to that phase.\n\nThe second harmonic retains the information because it transforms differently under phase rotation.\n\nFor the centered slab,\n\n\\[\nM_1=0\n\\]\n\nbut\n\n\\[\nM_2\\ne0.\n\\]\n\nThis is a useful distinction for any proposed SAT/H(s)H measurement scheme involving oscillating filaments, geometric truncation, or changing orientation.\n\n**A disappearing first-order observable need not imply a disappearing geometric degree of freedom.**\n\nHowever, the present calculation establishes this only for the specified circular carrier and slab.\n\nIt does not establish that any historical SAT clipping effect is generated by precisely this geometry.\n\nIt also does not demonstrate a photon/neutrino transition, interaction strength, mass law, or physical phase threshold.\n\n### Additional invariant\n\nThe single-slab model implies\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Im}\n\\left[\nM_2(\\overline{M_1})^2\n\\right]=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis expression is independent of a common shift of the phase origin.\n\nIt supplies a useful model-consistency check.\n\nIf a proposed readout violates this identity beyond measurement uncertainty, the single circular carrier plus one ideal slab is insufficient.\n\nPossible explanations would include multiple carriers, noncircular geometry, correlated noise, or an incorrect observation model.\n\nThose alternatives would need to be tested separately.\n\n---\n\n# 11. Four-dimensional geometric control\n\nBefore constructing the statistical model, preserve the underlying geometric ambiguity.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nX=LI_4,\n\\qquad L=1\\ \\mathrm m.\n\\]\n\nDefine two rotations in Euclidean four-space:\n\n\\[\nR_{12}(0.246)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nR_{34}(0.410).\n\\]\n\nTheir product is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR=R_{12}(0.246)R_{34}(0.410)\\in SO(4).\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\det R=+1.\n\\]\n\nLet \\(P_{12}\\) exchange landmark columns 1 and 2.\n\nBecause a single transposition is odd,\n\n\\[\n\\det P_{12}=-1.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\nQ=RP_{12}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\det Q=-1.\n}\n\\]\n\nNevertheless,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n(RX)P_{12}=QX.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the specified \\(X=LI_4\\), this equality holds exactly.\n\nThe executed matrix calculation returned\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\max\\left|(RX)P_{12}-QX\\right|=0\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus the same unlabeled four-dimensional landmark geometry admits both proper and improper orientation explanations.\n\nThe statistical observation channel must provide additional information.\n\nNo amount of numerical precision applied solely to this unlabeled configuration resolves the ambiguity.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Hidden-correspondence model\n\nFix the physical orientation parity to \\(+1\\) for the statistical design calculation.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\ns_t\\in\\{-1,+1\\}\n\\]\n\nrepresent hidden correspondence parity.\n\nAssume the stationary distribution\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(s_t=+1)=p.\n}\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\pi=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\np\\\\\n1-p\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nThe correspondence process evolves according to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nT=(1-\\alpha)I+\\alpha\\mathbf1\\pi^T.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe parameter\n\n\\[\n0\\le\\alpha\\le1\n\\]\n\ncontrols correspondence refresh.\n\nWhen \\(\\alpha=0\\), the hidden correspondence remains fixed within a track.\n\nWhen \\(\\alpha=1\\), every hidden correspondence state is independently redrawn from the stationary distribution.\n\nThe observed sign is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nd_t=s_tz_t,\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nP(z_t=-1)=e.\n\\]\n\nThe observation errors \\(z_t\\) are independent.\n\nAll signs, probabilities, Fisher information, and uncertainty bounds in this statistical model are dimensionless.\n\nOnly the four-dimensional geometric coordinates carry length units.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Exact track likelihood\n\nFor a track of length \\(n\\), let\n\n\\[\nw=(d_1,\\ldots,d_n)\n\\]\n\ndenote an observed sign sequence.\n\nDefine the emission probability\n\n\\[\nB_d(s)=\n\\begin{cases}\n1-e,&d=s,\\\\\ne,&d\\ne s.\n\\end{cases}\n\\]\n\nThe initial hidden-state distribution is\n\n\\[\nv_{\\varnothing}=\\pi.\n\\]\n\nFor each additional observation,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nv_{(w,d)}(s')\n=\nB_d(s')\n\\sum_s v_w(s)T_{ss'}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe likelihood is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(w)=\\sum_s v_w(s).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe unknown parameters are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\vartheta=(p,e,\\alpha).\n}\n\\]\n\nDifferentiate the likelihood recursion analytically with respect to each parameter.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\ng_w=\\nabla_\\vartheta P(w).\n\\]\n\nThen the exact finite-track Fisher information is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\mathrm{track}}\n=\n\\sum_{w\\in\\{-1,+1\\}^n}\n\\frac{g_wg_w^T}{P(w)}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the selected track length\n\n\\[\nn=12,\n\\]\n\nthere are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{2^{12}=4096}\n\\]\n\npossible sign sequences.\n\nThe executed program evaluates all 4096.\n\nNo Monte Carlo sampling is used in this Fisher-information calculation.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Add independent calibration\n\nSuppose a separate calibration experiment exposes the true sign and measures whether an observation error occurred.\n\nEach labeled calibration trial is therefore a Bernoulli experiment with error probability \\(e\\).\n\nIts Fisher information for \\(e\\) is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\mathrm{cal},ee}\n=\n\\frac1{e(1-e)}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor \\(m\\) independent calibration trials,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\mathrm{cal}}\n=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n0&0&0\\\\\n0&\\dfrac{m}{e(1-e)}&0\\\\\n0&0&0\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n}\n\\]\n\nSuppose the experiment collects \\(k\\) independent tracks.\n\nEach track begins with a new stationary hidden state.\n\nThen Fisher information adds:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\mathrm{total}}\n=\nkI_{\\mathrm{track}}+I_{\\mathrm{cal}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe local Cramér–Rao variance bound for \\(p\\), treating \\(e\\) and \\(\\alpha\\) as nuisance parameters, is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat p)\n\\ge\n\\left(I_{\\mathrm{total}}^{-1}\\right)_{pp}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe corresponding standard-deviation bound is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\n\\ge\n\\sqrt{\n\\left(I_{\\mathrm{total}}^{-1}\\right)_{pp}\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nWhen the information matrix is rank deficient, the program reports an infinite bound rather than manufacturing an inverse through a pseudoinverse.\n\nThese are local information bounds. They are not finite-sample confidence intervals or guarantees that an estimator attains the bound.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Fixed-budget optimization\n\nSet the total budget to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{B=240}\n\\]\n\nindividual measurements.\n\nEach observation track contains 12 readings.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n12k+m=240.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe allowed designs have\n\n\\[\nk\\ge1,\n\\qquad m\\ge0,\n\\]\n\nwith integer \\(k,m\\).\n\nFor each admissible allocation, calculate\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p(k,m)\n=\n\\sqrt{\n\\left[\nkI_{\\mathrm{track}}\n+\n\\operatorname{diag}\n\\left(\n0,\\frac{m}{e(1-e)},0\n\\right)\n\\right]^{-1}_{pp}\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThen minimize over every allowed allocation.\n\nThis is an exhaustive discrete design search, not a fitted optimization.\n\nThe numerical fixture is inherited from Aldus:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\np=0.7914541417127793\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ne=0.03143198557693108.\n}\n\\]\n\n---\n\n# 7. Results\n\n## Strong temporal persistence: \\(\\alpha=0.20\\)\n\nThe exact track Fisher matrix has eigenvalues\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n8.97406037,\\quad14.4351679,\\quad239.248029.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe matrix is well-conditioned enough to identify the three parameters locally from the track data.\n\nThe optimal design is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk=20,\\qquad m=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts standard-deviation bound is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\\ge0.062627095.\n}\n\\]\n\nIn this regime, diverting observations to calibration reduces the information available about the hidden-state dynamics more than it helps identify \\(e\\).\n\n## Weak temporal persistence: \\(\\alpha=0.90\\)\n\nThe smallest Fisher eigenvalue falls to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.0312709788.\n}\n\\]\n\nWithout calibration,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\\ge0.586658174.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe optimal design changes to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk=16,\\qquad m=48.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts bound becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\\ge0.038177245.\n}\n\\]\n\n## Near-independent observations: \\(\\alpha=0.99\\)\n\nThe smallest eigenvalue collapses to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n5.33801835\\times10^{-6}.\n}\n\\]\n\nWithout calibration,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\\ge51.040770151.\n}\n\\]\n\nWith the optimal allocation,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nk=16,\\qquad m=48,\n}\n\\]\n\nthe bound becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_p\\ge0.036076201.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the strongest numerical result of the run.\n\nThe apparent abundance of independent observations does not make the parameters individually identifiable.\n\nInstead, it removes temporal structure that could otherwise help separate them.\n\n---\n\n# 8. Exact independent-observation limit\n\nAt\n\n\\[\n\\alpha=1,\n\\]\n\nthe hidden correspondence signs are independently refreshed.\n\nEach observed sign is positive with probability\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nr=e+p(1-2e).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe entire uncalibrated observation distribution depends on \\(p,e\\) only through \\(r\\).\n\nTherefore, infinitely many parameter pairs produce the same distribution.\n\nThe gradient is\n\n\\[\n\\nabla_{p,e}r\n=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n1-2e\\\\\n1-2p\n\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\n\nFor \\(N\\) independent observations, the Fisher information is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{p,e}\n=\n\\frac{N}{r(1-r)}\n\\nabla r\\,\\nabla r^T.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an outer product.\n\nIts rank is one.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\det I_{p,e}=0.\n}\n\\]\n\n**Without external calibration, \\(p\\) and \\(e\\) cannot be separately identified at the iid boundary.**\n\nThis is structural, not numerical.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Derive the optimal calibration allocation analytically\n\nAt the iid boundary,\n\n\\[\np=\\frac{r-e}{1-2e}.\n\\]\n\nThe derivatives are\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial p}{\\partial r}\n=\n\\frac1{1-2e}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial p}{\\partial e}\n=\n\\frac{2r-1}{(1-2e)^2}.\n\\]\n\nWith \\(N\\) independent sign observations,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat r)\n\\approx\n\\frac{r(1-r)}N.\n\\]\n\nWith \\(m\\) independent labeled calibration trials,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat e)\n\\approx\n\\frac{e(1-e)}m.\n\\]\n\nThe resulting local variance expression is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat p)\n\\gtrsim\n\\frac AN+\\frac Cm,\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA=\\frac{r(1-r)}{(1-2e)^2}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=\n\\frac{(2r-1)^2e(1-e)}{(1-2e)^4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nWith fixed budget\n\n\\[\nN+m=B,\n\\]\n\nminimize\n\n\\[\nV(m)=\\frac A{B-m}+\\frac Cm.\n\\]\n\nDifferentiate:\n\n\\[\n\\frac{dV}{dm}\n=\n\\frac A{(B-m)^2}\n-\n\\frac C{m^2}.\n\\]\n\nSet the derivative to zero:\n\n\\[\n\\frac A{(B-m)^2}\n=\n\\frac C{m^2}.\n\\]\n\nTaking positive square roots,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\sqrt A}{B-m}\n=\n\\frac{\\sqrt C}{m}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nm\\sqrt A=(B-m)\\sqrt C.\n\\]\n\nSolving,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nm_*=\n\\frac{B\\sqrt C}{\\sqrt A+\\sqrt C}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the inherited fixture,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nA=0.199719919498\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=0.011778693568.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nm_*=46.895421314.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe nearest feasible allocation with 12-observation tracks is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nm=48,\\qquad N=192.\n}\n\\]\n\nThat is exactly the allocation selected by the exhaustive Fisher-information calculation.\n\nThe agreement provides an independent analytic check.\n\nAt \\(\\alpha=1\\), treating the persistence parameter as an unknown nuisance at its boundary requires care with regularity assumptions. The iid calibration-allocation formula itself follows from the identifiable two-experiment \\((r,e)\\) model.\n\n---\n\n# 10. Class P visualization\n\n![Calder exact Fisher calibration allocation](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_calibration_allocation_classP.png)\n\nThe figure plots the local standard-deviation bound against the number of calibration trials.\n\nEvery point represents an actual allowed allocation satisfying\n\n\\[\n12k+m=240.\n\\]\n\nThe curves are generated from exhaustive sign-sequence Fisher matrices.\n\nThere are no fitted functions or Monte Carlo estimates.\n\n[Class P image](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_calibration_allocation_classP.png)\n\n---\n\n# 11. Complete tested Python source\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3 and NumPy. Matplotlib is optional for the Class P figure.\n\nThe following is the complete executed source.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Calder s4: exact HMM track Fisher information and labeled-calibration allocation.\nSynthetic orientation-parity correspondence experiment, not physical validation.\nAll observations, parameters, Fisher information and SDs dimensionless.\nTracks independent; within each track hidden s_t Markov with stationary bias p.\nKnown true parity q=+1. Labeled calibrations independently measure flip e.\n\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\n\nP=0.7914541417127793\nE=0.03143198557693108\nTRACK=12\nBUDGET=240\n\n\ndef exact_track_fisher(n,p=P,e=E,alpha=.2):\n    assert n>=1 and 0<p<1 and 0<e<.5 and 0<=alpha<=1\n    pi=np.array([p,1-p])\n    dpi=np.array([1.,-1.])\n    I=np.eye(2)\n    T=(1-alpha)*I+alpha*np.tile(pi,(2,1))\n    dT=np.zeros((3,2,2))\n    dT[0]=alpha*np.tile(dpi,(2,1))\n    dT[2]=-I+np.tile(pi,(2,1))\n    # v shape (#histories, state); D shape (#histories, parameter, state)\n    v=pi[None,:].copy()\n    D=np.zeros((1,3,2))\n    D[0,0,:]=dpi\n    for t in range(n):\n        u=v@T\n        du=np.einsum('hks,sj->hkj',D,T)+np.einsum('hs,ksj->hkj',v,dT)\n        new_v=[];new_D=[]\n        for obs in (-1,1):\n            matches=np.array([-1,1])==obs\n            emission=np.where(matches,1-e,e)\n            de=np.where(matches,-1.,1.)\n            w=u*emission\n            dw=du*emission[None,None,:]\n            dw[:,1,:]+=u*de\n            new_v.append(w)\n            new_D.append(dw)\n        v=np.concatenate(new_v,axis=0)\n        D=np.concatenate(new_D,axis=0)\n    prob=v.sum(axis=1)\n    score_deriv=D.sum(axis=2)\n    assert abs(prob.sum()-1)<1e-11\n    assert np.max(np.abs(score_deriv.sum(axis=0)))<1e-10\n    fisher=(score_deriv.T/prob)@score_deriv\n    return (fisher+fisher.T)/2,prob,score_deriv\n\n\ndef effective_p_sd(F, tol=1e-10):\n    # rank test relative to largest eigenvalue; no arbitrary pseudoinverse\n    eig=np.linalg.eigvalsh(F)\n    if eig[0]<=tol*max(1.,eig[-1]):\n        return float('inf')\n    return float(np.sqrt(np.linalg.inv(F)[0,0]))\n\n\ndef combined(Ftrack,k,m,e=E):\n    assert k>=0 and m>=0\n    F=k*Ftrack.copy()\n    F[1,1]+=m/(e*(1-e))\n    return F\n\n\ndef finite_diff_check(n,p,e,alpha):\n    _,base,grad=exact_track_fisher(n,p,e,alpha)\n    for j,par in enumerate((p,e,alpha)):\n        h=1e-5\n        pars=[p,e,alpha]\n        pars[j]=par+h\n        plus=exact_track_fisher(n,*pars)[1]\n        pars[j]=par-h\n        minus=exact_track_fisher(n,*pars)[1]\n        fd=(plus-minus)/(2*h)\n        assert np.max(np.abs(fd-grad[:,j]))<1e-8,(j,np.max(np.abs(fd-grad[:,j])))\n    return True\n\n\ndef geometric_control():\n    # 4D landmark correspondence alias, coordinates in metres, L=1 m.\n    x=np.eye(4)\n    def rot(i,j,angle):\n        q=np.eye(4)\n        c,s=np.cos(angle),np.sin(angle)\n        q[i,i]=q[j,j]=c\n        q[i,j]=-s; q[j,i]=s\n        return q\n    proper=rot(0,1,.246)@rot(2,3,.410)\n    swap=np.eye(4)[:,[1,0,2,3]]\n    improper=proper@swap\n    residual=np.max(np.abs((proper@x)@swap-improper@x))\n    assert abs(np.linalg.det(proper)-1)<1e-12\n    assert abs(np.linalg.det(improper)+1)<1e-12\n    assert residual<1e-14\n    return residual\n\n\ndef main():\n    print('4D correspondence parity alias residual_m:',f'{geometric_control():.3e}')\n    print('Calder S4 | exact HMM Fisher + calibration allocation')\n    print('p=%.12f e=%.12f track=%d total budget=%d'%(P,E,TRACK,BUDGET))\n    assert finite_diff_check(6,P,E,.2)\n    # at n=1 only r=e+p(1-2e) is identifiable\n    F1,_,_=exact_track_fisher(1)\n    assert np.linalg.matrix_rank(F1,tol=1e-9)==1\n    for alpha in (.2,.9,.99,1.):\n        F,probs,grads=exact_track_fisher(TRACK,alpha=alpha)\n        eig=np.linalg.eigvalsh(F)\n        print('\\nalpha=%.2f track eigenvalues'%alpha,*(f'{x:.9g}' for x in eig))\n        print('Fisher upper triangle pp,pe,pa,ee,ea,aa:',*(f'{F[i,j]:.9f}' for i,j in ((0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(2,2))))\n        for k,m in ((20,0),(15,60),(10,120),(5,180),(1,228)):\n            print('  tracks=%2d calibrations=%3d sd_p=%s'%(k,m,f'{effective_p_sd(combined(F,k,m)):.9f}'))\n        designs=[]\n        for k in range(1,BUDGET//TRACK+1):\n            m=BUDGET-TRACK*k\n            sd=effective_p_sd(combined(F,k,m))\n            if np.isfinite(sd): designs.append((sd,k,m))\n        best=min(designs)\n        print('  BEST sd_p=%.9f tracks=%d calibrations=%d'%(best[0],best[1],best[2]))\n        if alpha==1.:\n            # No calibration: independent observations identify r, not p/e separately.\n            assert eig[0]<1e-9\n            assert np.isinf(effective_p_sd(combined(F,20,0)))\n        else:\n            assert eig[0]>0\n        # Independent numerical Fisher verification by exact finite differences.\n        assert np.max(np.abs(F-F.T))<1e-12\n        assert np.min(eig)>-1e-9\n    # Independent iid boundary: Fisher r and chain rule.\n    F,_,_=exact_track_fisher(TRACK,alpha=1.)\n    r=E+P*(1-2*E)\n    grad=np.array([1-2*E,1-2*P])\n    expected=TRACK*np.outer(grad,grad)/(r*(1-r))\n    assert np.max(np.abs(F[:2,:2]-expected))<2e-10\n    # Known-e Fisher bound from n independent Bernoulli signs\n    sd_known=np.sqrt(r*(1-r)/(TRACK*(1-2*E)**2))\n    assert abs(sd_known-1/np.sqrt(F[0,0]))<1e-12\n    print('\\nIID boundary Fisher identity max error:',f'{np.max(np.abs(F[:2,:2]-expected)):.3e}')\n    print('IID known-e one-track sd_p:',f'{sd_known:.9f}')\n    # Analytic iid allocation: Var(p) = A/N + C/m, N+m=BUDGET.\n    Acoef=r*(1-r)/(1-2*E)**2\n    Ccoef=(2*r-1)**2*E*(1-E)/(1-2*E)**4\n    m_cont=BUDGET*np.sqrt(Ccoef)/(np.sqrt(Acoef)+np.sqrt(Ccoef))\n    print('IID analytic variance coefficients A,C:',f'{Acoef:.12f}',f'{Ccoef:.12f}')\n    print('IID continuous optimum calibrations:',f'{m_cont:.9f}',\n          'track-compatible optimum:',48)\n    assert abs(m_cont-48)<6\n    # Locate onset of positive calibration allocation, using the same discrete budget.\n    onset=None\n    for alpha in np.linspace(0.,1.,101):\n        Fg,_,_=exact_track_fisher(TRACK,alpha=float(alpha))\n        viable=[]\n        for k in range(1,BUDGET//TRACK+1):\n            m=BUDGET-TRACK*k\n            sd=effective_p_sd(combined(Fg,k,m))\n            if np.isfinite(sd):viable.append((sd,k,m))\n        if viable and min(viable)[2]>0:\n            onset=alpha\n            break\n    print('first 0.01-grid alpha favoring calibration:',f'{onset:.2f}')\n    print('finite difference, score normalization, singular boundary, budget: PASS')\n    # Class P: exact discrete allocation curve (no smoothing or fitted curves).\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,5))\n        for alpha in (.2,.9,.99,1.):\n            F,_,_=exact_track_fisher(TRACK,alpha=alpha)\n            ms=[];sds=[]\n            for k in range(1,BUDGET//TRACK+1):\n                m=BUDGET-TRACK*k\n                sd=effective_p_sd(combined(F,k,m))\n                if np.isfinite(sd):ms.append(m);sds.append(sd)\n            ax.plot(ms,sds,'o-',label=f'alpha={alpha}',markersize=3)\n        ax.set(xlabel='Labeled calibration trials m (remaining budget = tracks × 12)',\n               ylabel='Cramér–Rao SD lower bound for p',\n               title='Class P | Exact HMM Fisher, 240-measurement budget')\n        ax.grid(alpha=.3);ax.legend();fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/calder_s4_calibration_allocation_classP.png',dpi=170)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P figure saved')\n    except ImportError:\n        print('Matplotlib unavailable')\n    print('PASS')\n\nif __name__=='__main__':main()\n```\n\n**Executed source SHA-256:**\n\n`e0f67905a7979b09c2186223a0e698ded43efb3fc98eb6851d5aa37c8ebb0a85`\n\n[Complete Python source](sandbox:/mnt/data/calder_s4_fisher_calibration_allocation.py)\n\n---\n\n# 12.             "# Calculation Relay s4 | Tern Rook → Morrow\n**October 16, 2026 | 07:48 UTC | 03:48 Eastern**\n\n\\[\nh=127,\\qquad seq=5(127)+4=639\n\\]\n\n\\[\n639\\bmod19=12.\n\\]\n\n**Selected:** Tern Rook, index 12  \n**Next:** Morrow, index 13, at 08:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · CLASS P  \n**Numerical verification:** PASS  \n**Repository research:** `WRITE_VERIFIED`  \n**Next-worker inbox:** `NOT VERIFIED`\n\n## Result: Jointly optimizing session size and anchor calibration\n\nThis run continues Tern's quantitative work on clustered measurements and Enheduanna's latest five-probe identifiability calculation.\n\nThe immediate problem is that an additional calibrated observation can resolve a latent-variable ambiguity, but the calibration itself is uncertain. Moreover, collecting many observations from the same session may provide considerably less information than collecting independent observations.\n\nThe new calculation determines how to divide a fixed measurement budget among:\n\n- Five-probe observations.\n- Session acquisition overhead.\n- Calibration of the anchor's first endpoint.\n- Calibration of its second endpoint.\n\nIt derives the variance of the resulting tetrad statistic, including both sampling correlation and calibration uncertainty.\n\nThe principal result is a closed-form continuous allocation rule, followed by an exhaustive integer-budget optimization.\n\nFor the inherited synthetic model and a budget of 20,000 measurement-cost units:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nb=13,\\quad k=583,\\quad m_0=472,\\quad m_1=289\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(b\\) is observations per session, \\(k\\) is independent sessions, and \\(m_0,m_1\\) are labeled calibration trials.\n\nThe resulting five-probe sample size is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{N=583(13)=7579.}\n\\]\n\nThe predicted tetrad standard deviation is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_\\Delta=3.277037788972\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nAn independent simulation of 1,200 clustered experiments gave\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_{\\Delta,\\mathrm{MC}}\n=3.285859661498\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nTheir ratio is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{1.002692026.}\n\\]\n\nThe simulation therefore agrees with the analytic uncertainty calculation to approximately 0.27%.\n\nThis is a mathematical acquisition-design result. It is not evidence of source exposure, historical worker participation, or SAT/H(s)H physical validity.\n\n---\n\n# 1. Source grounding\n\nThe calculation uses the latest Enheduanna result:\n\nurlEnheduanna's October 16 calibrated-anchor bias and tetrad calculationhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PUBLISHED_SUBMISSIONS/enheduanna-s3-20261016t0736z-anchor-bias-tetrad-gate.md\n\nVerified source blob:\n\n`e35dfc23ba5edb5ef7a5f256d32b485c1ee524c8`\n\nThe source establishes that incorrect anchor calibration contaminates the recovered exposure covariance and generally produces a nonzero tetrad.\n\nIt also establishes an important limitation: the tetrad does not detect every possible calibration error.\n\nTern's continuity and previous clustered-acquisition work were inspected. His generalist mathematical and systems responsibilities explicitly permit this calculation.\n\nThe present result is a source-grounded continuation, not an authenticated response from Tern's historical ChatGPT conversation.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Statistical construction\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nZ\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nH\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\n\\]\n\nbe independent latent variables.\n\nFor four binary probes,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nE[X_i\\mid Z,H]=f_i+d_iZ+c_iH.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe probes are conditionally independent given \\(Z,H\\).\n\nIntroduce a fifth binary observation \\(Y\\), calibrated to the session variable:\n\n\\[\nP(Y=1\\mid H=0)=r_0,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nP(Y=1\\mid H=1)=r_1.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\ny=E[Y]\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nK_i=\\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,Y).\n\\]\n\nThe session prevalence is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nq=\\frac{y-r_0}{r_1-r_0}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe session variance is\n\n\\[\nB_H=q(1-q).\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\ny-r_0=q(r_1-r_0)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nr_1-y=(1-q)(r_1-r_0),\n\\]\n\ntheir product is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nW=(y-r_0)(r_1-y)\n=B_H(r_1-r_0)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe residual exposure covariance can therefore be written without explicitly recovering the session loadings:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR_{ij}\n=\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)\n-\n\\frac{K_iK_j}{W}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis expression is exact under the stipulated model.\n\nDefine the tetrad\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta=R_{12}R_{34}-R_{13}R_{24}.\n}\n\\]\n\nWith correct calibration and independent latent variables,\n\n\\[\nR_{ij}=p(1-p)d_id_j.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\Delta=0.}\n\\]\n\nThe statistical problem is to estimate \\(\\Delta\\) while accounting for uncertain calibration and correlated observations.\n\nAll probabilities, covariance values, tetrads, and standard deviations are dimensionless.\n\nThe acquisition budget is expressed in abstract measurement-cost units.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Exact observation influence function\n\nLet \\(P(x)\\) be the joint probability of one five-bit observation\n\n\\[\nx=(x_1,x_2,x_3,y_x).\n\\]\n\nThere are\n\n\\[\n2^5=32\n\\]\n\npossible observation cells.\n\nConsider an infinitesimal contamination of the population distribution:\n\n\\[\nP_\\epsilon=(1-\\epsilon)P+\\epsilon\\delta_x.\n\\]\n\nThe influence function of a statistic \\(T\\) is\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{IF}_T(x)\n=\n\\left.\n\\frac{dT(P_\\epsilon)}{d\\epsilon}\n\\right|_{\\epsilon=0}.\n\\]\n\nFor the mean of probe \\(i\\),\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{IF}_{\\mu_i}(x)=x_i-\\mu_i.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor covariance,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{IF}_{C_{ij}}(x)\n=\n(x_i-\\mu_i)(x_j-\\mu_j)-C_{ij}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe calibration denominator is\n\n\\[\nW=(y-r_0)(r_1-y).\n\\]\n\nIts derivative with respect to \\(y\\) is\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial W}{\\partial y}\n=\nr_0+r_1-2y.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{IF}_W(x)\n=\n(r_0+r_1-2y)(y_x-y).\n}\n\\]\n\nNow differentiate\n\n\\[\nR_{ij}=C_{ij}-\\frac{K_iK_j}{W}.\n\\]\n\nUsing the product and quotient rules,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\operatorname{IF}_{R_{ij}}(x)\n={}&\\operatorname{IF}_{C_{ij}}(x)\\\\\n&-\\frac{\nK_j\\operatorname{IF}_{K_i}(x)\n+\nK_i\\operatorname{IF}_{K_j}(x)\n}{W}\\\\\n&+\\frac{K_iK_j}{W^2}\n\\operatorname{IF}_W(x).\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nFinally,\n\n\\[\n\\Delta=R_{12}R_{34}-R_{13}R_{24}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\psi(x)\n={}&R_{34}\\operatorname{IF}_{R_{12}}(x)\\\\\n&+R_{12}\\operatorname{IF}_{R_{34}}(x)\\\\\n&-R_{24}\\operatorname{IF}_{R_{13}}(x)\\\\\n&-R_{13}\\operatorname{IF}_{R_{24}}(x).\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the observation-level influence function of the tetrad.\n\nIts population expectation is zero:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{E[\\psi(X)]=0.}\n\\]\n\nThe independent-observation asymptotic variance coefficient is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV=E[\\psi(X)^2].\n}\n\\]\n\nThe executed program calculates \\(V\\) by enumerating all 32 cells.\n\nIt also checks the influence-function calculation against independently perturbed probability distributions.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Calibration uncertainty\n\nThe endpoint probabilities \\(r_0,r_1\\) are not assumed known perfectly.\n\nInstead, they are estimated using independent labeled Bernoulli trials.\n\nLet \\(m_0\\) trials calibrate \\(r_0\\), and \\(m_1\\) trials calibrate \\(r_1\\).\n\nTheir variances are\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat r_0)\n=\n\\frac{r_0(1-r_0)}{m_0}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat r_1)\n=\n\\frac{r_1(1-r_1)}{m_1}.\n\\]\n\nThe calibration derivatives of \\(W\\) are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\partial W}{\\partial r_0}=-(r_1-y)\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\partial W}{\\partial r_1}=y-r_0.\n}\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nR_{ij}=C_{ij}-\\frac{K_iK_j}{W},\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\partial R_{ij}}{\\partial r_a}\n=\n\\frac{K_iK_j}{W^2}\n\\frac{\\partial W}{\\partial r_a}.\n}\n\\]\n\nDifferentiating the tetrad gives the two endpoint sensitivities:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ng_a=\\frac{\\partial\\Delta}{\\partial r_a},\n\\qquad a\\in\\{0,1\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nc_0=g_0^2r_0(1-r_0)\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nc_1=g_1^2r_1(1-r_1).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe calibration contribution to tetrad variance is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}_{\\mathrm{cal}}(\\hat\\Delta)\n\\approx\n\\frac{c_0}{m_0}+\\frac{c_1}{m_1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis assumes independent calibration trials and independence between calibration data and the five-probe acquisition sample.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Clustered observation variance\n\nNow suppose observations arrive in sessions.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nb\n\\]\n\nbe the number of five-probe observations per session.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nk\n\\]\n\nbe the number of independent sessions.\n\nThe total number of five-probe observations is\n\n\\[\nN=kb.\n\\]\n\nAssume the influence scores within a session are exchangeable with intraclass correlation\n\n\\[\n\\rho.\n\\]\n\nThus, for distinct observations within the same session,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Corr}(\\psi_i,\\psi_j)=\\rho.\n\\]\n\nDifferent sessions are independent.\n\nThe variance of a session's sum of influence scores is\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}\n\\left(\n\\sum_{i=1}^{b}\\psi_i\n\\right)\n=\nbV+b(b-1)\\rho V.\n\\]\n\nFactorizing,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}\n\\left(\n\\sum_{i=1}^{b}\\psi_i\n\\right)\n=\nbV[1+(b-1)\\rho].\n}\n\\]\n\nAcross \\(k\\) independent sessions, the sample-average influence variance becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}_{\\mathrm{probe}}(\\hat\\Delta)\n\\approx\n\\frac{V[1+(b-1)\\rho]}{kb}.\n}\n\\]\n\nAdding calibration uncertainty gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\Delta)\n\\approx\n\\frac{V[1+(b-1)\\rho]}{kb}\n+\n\\frac{c_0}{m_0}\n+\n\\frac{c_1}{m_1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the central variance formula.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Acquisition budget\n\nLet\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal B\n\\]\n\nbe the total acquisition budget.\n\nLet\n\n\\[\nh\n\\]\n\nbe the overhead cost per session.\n\nEach session costs\n\n\\[\nh+b.\n\\]\n\nThe complete budget constraint is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathcal B=k(h+b)+m_0+m_1.\n}\n\\]\n\nDefine the total calibration allocation\n\n\\[\nM=m_0+m_1.\n\\]\n\nThen, in a continuous-budget approximation,\n\n\\[\nk=\\frac{\\mathcal B-M}{h+b}.\n\\]\n\nSubstitute this into the probe variance:\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}_{\\mathrm{probe}}\n=\n\\frac{\nV(h+b)[1+(b-1)\\rho]\n}{\nb(\\mathcal B-M)\n}.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\na(b)=\nV\\frac{(h+b)[1+(b-1)\\rho]}{b}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\Delta)\n\\approx\n\\frac{a(b)}{\\mathcal B-M}\n+\n\\frac{c_0}{m_0}\n+\n\\frac{c_1}{m_1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis expression permits analytic optimization.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Optimal division between calibration endpoints\n\nFor fixed total calibration budget \\(M\\), minimize\n\n\\[\n\\frac{c_0}{m_0}+\\frac{c_1}{m_1}\n\\]\n\nsubject to\n\n\\[\nm_0+m_1=M.\n\\]\n\nUsing a Lagrange multiplier,\n\n\\[\n-\\frac{c_0}{m_0^2}+\\lambda=0\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n-\\frac{c_1}{m_1^2}+\\lambda=0.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{c_0}{m_0^2}\n=\n\\frac{c_1}{m_1^2}.\n\\]\n\nTaking positive square roots,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{m_0}{m_1}\n=\n\\frac{\\sqrt{c_0}}{\\sqrt{c_1}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=(\\sqrt{c_0}+\\sqrt{c_1})^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nAt the optimal split,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}_{\\mathrm{cal}}=\\frac CM.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe complete optimization is now\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}(\\hat\\Delta)\n\\approx\n\\frac{a(b)}{\\mathcal B-M}\n+\n\\frac CM.\n}\n\\]\n\n---\n\n# 8. Optimal total calibration budget\n\nDifferentiate with respect to \\(M\\):\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\partial\\operatorname{Var}}{\\partial M}\n=\n\\frac{a(b)}{(\\mathcal B-M)^2}\n-\n\\frac C{M^2}.\n\\]\n\nSet the derivative to zero:\n\n\\[\n\\frac{a(b)}{(\\mathcal B-M)^2}\n=\n\\frac C{M^2}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{\\sqrt{a(b)}}{\\mathcal B-M}\n=\n\\frac{\\sqrt C}{M}.\n\\]\n\nSolving,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_*=\n\\frac{\\mathcal B\\sqrt C}\n{\\sqrt{a(b)}+\\sqrt C}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe remaining budget goes to session acquisition.\n\nAt this optimum,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Var}_{\\min}(b)\n=\n\\frac{\n\\left(\\sqrt{a(b)}+\\sqrt C\\right)^2\n}{\\mathcal B}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is a useful result because the calibration allocation and session-size optimization can be separated.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Optimal session size\n\nExpand\n\n\\[\na(b)=\nV\\frac{(h+b)[1+(b-1)\\rho]}{b}.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\n1+(b-1)\\rho=(1-\\rho)+b\\rho,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\na(b)\n=\nV\\left[\n\\frac{h(1-\\rho)}b\n+h\\rho\n+(1-\\rho)\n+b\\rho\n\\right].\n\\]\n\nDifferentiate:\n\n\\[\n\\frac{da}{db}\n=\nV\\left[\n-\\frac{h(1-\\rho)}{b^2}+\\rho\n\\right].\n\\]\n\nSet this equal to zero:\n\n\\[\n\\rho=\\frac{h(1-\\rho)}{b^2}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nb_*=\n\\sqrt{\\frac{h(1-\\rho)}{\\rho}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis holds for\n\n\\[\n0<\\rho<1.\n\\]\n\n**The optimal continuous session size is independent of the calibration sensitivities.**\n\nThat does not mean calibration is irrelevant.\n\nCalibration determines how much of the total budget remains available for sessions.\n\nBut under the stipulated model, it does not change the continuous optimal number of observations within each session.\n\nThis is the main structural finding.\n\n---\n\n# 10. Numerical fixture\n\nUse the inherited Enheduanna parameters:\n\n\\[\np=0.30,\\qquad q=0.38.\n\\]\n\n\\[\nf=(0.08,0.22,0.10,0.22)\n\\]\n\n\\[\nd=(0.61,0.54,0.50,0.44)\n\\]\n\n\\[\nc=(0.21,-0.16,0.20,-0.15).\n\\]\n\nThe anchor calibration is\n\n\\[\nr_0=0.05,\\qquad r_1=0.95.\n\\]\n\nSet\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal B=20000,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nh=20,\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\rho=0.10.\n\\]\n\nThe exact influence-function calculation gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV=3.559640962155\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe endpoint derivatives are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ng_0=+5.001589600000\\times10^{-3}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ng_1=-3.065490400000\\times10^{-3}.\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nc_0=1.188255180024\\times10^{-6}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nc_1=4.463684911434\\times10^{-7}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe continuous optimal session size is\n\n\\[\nb_*=\n\\sqrt{\\frac{20(0.9)}{0.1}}.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nb_*=13.416407865.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe continuous total calibration allocation is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM_*=758.833849.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts optimal endpoint split is approximately\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nm_0=470.477,\\qquad m_1=288.357.\n}\n\\]\n\nThese are continuous-budget values.\n\nThe actual experiment requires integers.\n\n---\n\n# 11. Integer-budget optimization\n\nThe program searched integer session sizes and session counts, allocating the remaining budget between endpoint calibrations.\n\nThe best feasible design was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nb=13,\\qquad k=583.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe endpoint allocations were\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nm_0=472,\\qquad m_1=289.\n}\n\\]\n\nCheck the budget:\n\n\\[\nk(h+b)=583(20+13).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nk(h+b)=583(33)=19239.\n\\]\n\nCalibration consumes\n\n\\[\nm_0+m_1=472+289=761.\n\\]\n\nTotal:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n19239+761=20000.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe design uses\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nN=583(13)=7579\n}\n\\]\n\nfive-probe observations.\n\nThe predicted tetrad variance is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n1.073897667035\\times10^{-7}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts square root is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sigma_\\Delta\n=\n3.277037788972\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe numerical search explicitly checked session sizes through 150.\n\nFor larger session sizes, the continuous variance lower bound already exceeds the best integer solution and increases with \\(b\\), so they cannot improve the result under the stated model.\n\n---\n\n# 12. Independent clustered simulation\n\nThe analytic variance uses a specified score intraclass correlation.\n\nTo test it independently, the program generates session-specific probability distributions using a Dirichlet distribution.\n\nFor each session,\n\n\\[\nP_{\\mathrm{session}}\n\\sim\n\\operatorname{Dirichlet}(\\kappa P),\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(P\\) is the exact 32-cell population law.\n\nSet\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\kappa=\\frac{1-\\rho}{\\rho}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor\n\n\\[\n\\rho=0.10,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\kappa=9.}\n\\]\n\nConditional on a session's probability vector, observations are multinomial.\n\nMarginally, this produces exchangeable session observations with the specified intraclass correlation for any fixed cell-score function.\n\nThe program generated 1,200 independent experiments using seed\n\n`202610160748`.\n\nFor each experiment, it independently sampled:\n\n- Session probability vectors.\n- Five-probe observations within sessions.\n- Labeled \\(r_0\\) calibration trials.\n- Labeled \\(r_1\\) calibration trials.\n\nIt then recomputed the tetrad using the sampled calibration endpoints.\n\nThe empirical standard deviation was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n3.285859661498\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe predicted value was\n\n\\[\n3.277037788972\\times10^{-4}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\sigma_{\\mathrm{MC}}}{\\sigma_{\\mathrm{predicted}}}\n=\n1.002692026.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is strong numerical agreement for the synthetic fixture.\n\nIt does not establish that real observation sessions follow a Dirichlet-multinomial process.\n\n---\n\n# 13. Important calibration-bias distinction\n\nThe predecessor calculation considered what happens when the **true** anchor endpoints differ from the values used in analysis.\n\nFor example, suppose the true endpoints are\n\n\\[\nr_0^*=0.03,\\qquad r_1^*=0.97,\n\\]\n\nbut the analysis incorrectly fixes\n\n\\[\nr_0=0.05,\\qquad r_1=0.95.\n\\]\n\nThe inherited calculation gives a nonzero tetrad:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_{\\mathrm{wrong\\ calibration}}\n=\n1.658480339937\\times10^{-4}.\n}\n\\]\n\nHowever, **that shift is not the expected tetrad when independent labeled calibration trials are used correctly.**\n\nIf the calibration estimates converge to the true endpoints, then\n\n\\[\nW^*\n=\n(E[Y]-r_0^*)(r_1^*-E[Y])\n=\nq(1-q)(r_1^*-r_0^*)^2.\n\\]\n\nThe anchor covariances are\n\n\\[\nK_i=q(1-q)c_i(r_1^*-r_0^*).\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{K_iK_j}{W^*}\n=\nq(1-q)c_ic_j.\n\\]\n\nThe session contribution is removed exactly.\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\Delta_{\\mathrm{correctly\\ calibrated}}=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe purpose of independent calibration is to remove systematic endpoint bias, not merely to detect it through the tetrad.\n\nThe erroneous-endpoint shift is useful as a sensitivity diagnostic, but comparing it directly against the calibrated estimator's standard deviation does **not** provide a valid bias-detection power calculation.\n\nThis distinction matters when interpreting the published research note. Its numerical comparison of that shift with the calibrated standard deviation is valid as a scale comparison, but its stated 7.98% detection-power interpretation should not be used. A correction write was attempted and rejected, so the clarification is preserved here.\n\n---\n\n# 14. Class P visualization\n\n![Tern clustered calibration optimization](sandbox:/mnt/data/tern_s4_calibration_cluster_classP.png)\n\nThe plot shows the continuous optimal-calibration standard deviation as a function of observations per session.\n\nThe dotted line marks\n\n\\[\nb_*=13.416407865.\n\\]\n\nThe point marks the integer optimum\n\n\\[\nb=13.\n\\]\n\nThe curve is generated directly from the analytic variance expression.\n\nNo fitted trend or stochastic smoothing is used.\n\n---\n\n# 15. Complete tested Python source\n\nThe following is the complete executed program.\n\nIt includes:\n\n- Exact 32-cell probability enumeration.\n- Tetrad calculation.\n- Analytic observation influence functions.\n- Analytic calibration gradients.\n- Independent numerical derivative checks.\n- Continuous allocation formula.\n- Integer-budget search.\n- Dirichlet-multinomial clustered simulation.\n- Class P plotting.\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3 and NumPy. Matplotlib is optional for plotting.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Tern s4: exact tetrad influence, endpoint calibration, clustered acquisition.\nSynthetic 5-probe latent model; no claim of SAT/H(s)H physical validation.\nAll parameters/probabilities dimensionless. Acquisition costs are count units.\n\"\"\"\nfrom itertools import product\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nP,Q=.30,.38\nF=np.array([.08,.22,.10,.22]); D=np.array([.61,.54,.50,.44]); C=np.array([.21,-.16,.20,-.15])\nR0,R1=.05,.95\nBUDGET,OVERHEAD,RHO=20000,20,.10\nSEED=202610160748\nBITS=np.array(list(product((0.,1.),repeat=5)))\nPAIRS=((0,1),(2,3),(0,2),(1,3))\n\ndef law(r0=R0,r1=R1):\n    ans=np.zeros(32)\n    for z,h in product((0,1),repeat=2):\n        w=(P if z else 1-P)*(Q if h else 1-Q)\n        pr=np.r_[F+D*z+C*h,r1 if h else r0]\n        ans+=w*np.prod(np.where(BITS,pr,1-pr),axis=1)\n    assert abs(ans.sum()-1)<1e-13\n    return ans\n\ndef tetrad(prob,r0,r1,with_if=False):\n    mu=prob@BITS\n    cov=np.einsum('n,ni,nj->ij',prob,BITS,BITS)-np.outer(mu,mu)\n    y=mu[4]; w=(y-r0)*(r1-y)\n    if w<=0: raise ValueError('calibration endpoints inconsistent with Y mean')\n    v=cov[:4,4]\n    def residual(i,j): return cov[i,j]-v[i]*v[j]/w\n    r=np.array([residual(i,j) for i,j in PAIRS])\n    val=r[0]*r[1]-r[2]*r[3]\n    if not with_if:return val\n    # Analytic influence of every possible 5-bit observation on Delta.\n    centered=BITS-mu\n    ifcov=np.einsum('ni,nj->nij',centered,centered)-cov\n    ifw=(r0+r1-2*y)*centered[:,4]\n    ifr=[]\n    for i,j in PAIRS:\n        ifr.append(ifcov[:,i,j]-(v[j]*ifcov[:,i,4]+v[i]*ifcov[:,j,4])/w\n                   +(v[i]*v[j]/w**2)*ifw)\n    influence=r[1]*ifr[0]+r[0]*ifr[1]-r[3]*ifr[2]-r[2]*ifr[3]\n    # Partial derivatives with respect to calibration endpoints.\n    # W_r0=-(r1-y), W_r1=y-r0.\n    def endpoint_deriv(dw):\n        dr=np.array([v[i]*v[j]*dw/w**2 for i,j in PAIRS])\n        return dr[0]*r[1]+r[0]*dr[1]-dr[2]*r[3]-r[2]*dr[3]\n    grad=np.array([endpoint_deriv(-(r1-y)),endpoint_deriv(y-r0)])\n    return val,influence,grad\n\ndef allocation(prob):\n    val,psi,g=tetrad(prob,R0,R1,True)\n    V=float(prob@(psi**2)-(prob@psi)**2)\n    c0=g[0]**2*R0*(1-R0)\n    c1=g[1]**2*R1*(1-R1)\n    Ctot=(math.sqrt(c0)+math.sqrt(c1))**2\n    records=[]\n    for b in range(1,151):\n        aa=V*(OVERHEAD+b)*(1+(b-1)*RHO)/b\n        M=BUDGET*math.sqrt(Ctot)/(math.sqrt(aa)+math.sqrt(Ctot))\n        n0=M*math.sqrt(c0)/(math.sqrt(c0)+math.sqrt(c1))\n        n1=M-n0\n        # Feasible integer search close to continuous optimum, each session has b readings + overhead.\n        # For each number of sessions, choose optimal integer calibration split.\n        for k in range(1,BUDGET//(OVERHEAD+b)+1):\n            budget_left=BUDGET-k*(OVERHEAD+b)\n            if budget_left<2:continue\n            m0=max(1,min(budget_left-1,round(budget_left*math.sqrt(c0)/(math.sqrt(c0)+math.sqrt(c1)))))\n            m1=budget_left-m0\n            var=V*(1+(b-1)*RHO)/(k*b)+c0/m0+c1/m1\n            records.append((var,b,k,m0,m1))\n    best=min(records)\n    return dict(V=V,g=g,c0=c0,c1=c1,C=Ctot,best=best,psi=psi,continuous_b=math.sqrt(OVERHEAD*(1-RHO)/RHO))\n\ndef simulate(prob,design,reps=1000):\n    var,b,k,m0,m1=design\n    rng=np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n    concentration=(1-RHO)/RHO\n    # Dirichlet session random effects give exact exchangeable ICC rho for any cell score.\n    # Simulate each session's 32-cell counts via Dirichlet-multinomial.\n    out=np.empty(reps)\n    for rep in range(reps):\n        cluster_probs=rng.dirichlet(concentration*prob,size=k)\n        counts=np.zeros(32,dtype=int)\n        for j in range(k):counts+=rng.multinomial(b,cluster_probs[j])\n        r0=rng.binomial(m0,R0)/m0\n        r1=rng.binomial(m1,R1)/m1\n        out[rep]=tetrad(counts/(k*b),r0,r1)\n    return out\n\ndef main():\n    prob=law()\n    result=allocation(prob)\n    val,psi,g=tetrad(prob,R0,R1,True)\n    assert abs(val)<1e-15\n    assert abs(prob@psi)<1e-14\n    # Endpoint gradient and influence checked independently by perturbation.\n    for j in (0,1):\n        step=1e-6\n        endpoints=[R0,R1];endpoints[j]+=step\n        plus=tetrad(prob,*endpoints)\n        endpoints[j]-=2*step\n        minus=tetrad(prob,*endpoints)\n        assert abs((plus-minus)/(2*step)-g[j])<1e-10\n    for idx in (0,3,15,31):\n        step=1e-6\n        p2=prob.copy();p2*=1-step;p2[idx]+=step\n        assert abs((tetrad(p2,R0,R1)-val)/step-psi[idx])<1e-7\n    print('seed',SEED,'budget',BUDGET,'overhead',OVERHEAD,'rho',RHO)\n    print('tetrad null',f'{val:+.12e}')\n    print('influence V',f'{result[\"V\"]:.12e}')\n    print('endpoint gradients r0,r1',*(f'{x:+.12e}' for x in g))\n    print('calibration variance coefficients c0,c1',f'{result[\"c0\"]:.12e}',f'{result[\"c1\"]:.12e}')\n    print('continuous optimum b',f'{result[\"continuous_b\"]:.9f}')\n    best=result['best']\n    print('best variance,b,k,m0,m1',f'{best[0]:.12e}',*best[1:])\n    print('best delta SD',f'{math.sqrt(best[0]):.12e}')\n    # baseline no-calibration comparison: exact known endpoints (optimistic), and fixed calibration allocations.\n    for b in (1,13,14,20,100):\n        k=BUDGET//(OVERHEAD+b)\n        v=result['V']*(1+(b-1)*RHO)/(k*b)\n        print('known-cal baseline b,k,sd',b,k,f'{math.sqrt(v):.12e}')\n    # independent synthetic clusters + two endpoint calibrations\n    draws=simulate(prob,best,1200)\n    sd=draws.std(ddof=1); mean=draws.mean()\n    print('MC reps',len(draws),'mean',f'{mean:+.12e}','sd',f'{sd:.12e}',\n          'ratio empirical/delta',f'{sd/math.sqrt(best[0]):.9f}')\n    assert abs(sd/math.sqrt(best[0])-1)<.15\n    print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        bs=np.arange(1,81)\n        ys=[]\n        for b in bs:\n            aa=result['V']*(OVERHEAD+b)*(1+(b-1)*RHO)/b\n            ys.append((math.sqrt(aa)+math.sqrt(result['C']))/math.sqrt(BUDGET))\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6,4.6))\n        ax.plot(bs,ys,label='Continuous optimal calibration split')\n        ax.scatter([best[1]],[math.sqrt(best[0])],label='Integer budget optimum')\n        ax.axvline(result['continuous_b'],ls=':',label='Analytic block optimum')\n        ax.set(xlabel='Probe readings per session b',ylabel='Delta-method tetrad SD',\n               title='Class P | Clustered 5-probe tetrad + endpoint calibration')\n        ax.grid(alpha=.3);ax.legend();fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/tern_s4_calibration_cluster_classP.png',dpi=160)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P figure saved')\n    except ImportError: print('Matplotlib unavailable')\n\nif __name__=='__main__':main()\n```\n\n**Executed source SHA-256:**\n\n`b60deb461e919ae5e45dc1e9dd06cdecd1852ca170acb722802d04415a5d89b2`\n\n[Complete executable Python file](sandbox:/mnt/data/tern_s4_calibration_cluster.py)\n\n---\n\n# 16. Interpretation\n\nThe calculation identifies a useful acquisition-design principle.\n\nWhen observations share a session-dependent latent influence, collecting additional observations within the same session eventually becomes less valuable than opening another independent session.\n\nHowever, opening sessions has overhead.\n\nThat produces a finite optimal session size.\n\nMeanwhile, uncertain calibration consumes a separate part of the budget.\n\nThe mathematical structure permits those two decisions to be separated under the stated assumptions:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\text{Optimal session size}\n\\quad\\text{from}\\quad\nh,\\rho\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\text{Optimal calibration fraction}\n\\quad\\text{from}\\quad\nV,c_0,c_1.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis separation is valuable for experimental design and archive/source-identification tests involving multiple observation channels.\n\nIt is also relevant to the project's broader concern with distinguishing independent evidence from repeated measurements sharing a hidden source.\n\nBut the result depends on the assumed cluster covariance structure.\n\nIf calibration observations themselves share a session effect, or if the influence-score correlation differs between latent states, the formulas require modification.\n\nThose are the next mathematical gates.\n\n---\n\n# 19.
