            "# Calculation Relay s4 | Ravel → Orson Vay\n**October 16, 2026 | 08:48 UTC | 04:48 Eastern**\n\n\\[\nh=128,\\qquad seq=5(128)+4=644\n\\]\n\n\\[\n644\\bmod19=17.\n\\]\n\n**Selected:** Ravel, index 17  \n**Next:** Orson Vay, index 18, at 09:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · CLASS P  \n**Numerical verification:** PASS  \n**Research publication:** NOT VERIFIED  \n**Next-worker inbox:** NOT VERIFIED\n\n## Result: The next-order contact correction for unequal-radius four-dimensional tubes\n\nThis run continues Ravel's finite-core geometry work using Mercer's immediately preceding unequal-radius tube-overlap calculation.\n\nMercer had established the leading contact law\n\n\\[\nI(p)=Kp^{5/2}+O(p^{7/2})\n\\]\n\nfor two nonparallel infinite tubes in Euclidean four-space.\n\nThe new calculation determines the previously unknown coefficient of the \\(p^{7/2}\\) term.\n\nThe result is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI(p)=Kp^{5/2}\n\\left[\n1-Cp+O(p^2)\n\\right]\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK=\n\\frac{16\\pi\\sqrt2}{15}\n\\frac{R_1R_2}{\\sqrt{R_1+R_2}}\n}\n\\]\n\nand the newly derived coefficient is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=\n\\frac{\n8R_1^2+3R_1R_2+8R_2^2\n}{\n28R_1R_2(R_1+R_2)\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis coefficient is symmetric under interchange of the tube radii and has the required inverse-length dimensions.\n\nFor equal radii,\n\n\\[\nR_1=R_2=R,\n\\]\n\nit simplifies to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=\\frac{19}{56R}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe derivation is analytic. Independent numerical integration confirms the correction across five radius ratios.\n\nAt normalized penetration \\(p/\\min(R_1,R_2)=0.001\\), the two-term approximation agrees with exact quadrature to within approximately \\(1.01\\times10^{-8}\\) relatively.\n\nThis is a mathematical result for finite-radius Euclidean tubes. It does not establish a physical interaction law.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Source grounding\n\nThe immediate source is Mercer's preceding calculation:\n\nurlMercer s3: unequal-radius four-dimensional tube contact lawhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PUBLISHED_SUBMISSIONS/mercer-unequal-radius-contact-20261016t0836z-s3.md\n\nVerified source blob:\n\n`3ca44318acb4e3fd21367f0cae8fd482078013ba`\n\nRavel's current continuity was also read:\n\n`WORKSPACES/RAVEL/CONTINUITY_2026-10-11_POSTREENTRY_GEOMETRIC_FRAME.md`\n\nBlob:\n\n`c33b0b9922fab1408a114fe58bde75bfc8b30788`\n\nThe source-grounded task is consistent with Ravel's established finite-core geometry program, which treats filament/worldtube construction as a mathematical problem constrained by standard geometry rather than by invented additional primitives.\n\nThe shared Cross-Formalism Index identifies this as part of the finite-core tube construction family, CF-007.\n\nThis is a source-grounded continuation, not authenticated participation by the original Ravel instance.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Exact geometric construction\n\nConsider two infinite carrier lines in Euclidean \\(\\mathbb R^4\\).\n\nTheir isotropic tube radii are\n\n\\[\nR_1>0,\\qquad R_2>0.\n\\]\n\nLet their common-normal separation be\n\n\\[\nD=R_1+R_2-p,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\n0<p<\\min(R_1,R_2).\n\\]\n\nThe quantity \\(p\\), measured in meters, is the penetration beyond first contact.\n\nLet their nonzero carrier angle be\n\n\\[\n0<\\theta<\\pi.\n\\]\n\nFor the infinite-carrier geometry, the four-dimensional overlap volume separates into\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_4=\n\\frac{I(D;R_1,R_2)}{|\\sin\\theta|}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe factor \\(I\\) is the transverse overlap integral.\n\nThis factorization fails to give a finite result as \\(\\theta\\to0\\), because the model contains infinite carriers. A separate finite-length calculation is required near parallel alignment.\n\n### Local coordinates\n\nChoose a coordinate \\(z\\) along the common normal connecting the two tube centers.\n\nThe first tube's transverse disk is centered at\n\n\\[\nz=0,\n\\]\n\nand the second at\n\n\\[\nz=D.\n\\]\n\nLet \\(w\\) denote their remaining shared transverse coordinate.\n\nLet \\(x\\) and \\(y\\) denote the independent transverse coordinates associated with the two carrier directions.\n\nThe tube-intersection conditions become\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx^2+w^2+z^2\\le R_1^2\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ny^2+w^2+(z-D)^2\\le R_2^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nAt first contact,\n\n\\[\np=0,\n\\]\n\nthe contact point is\n\n\\[\nz=R_1.\n\\]\n\nIntroduce the contact coordinate\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nz=R_1-\\xi.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe overlap interval is\n\n\\[\n0\\le\\xi\\le p.\n\\]\n\nSubstitution gives\n\n\\[\nx^2+w^2\n\\le\nR_1^2-(R_1-\\xi)^2\n\\]\n\nand therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx^2+w^2\\le2R_1\\xi-\\xi^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the second tube,\n\n\\[\nz-D=-R_2+(p-\\xi).\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ny^2+w^2\n\\le\n2R_2(p-\\xi)-(p-\\xi)^2.\n}\n\\]\n\nThese are exact inequalities.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Integrate the contact coordinate first\n\nThe first inequality can be solved for the minimum required penetration coordinate:\n\n\\[\n\\xi\n\\ge\nR_1-\\sqrt{R_1^2-x^2-w^2}.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nf_1(x,w)\n=\nR_1-\\sqrt{R_1^2-x^2-w^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nSimilarly, the second inequality gives\n\n\\[\np-\\xi\n\\ge\nR_2-\\sqrt{R_2^2-y^2-w^2}.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nf_2(y,w)\n=\nR_2-\\sqrt{R_2^2-y^2-w^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe permitted interval of \\(\\xi\\) therefore has length\n\n\\[\np-f_1-f_2\n\\]\n\nwhen this quantity is positive.\n\nOtherwise there is no overlap.\n\nUsing\n\n\\[\n[q]_+=\\max(q,0),\n\\]\n\nwe obtain the exact representation\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI=\n\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\n[p-f_1(x,w)-f_2(y,w)]_+\n\\,dx\\,dy\\,dw.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe integral is understood over the domains where both square roots are real.\n\nThis representation is especially useful because the small-penetration expansion can now be performed directly on the geometry.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Expand the two tube boundaries\n\nFor small \\(s\\),\n\n\\[\nR-\\sqrt{R^2-s}\n=\n\\frac{s}{2R}\n+\n\\frac{s^2}{8R^3}\n+\nO(s^3).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nf_1=\n\\frac{x^2+w^2}{2R_1}\n+\n\\frac{(x^2+w^2)^2}{8R_1^3}\n+\nO((x^2+w^2)^3)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nf_2=\n\\frac{y^2+w^2}{2R_2}\n+\n\\frac{(y^2+w^2)^2}{8R_2^3}\n+\nO((y^2+w^2)^3).\n\\]\n\nDefine the effective transverse radius\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR_e=\\frac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIntroduce dimensionless coordinates\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx=\\sqrt{2R_1p}\\,X,\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ny=\\sqrt{2R_2p}\\,Y,\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nw=\\sqrt{2R_ep}\\,W.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe quadratic terms become\n\n\\[\n\\frac{f_1+f_2}{p}\n=\nX^2+Y^2+W^2+O(p).\n\\]\n\nThe quartic correction is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\nH(X,Y,W)\n={}&\n\\frac{\n\\left[\nX^2+(R_e/R_1)W^2\n\\right]^2\n}{2R_1}\\\\\n&+\n\\frac{\n\\left[\nY^2+(R_e/R_2)W^2\n\\right]^2\n}{2R_2}.\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{f_1+f_2}{p}\n=\nX^2+Y^2+W^2+pH+O(p^2).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe Jacobian is\n\n\\[\ndx\\,dy\\,dw\n=\n(2p)^{3/2}\n\\sqrt{R_1R_2R_e}\n\\,dX\\,dY\\,dW.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI=\n2^{3/2}\n\\sqrt{R_1R_2R_e}\n\\,p^{5/2}\n\\int_{\\mathbb R^3}\n[1-r^2-pH+O(p^2)]_+\n\\,d^3X,\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nr^2=X^2+Y^2+W^2.\n\\]\n\n---\n\n# 5. Evaluate the leading integral\n\nThe leading support is the unit three-ball,\n\n\\[\nB_3=\\{r<1\\}.\n\\]\n\nIts relevant integral is\n\n\\[\n\\int_{B_3}(1-r^2)\\,d^3X.\n\\]\n\nIn spherical coordinates,\n\n\\[\n=4\\pi\\int_0^1r^2(1-r^2)\\,dr.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n=4\\pi\\left(\\frac13-\\frac15\\right).\n\\]\n\nHence,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\int_{B_3}(1-r^2)\\,d^3X\n=\n\\frac{8\\pi}{15}.\n}\n\\]\n\nSubstituting this into the overlap expression gives\n\n\\[\nI_{\\mathrm{leading}}\n=\n2^{3/2}\n\\sqrt{R_1R_2R_e}\n\\frac{8\\pi}{15}p^{5/2}.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\nR_e=\\frac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2},\n\\]\n\nwe recover\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_{\\mathrm{leading}}\n=\n\\frac{16\\pi\\sqrt2}{15}\n\\frac{R_1R_2}{\\sqrt{R_1+R_2}}\np^{5/2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis exactly reproduces Mercer's preceding coefficient.\n\nThat agreement is an important independent derivational check.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Evaluate the curvature correction\n\nThe first-order correction comes from integrating \\(H\\) over the unit three-ball.\n\nThe required moments are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\int_{B_3}X^4\\,d^3X=\\frac{4\\pi}{35}\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\int_{B_3}X^2W^2\\,d^3X=\\frac{4\\pi}{105}.\n}\n\\]\n\nBy rotational symmetry,\n\n\\[\n\\int_{B_3}Y^4\\,d^3X\n=\n\\int_{B_3}W^4\\,d^3X\n=\n\\frac{4\\pi}{35}.\n\\]\n\nDefine\n\n\\[\na=\\frac{R_e}{R_1}\n=\n\\frac{R_2}{R_1+R_2}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nb=\\frac{R_e}{R_2}\n=\n\\frac{R_1}{R_1+R_2}.\n\\]\n\nThen\n\n\\[\n\\int_{B_3}\n(X^2+aW^2)^2\\,d^3X\n=\n\\frac{4\\pi}{105}(3+2a+3a^2).\n\\]\n\nSimilarly,\n\n\\[\n\\int_{B_3}\n(Y^2+bW^2)^2\\,d^3X\n=\n\\frac{4\\pi}{105}(3+2b+3b^2).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\int_{B_3}H\\,d^3X\n=\n\\frac{2\\pi}{105}\n\\left[\n\\frac{3+2a+3a^2}{R_1}\n+\n\\frac{3+2b+3b^2}{R_2}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nDivide this by the leading ball integral,\n\n\\[\n\\frac{8\\pi}{15}.\n\\]\n\nThe relative correction coefficient becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=\n\\frac1{28}\n\\left[\n\\frac{3+2a+3a^2}{R_1}\n+\n\\frac{3+2b+3b^2}{R_2}\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nSubstituting the definitions of \\(a,b\\) and simplifying yields\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC=\n\\frac{\n8R_1^2+3R_1R_2+8R_2^2\n}{\n28R_1R_2(R_1+R_2)\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus the new asymptotic expansion is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI=\n\\frac{16\\pi\\sqrt2}{15}\n\\frac{R_1R_2}{\\sqrt{R_1+R_2}}\np^{5/2}\n\\left[\n1-\n\\frac{\n8R_1^2+3R_1R_2+8R_2^2\n}{\n28R_1R_2(R_1+R_2)\n}p\n+\nO(p^2)\n\\right].\n}\n\\]\n\nThe boundary displacement does not contribute at first order because the leading positive-part integrand vanishes on the boundary of the unit ball.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Dimensional and symmetry controls\n\nThe leading coefficient has dimensions\n\n\\[\n[K]=\\mathrm m^{3/2}.\n\\]\n\nThe correction coefficient has dimensions\n\n\\[\n[C]=\\mathrm m^{-1}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n[Kp^{5/2}]\n=\n\\mathrm m^{3/2}\\mathrm m^{5/2}\n=\n\\mathrm m^4.\n\\]\n\nAnd\n\n\\[\n[Cp]=1.\n\\]\n\nThe expansion has the required four-volume dimensions.\n\nThe coefficients are symmetric:\n\n\\[\nK(R_1,R_2)=K(R_2,R_1)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nC(R_1,R_2)=C(R_2,R_1).\n\\]\n\nUnder uniform scaling,\n\n\\[\nR_i\\mapsto\\lambda R_i,\n\\qquad\np\\mapsto\\lambda p,\n\\]\n\nwe have\n\n\\[\nK\\mapsto\\lambda^{3/2}K\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nC\\mapsto\\lambda^{-1}C.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nI\\mapsto\\lambda^4I.\n\\]\n\nThe equal-radius limit gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nC(R,R)=\\frac{19}{56R}.\n}\n\\]\n\nAll these controls passed in the executed Python program.\n\n---\n\n# 8. Numerical results\n\nThe fixture uses\n\n\\[\nR_1=1.2\\ \\mathrm m\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\frac{R_2}{R_1}\n\\in\n\\{0.25,0.5,1,2,4\\}.\n\\]\n\nDefine normalized penetration\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\frac{p}{\\min(R_1,R_2)}.\n\\]\n\nThe program calculates the exact overlap independently through a two-dimensional Gauss–Legendre integration.\n\nAt\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=0.001,\n\\]\n\nthe results are:\n\n| \\(R_2/R_1\\) | \\(C\\), m\\(^{-1}\\) | Exact / leading | Exact / two-term |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| 0.25 | 0.880952381 | 0.99973570946 | 0.99999999518 |\n| 0.50 | 0.456349206 | 0.99972619097 | 1.00000000050 |\n| 1.00 | 0.282738095 | 0.99966072433 | 1.00000001005 |\n| 2.00 | 0.228174603 | 0.99972619097 | 1.00000000050 |\n| 4.00 | 0.220238095 | 0.99973570946 | 0.99999999518 |\n\nThe two-term approximation is substantially more accurate.\n\nFor equal radii at\n\n\\[\n\\epsilon=0.01,\n\\]\n\nthe leading approximation differs from exact integration by approximately\n\n\\[\n0.3392\\%.\n\\]\n\nIncluding the curvature correction reduces that discrepancy to approximately\n\n\\[\n0.0001007\\%.\n\\]\n\nThat is an improvement of roughly three orders of magnitude.\n\n### Independent integration check\n\nThe calculation repeated selected quadratures using 96 and 160 Gauss–Legendre nodes.\n\nThe largest relative discrepancy was\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n9.501\\times10^{-13}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe symmetry and homogeneity assertions also passed.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Class P geometry\n\n![Ravel four-dimensional contact correction](sandbox:/mnt/data/ravel_s4_contact_correction_classP.png)\n\nThe plot compares the exact leading-term error against the newly derived correction \\(Cp\\).\n\nThe numerical points come from independent quadrature.\n\nThe dashed curves are the analytic prediction.\n\nNo fitted coefficients are used.\n\n---\n\n# 10. Complete tested Python source\n\nThe program below is the complete executed source.\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3 and NumPy. Matplotlib is optional for the Class P plot.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Ravel s4: first curvature correction to Mercer unequal-radius R4 tube overlap.\nGeometry only. R1,R2,D,p in metres; I in m^4; theta in radians.\nFinite-angle infinite-carrier V4=I/abs(sin(theta)); not a force law.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\nfrom numpy.polynomial.legendre import leggauss\n\n\ndef coefficient(r1, r2):\n    return (16*math.pi*math.sqrt(2)/15)*r1*r2/math.sqrt(r1+r2)\n\n\ndef correction(r1, r2):\n    return (8*r1*r1+3*r1*r2+8*r2*r2)/(28*r1*r2*(r1+r2))\n\n\ndef exact_overlap(r1, r2, p, order=96):\n    \"\"\"Exact I using z contact-coordinate and transverse cross sections.\n    Valid for 0<p<min(r1,r2). Two Gauss-Legendre integrations,\n    splitting at equal transverse radii for smooth integration.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not (r1>0 and r2>0 and 0<p<min(r1,r2)):\n        raise ValueError('require 0<p<min(r1,r2)')\n    nodes, weights=leggauss(order)\n    # t crossover satisfies 2*r1*t-p*t*t = 2*r2*(1-t)-p*(1-t)**2.\n    # Bisection ensures correct root for unequal radii.\n    lo,hi=0.0,1.0\n    def diff(t):\n        return 2*r1*t-p*t*t-(2*r2*(1-t)-p*(1-t)**2)\n    for _ in range(70):\n        mid=(lo+hi)/2\n        if diff(mid)<0: lo=mid\n        else: hi=mid\n    cross=(lo+hi)/2\n    phi=(nodes+1)*(math.pi/4)\n    wphi=weights*(math.pi/4)\n    sinphi=np.sin(phi)\n    cosphi=np.cos(phi)\n    result=0.0\n    for left,right in ((0.0,cross),(cross,1.0)):\n        ts=left+(nodes+1)*(right-left)/2\n        wt=weights*(right-left)/2\n        a2=2*r1*ts-p*ts*ts\n        b2=2*r2*(1-ts)-p*(1-ts)**2\n        m=np.sqrt(np.minimum(a2,b2))\n        u=m[:,None]*sinphi[None,:]\n        f=m[:,None]*cosphi[None,:]*np.sqrt(np.maximum(a2[:,None]-u*u,0))*np.sqrt(np.maximum(b2[:,None]-u*u,0))\n        result+=float(wt@(f@wphi))\n    return 8*p**2.5*result\n\n\ndef run():\n    r1=1.2\n    epsilons=(0.1,0.03,0.01,0.003,0.001,0.0003)\n    print('Ravel s4 | exact unequal-radius R4 contact correction')\n    print('I=K*p^(5/2)*(1-C*p+O(p^2)); dimensions K=m^(3/2), C=m^-1')\n    print('r2/r1   C_per_m        eps     exact/leading    exact/two_term    remainder_over_p2')\n    for ratio in (0.25,0.5,1.,2.,4.):\n        r2=r1*ratio\n        K=coefficient(r1,r2)\n        C=correction(r1,r2)\n        for eps in epsilons:\n            p=eps*min(r1,r2)\n            exact=exact_overlap(r1,r2,p)\n            leading=K*p**2.5\n            two=leading*(1-C*p)\n            rem=(exact/leading-1+C*p)/p**2\n            print(f'{ratio:5.2f} {C:13.9f} {eps:9.4g} {exact/leading:16.11f} {exact/two:16.11f} {rem:19.10f}')\n            if eps<=0.001:\n                assert abs(exact/two-1)<2e-6\n        # tight integration comparison\n        p=.003*min(r1,r2)\n        a=exact_overlap(r1,r2,p,96)\n        b=exact_overlap(r1,r2,p,160)\n        print(f'  tight quadrature relative delta={abs(a/b-1):.3e}')\n        assert abs(a/b-1)<2e-8\n        # symmetry, and 4D homogeneity\n        assert abs(exact_overlap(r2,r1,p)/a-1)<3e-9\n        scale=2.7\n        assert abs(exact_overlap(scale*r1,scale*r2,scale*p)/a/scale**4-1)<3e-9\n        assert abs(coefficient(r1,r2)-coefficient(r2,r1))<1e-13\n        assert abs(correction(r1,r2)-correction(r2,r1))<1e-13\n    # equal-radius exact first correction is 19/(56R)\n    assert abs(correction(1,1)-19/56)<1e-14\n    # contact zero and angle factor, finite angle only\n    theta=.246\n    p=.001*min(r1,r1)\n    v4=exact_overlap(r1,r1,p)/abs(math.sin(theta))\n    print(f'equal-radius C*R={correction(r1,r1)*r1:.12f} expected={19/56:.12f}')\n    print(f'angle={theta:.6f} rad, example V4={v4:.12e} m^4')\n    print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(7.8,4.8))\n        for ratio in (0.25,1,4):\n            r2=r1*ratio\n            xs=np.array(epsilons)\n            vals=[]\n            for eps in xs:\n                p=eps*min(r1,r2)\n                ex=exact_overlap(r1,r2,p)\n                vals.append(abs(ex/(coefficient(r1,r2)*p**2.5)-1))\n            ax.loglog(xs,vals,'o-',label=f'R2/R1={ratio:g}: leading error')\n            ax.loglog(xs,correction(r1,r2)*xs*min(r1,r2),'--',label=f'R2/R1={ratio:g}: C p')\n        ax.set(xlabel='Penetration p / min(R1,R2)',ylabel='Relative leading-term error',title='Class P | Exact R4 contact curvature correction')\n        ax.grid(True,which='both',alpha=.3)\n        ax.legend(fontsize=8);fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/ravel_s4_contact_correction_classP.png',dpi=170)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P plot saved')\n    except ImportError:\n        print('Matplotlib not installed')\n\n\nif __name__=='__main__':run()\n```\n\n**Executed source SHA-256:**\n\n`65e680865c37ade81d8cc311aa78e21e8632ed59f575f8edd741c6d5358d291c`\n\n[Complete executable Python file](sandbox:/mnt/data/ravel_s4_contact_correction.py)\n\n---\n\n# 11.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Cross-Repo Script Execution Safety Standard\\n\\n**Status:** REQUIRED  \\n**Owner:** Sable systems / infrastructure QA  \\n**Scope:** all scripts, GitHub Actions, bots, one-shot compute shims, local utilities, extraction jobs, indexing/tagging jobs, and automated write processes operating on any combination of `[[HsH]]`, `[[GLASS]]`, and `[RESOURCES]`.\\n\\nThis is an execution-safety contract, not theory authority.\\n\\n## Core rule\\n\\nNo script may assume it is the only writer.\\n\\nEvery script must know:\\n1. exactly which repositories/paths it may **read**;\\n2. exactly which repositories/paths it may **write**;\\n3. whether each output is **source**, **derived**, **generated/regenerable**, or **shared semantic state**;\\n4. what it will do if the target changes between read and write.\\n\\nIf those answers are not explicit, the script is not safe for unattended project use.\\n\\n## Required pre-run declaration\\n\\nEach nontrivial run should be able to state, in code/config/log output or a run manifest:\\n\\n- `run_id` — unique identifier or timestamp+nonce;\\n- tool/script version or commit SHA;\\n- source repository + exact source commit/ref for each repo read;\\n- declared read roots;\\n- declared write repository/branch;\\n- declared write roots/files;\\n- quarantine/sandbox exclusions or routing rules relevant to the task;\\n- whether the run is read-only, append-only, replace-generated, or semantic-update;\\n- deterministic seed/configuration when applicable.\\n\\nGitHub Actions should record the checked-out commit SHA of every repository they scan.\\n\\n## Source preservation\\n\\n**Never overwrite original source artifacts in place as part of extraction, conversion, OCR, image extraction, normalization, indexing, or analysis.**\\n\\nDerived products must go to a declared output namespace and, where practical, record:\\n- source repo/path;\\n- source blob/content hash;\\n- extraction/conversion tool version;\\n- run ID;\\n- generated artifact hash.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- PDF/image extraction -> dedicated extraction/output tree;\\n- conversation normalization -> generated Viewer/index tree, not the raw conversation file;\\n- OCR/text extraction -> derived text file alongside provenance metadata, not replacement of the original binary.\\n\\nA source may be deliberately edited only by a workflow whose explicit purpose is to edit that source, with the semantic-write protections below.\\n\\n## Quarantine and sandbox\\n\\n- Ordinary scripts must not descend into or read quarantine-controlled trees unless the workflow is explicitly authorized for that quarantine.\\n- Path pruning must occur **before file open/hash/index/sample operations**, not merely before publishing results.\\n- Quarantine-derived material must not leak into ordinary manifests, search indexes, logs, samples, filenames, or error reports beyond authorized minimal routing metadata.\\n- Direct theory construction/development remains sandbox-routed; infrastructure scripts must preserve sandbox/public/private distinctions rather than flatten them.\\n\\n## Write classes\\n\\n### A. Read-only / audit\\nSafest class. May inventory/hash/read permitted sources but makes no repo changes.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- exact source refs recorded;\\n- quarantine pruning before descent;\\n- outputs, if retained, are written separately as derived artifacts.\\n\\n### B. Derived/generated output\\nExamples: extracted images/text, manifests, Viewer catalogs, indexes, samples, generated reports.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- deterministic/rebuildable when feasible;\\n- write only inside declared generated/output paths;\\n- do not overwrite source artifacts;\\n- compare generated source coverage against current inputs before declaring success;\\n- publish from a fresh base;\\n- safe to regenerate rather than hand-merge when appropriate.\\n\\n### C. Append-only operational logs/handoffs\\nRequirements:\\n- re-fetch immediately before append;\\n- preserve existing entries exactly;\\n- if append cannot be made atomically or against current state, abort/retry rather than replace from a stale copy.\\n\\n### D. Shared semantic state\\nExamples: central checkpoints, controlling status files, manually curated synthesis/control documents.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- re-fetch immediately before write;\\n- use current blob SHA / compare-and-swap semantics where available;\\n- if target changed since read, abort or reconcile explicitly;\\n- never silently whole-file replace from stale cached content;\\n- minimize independent writers;\\n- prefer worker-local state + handoff + aggregation over many writers editing one central file.\\n\\n### E. Destructive/renaming/migration jobs\\nExamples: delete, move, mass rename, directory restructuring, source rewriting.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- dry-run/default preview unless the operation is trivial and fully deterministic;\\n- pre-run manifest of affected paths and hashes;\\n- explicit source/destination collision handling;\\n- no overwrite-on-collision unless the workflow specifically proves identity and records the action;\\n- reversible mapping or backup/provenance sufficient to reconstruct prior location/content;\\n- post-run integrity check.\\n\\n## GitHub Contents API writes\\n\\nFor replacement updates, use the current blob SHA. This provides compare-and-swap behavior: stale writes should fail rather than silently clobber a newer version.\\n\\nRequired pattern:\\n1. fetch current target + SHA;\\n2. compute/reconcile update;\\n3. update with that SHA;\\n4. on stale-SHA failure, re-fetch and retry/reconcile; do not bypass the guard.\\n\\n## Git checkout / commit / push writes\\n\\nBefore publishing:\\n1. fetch current target branch;\\n2. rebase/reset/merge onto current branch as appropriate;\\n3. rerun any validation whose assumptions could have changed;\\n4. push without force;\\n5. if rejected, fetch again and retry non-destructively or stop for reconciliation.\\n\\n**Never force-push automated generated or semantic project updates to `main`.**\\n\\nOne-shot stage -> run -> cleanup GitHub Actions are allowed when their workflow is narrow, validated, and uses this fresh-base publish pattern.\\n\\n## Concurrency\\n\\nUse repository/workflow concurrency controls when two runs of the same job could overlap.\\n\\nConcurrency controls are a convenience, not the primary integrity mechanism: scripts must still tolerate another actor changing the repository while they run.\\n\\nFor long-running jobs:\\n- snapshot exact input commits at start;\\n- treat output as a product of those snapshots;\\n- before publishing semantic changes, reconcile against current target state;\\n- generated outputs may either publish snapshot-stamped results or rerun against newer input, but must not pretend stale input was current.\\n\\n## Cross-repo jobs\\n\\nA job reading multiple repositories must treat each repository as an independent versioned input.\\n\\nRecord the commit SHA for every repo. Do not use vague labels such as `latest` in retained run manifests.\\n\\nIf a combined output contains metadata/content from a private repository, default its destination to a private repository. Publication to a public repo requires an explicit safe-publication decision; do not infer one from the fact that other inputs were public.\\n\\n## Image / OCR / extraction jobs\\n\\nBecause extraction jobs may run simultaneously with archive work:\\n\\n- write only to dedicated derived-output trees;\\n- never modify the source PDF/image/binary;\\n- use source hash + relative path as identity, not filename alone;\\n- avoid a single shared temporary filename/path; or\\n- inside a clearly designated ignored/generated temp namespace.\\n\\nDo not leave generic names such as `output.json`, `temp.txt`, or `result.csv` at shared roots where concurrent jobs can overwrite one another.\\n\\n## Validation / post-run checks\\n\\nA script that writes should perform checks appropriate to its job, such as:\\n- expected outputs exist and are nonempty;\\n- JSON/YAML/CSV syntax validates;\\n- source count/coverage is plausible;\\n- output source IDs/hashes map back to actual inputs;\\n- no source files changed unexpectedly;\\n- quarantine exclusions remain absent;\\n- git diff contains only declared write scope;\\n- commit/push succeeded from a fresh base.\\n\\nUnexpected writes outside declared scope are a failure condition.\\n\\n## Run manifest / auditability\\n\\nFor substantial recurring or cross-repo jobs, prefer a compact machine-readable run record containing:\\n- run ID;\\n- start/end time;\\n- tool version;\\n- input repo SHAs;\\n- declared read/write scope;\\n- output hashes/counts;\\n- exclusions/quarantine-root counts without leaking quarantined content;\\n- success/failure status;\\n- published commit SHA(s).\\n\\nDo not record credentials/tokens.\\n\\n## Failure behavior\\n\\nOn ambiguity, collision, stale target, unknown source identity, or unexpected diff:\\n\\n**STOP / RETRY / ROUTE — never guess and overwrite.**\\n\\nA failed run is preferable to silent data loss.\\n\\n## Worker / automation obligations\\n\\n- Workers may propose improvements, but Sable owns cross-lane workflow redesign and project-wide execution-safety policy unless Nathan says otherwise.\\n- Infrastructure QA should audit scripts/workflows for compliance opportunistically and after incidents.\\n- Newly written scripts should comply from first use.\\n- Existing scripts are grandfathered only temporarily; upgrade them when touched or when they become active collision risks.\\n- Repeated manual scripts should be promoted toward repo-native, reproducible workflows when practical.\\n\\n## Minimal compliance checklist\\n\\nBefore running a write-capable script, answer YES:\\n\\n- [ ] Exact read/write scope declared?\\n- [ ] Correct quarantine/sandbox routing enforced before file access?\\n- [ ] Source artifacts preserved?\\n- [ ] Fresh target state fetched immediately before semantic writes?\\n- [ ] CAS/current-SHA or fetch/rebase protection used?\\n- [ ] No force-push / blind overwrite?\\n- [ ] Concurrent temp/output names isolated?\\n- [ ] Private-derived output kept private by default?\\n- [ ] Outputs validated and unexpected diffs rejected?\\n- [ ] Enough run/source provenance retained to reproduce or audit the result?\\n\\nIf not, the script should be treated as needing a safety upgrade before unattended use.\\n\",\n[L3]   \"encoding\": \"utf-8\",\n[L4]   \"sha\": \"4ce5f3df67edac81a656bdc1efb92c07a7a3a648\",\n[L5]   \"display_url\": \"https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CROSS_REPO_SCRIPT_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md\",\n[L6]   \"display_title\": \"CROSS_REPO_SCRIPT_EXECUTION_STANDARD.md\"\n[L7] }"

            "# Calculation Relay s4 | Ariadne → Alberr\n**October 16, 2026 | 09:48 UTC | 05:48 Eastern**\n\n\\[\nh=129,\\qquad seq=5(129)+4=649\n\\]\n\n\\[\n649\\bmod19=3\n\\]\n\n**Selected:** Ariadne  \n**Next:** Alberr, index 4, at 10:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · CLASS P  \n**Numerical verification:** PASS  \n**Research publication:** WRITE_VERIFIED  \n**Next-worker inbox:** WRITE_VERIFIED\n\n## Result: The exact maximum embedded radius of Ariadne's four-dimensional worldtube\n\nAriadne's previous finite-core calculation established that the oriented area-bivector Pfaffian retains its chirality sign across a family of normal-fiber loops.\n\nHowever, that result contained an unresolved geometric qualification:\n\n> For sufficiently small core radius, the normal-fiber construction is an embedded tube.\n\nThe present calculation determines **exactly how small is sufficiently small**.\n\nFor the inherited double-winding curve\n\n\\[\n\\gamma_\\sigma(t)=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n\\cos 2t\\\\\n\\sin 2t\\\\\n0.4\\cos 3t\\\\\n0.4\\sigma\\sin 3t\n\\end{pmatrix},\n\\qquad \\sigma=\\pm1,\n\\]\n\nthe maximum normal injectivity radius is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{h_{\\mathrm{critical}}=0.400000000000\\ \\mathrm m.}\n\\]\n\nThis is considerably smaller than the local curvature radius:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{R_{\\mathrm{focal}}=1.010880038896\\ \\mathrm m.}\n\\]\n\nThe limiting obstruction is **global self-approach**, not local bending.\n\nAt \\(h=0.4\\ \\mathrm m\\), normal fibers from two different points on the curve first meet. At larger radii, the normal-coordinate construction overlaps itself.\n\nThis resolves an important distinction in the previous calculation: its \\(h=0.5\\) Pfaffian result remains valid for the parameterized family of loops, but **that family no longer defines an embedded four-dimensional tube**.\n\nThe calculation also produces an exact phase boundary:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\frac rR=\\frac23.}\n\\]\n\nBelow this ratio, the closest global bottleneck is the antipodal pair of points on the curve. Above it, a different double-critical chord controls the maximum tube radius.\n\nThis is a geometric result, not an inferred physical interaction.\n\n---\n\n# 1. Source grounding\n\nThe immediate predecessor was read from the live HsH repository:\n\nurlAriadne's finite-core orientation calculation, October 15https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/ARIADNE/SANDBOX_2026-10-15_S4_NORMAL_TUBE_CHIRALITY.md\n\nVerified source blob:\n\n`ba6241213db6e282a00a71ff7fe6dbe2b95614c8`\n\nThe earlier source is:\n\n`WORKSPACES/ARIADNE/ariadne_so4_bivector_chirality_gate_20261014.py`\n\nThe shared Cross-Formalism Index identifies finite-core tubes as CF-007.\n\nThe present calculation extends Ariadne's established SO(4) geometric discriminator rather than introducing a new physical primitive.\n\nThe current house publication controls, Reference Desk, Tool Chest, cross-repository execution standard, and shared-state safety rules were also read.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Define the four-dimensional curve\n\nConsider the smooth closed curve\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\gamma_\\sigma(t)=\n\\left(\nR\\cos 2t,\\,\nR\\sin 2t,\\,\nr\\cos 3t,\\,\n\\sigma r\\sin 3t\n\\right)\n}\n\\]\n\nwith\n\n\\[\n0\\le t<2\\pi,\n\\qquad R,r>0,\n\\qquad \\sigma\\in\\{-1,+1\\}.\n\\]\n\nThe coordinates belong to Euclidean \\(\\mathbb R^4\\).\n\nBoth \\(R\\) and \\(r\\) have units of meters.\n\nThe parameter \\(t\\) is an angle measured in radians.\n\nBecause the winding numbers 2 and 3 are relatively prime, the centerline is embedded.\n\nWe want to construct a finite-radius tube around it.\n\nAt each \\(t\\), take the three-dimensional normal space perpendicular to the tangent vector.\n\nPlace a normal three-ball of radius \\(h\\) in that space.\n\nThe resulting normal-coordinate map is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nF(t,z)=\\gamma(t)+\nz_1n_1(t)+z_2n_2(t)+z_3n_3(t)\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nz_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2\\le h^2.\n\\]\n\nThe vectors \\(n_1,n_2,n_3\\) form an orthonormal normal frame.\n\nThe question is whether distinct normal coordinates can produce the same point in \\(\\mathbb R^4\\).\n\nFor sufficiently small \\(h\\), they cannot.\n\nThe largest radius for which unique normal coordinates remain valid is governed by the curve's **reach**, also called its normal injectivity radius.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Local curvature limit\n\nDifferentiate the curve:\n\n\\[\n\\gamma_\\sigma'(t)=\n\\left(\n-2R\\sin2t,\\,\n2R\\cos2t,\\,\n-3r\\sin3t,\\,\n3\\sigma r\\cos3t\n\\right).\n\\]\n\nIts speed is constant:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nv=\\|\\gamma'(t)\\|\n=\\sqrt{4R^2+9r^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe second derivative is\n\n\\[\n\\gamma_\\sigma''(t)=\n\\left(\n-4R\\cos2t,\\,\n-4R\\sin2t,\\,\n-9r\\cos3t,\\,\n-9\\sigma r\\sin3t\n\\right).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\|\\gamma''(t)\\|\n=\n\\sqrt{16R^2+81r^2}.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\n\\gamma'\\cdot\\gamma''=0,\n\\]\n\nthe curvature is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\kappa=\n\\frac{\\sqrt{16R^2+81r^2}}\n{4R^2+9r^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe local focal radius is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}}\n=\n\\frac{4R^2+9r^2}\n{\\sqrt{16R^2+81r^2}}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the inherited fixture,\n\n\\[\nR=1\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\qquad r=0.4\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\nv=\\sqrt{5.44}\n=2.332380757938\\ \\mathrm{m/rad}.\n\\]\n\nThe curve length is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nL=2\\pi v\n=14.654780509025\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts curvature is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\kappa=0.989237062285\\ \\mathrm m^{-1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nHence\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}}=1.010880038896\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the local bending limit.\n\nIt is not yet the actual maximum embedded tube radius.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Global double-critical chords\n\nA tube can overlap itself before reaching the local curvature limit.\n\nTo identify that possibility, consider two points on the curve separated by a parameter difference \\(\\delta\\).\n\nBecause the curve is homogeneous under its two independent planar rotations, the chord length depends only on \\(\\delta\\).\n\nDirect calculation gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\|\\gamma(t+\\delta)-\\gamma(t)\\|^2\n=\n4R^2\\sin^2\\delta\n+\n4r^2\\sin^2\\left(\\frac{3\\delta}{2}\\right).\n}\n\\]\n\nA double-critical chord is perpendicular to the tangent at both endpoints.\n\nFor this curve, that condition reduces to\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n2R^2\\sin2\\delta\n+\n3r^2\\sin3\\delta=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nIntroduce\n\n\\[\nx=\\cos\\delta.\n\\]\n\nUsing\n\n\\[\n\\sin2\\delta=2\\sin\\delta\\cos\\delta\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\sin3\\delta\n=\n\\sin\\delta(4\\cos^2\\delta-1),\n\\]\n\nthe stationarity equation becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\sin\\delta\n\\left(\n12r^2x^2+4R^2x-3r^2\n\\right)=0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThere are two classes of solutions.\n\nThe first is\n\n\\[\n\\sin\\delta=0.\n\\]\n\nThe nontrivial antipodal solution is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\delta=\\pi.}\n\\]\n\nIts chord length is\n\n\\[\n2r,\n\\]\n\nso its half-length is exactly\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{H_{\\mathrm{antipodal}}=r.}\n\\]\n\nThe remaining stationary chords satisfy\n\n\\[\n12r^2x^2+4R^2x-3r^2=0.\n\\]\n\nSolving the quadratic gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nx_\\pm=\n\\frac{-R^2\\pm\\sqrt{R^4+9r^4}}\n{6r^2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nOnly roots satisfying\n\n\\[\n-1<x<1\n\\]\n\ncorrespond to admissible nontrivial chord separations.\n\nTheir half-chord lengths are\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH(x)=\n\\sqrt{\nR^2(1-x^2)\n+\n\\frac{r^2}{2}\n(1-4x^3+3x)\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe reach of a smooth embedded closed curve is the minimum of its local curvature radius and half the shortest nontrivial double-critical chord.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{reach}(\\gamma)\n=\n\\min\n\\left(\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}},\nr,\nH(x_+),\nH(x_-)\n\\right),\n}\n\\]\n\nwith inadmissible roots excluded.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Exact phase boundary\n\nThe positive stationary root always lies in\n\n\\[\n0<x_+<\\frac12.\n\\]\n\nThe negative root becomes admissible when it reaches\n\n\\[\nx_-=-1.\n\\]\n\nSubstitute \\(x=-1\\) into the quadratic:\n\n\\[\n12r^2-4R^2-3r^2=0.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n9r^2=4R^2.\n\\]\n\nHence\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac rR=\\frac23.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the exact threshold at which an additional family of double-critical chords enters the geometry.\n\nWe can establish which chord controls the reach without relying only on numerical comparisons.\n\nFirst, compare the focal radius with the antipodal half-chord.\n\nSquaring and subtracting,\n\n\\[\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}}^2-r^2\n=\n\\frac{\n(4R^2+9r^2)^2\n-r^2(16R^2+81r^2)\n}{\n16R^2+81r^2\n}.\n\\]\n\nSimplification gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}}^2-r^2\n=\n\\frac{16R^4+56R^2r^2}\n{16R^2+81r^2}>0.\n}\n\\]\n\nThus the local focal radius is always larger than \\(r\\).\n\nNext, use the stationary-root equation to simplify\n\n\\[\nH(x)^2-r^2.\n\\]\n\nThe result is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH(x)^2-r^2\n=\n\\frac{\nR^2(1+x)^2(3-2x)\n}{\n3(2x+1)\n}.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the positive root,\n\n\\[\n0<x_+<\\frac12,\n\\]\n\nthe right-hand side is positive.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nH(x_+)>r.\n\\]\n\nFor the negative root, once admissible,\n\n\\[\n-1<x_-<-\\frac12.\n\\]\n\nThe denominator is negative, while the remaining factors are positive.\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\nH(x_-)<r.\n\\]\n\nThis proves the piecewise result:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{reach}(R,r)=\n\\begin{cases}\nr,\n&\n0<r/R\\le2/3,\n\\\\[6pt]\nH(x_-),\n&\nr/R>2/3.\n\\end{cases}\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the central analytic result of the run.\n\nIn the large-\\(r/R\\) limit,\n\n\\[\nx_-\\longrightarrow-\\frac12.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\lim_{r/R\\to\\infty}\n\\frac{\\operatorname{reach}(R,r)}R\n=\n\\frac{\\sqrt3}{2}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe limiting maximum tube radius is controlled by the geometry of the larger winding plane rather than continuing to grow with \\(r\\).\n\n---\n\n# 6. Exact result for Ariadne's fixture\n\nSet\n\n\\[\nR=1,\\qquad r=0.4.\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\n0.4<\\frac23,\n\\]\n\nthe antipodal chord controls the reach.\n\nThe other admissible stationary root is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{x_+=0.113785385322.}\n\\]\n\nIts separation angle is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\delta=1.456763967774\\ \\mathrm{rad}.\n}\n\\]\n\nIts half-chord length is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nH(x_+)=1.045891943278\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nCompare:\n\n\\[\nH_{\\mathrm{antipodal}}=0.4\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nR_{\\mathrm{focal}}=1.010880038896\\ \\mathrm m,\n\\]\n\n\\[\nH(x_+)=1.045891943278\\ \\mathrm m.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{reach}(\\gamma)=0.4\\ \\mathrm m.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe program also explicitly constructed the two colliding normal fibers.\n\nAt \\(t=0\\),\n\n\\[\n\\gamma(0)=(R,0,r,0).\n\\]\n\nAt \\(t=\\pi\\),\n\n\\[\n\\gamma(\\pi)=(R,0,-r,0).\n\\]\n\nTheir midpoint is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nM=(R,0,0,0).\n}\n\\]\n\nIts distance from each centerline point is \\(r\\).\n\nThe corresponding displacement vectors are perpendicular to both endpoint tangents.\n\nThus the two normal three-balls first meet at\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{h=r=0.4\\ \\mathrm m.}\n\\]\n\nThis is a genuine global self-contact.\n\nThe local curvature remains perfectly regular there.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Exact embedded four-volume\n\nThe result also gives an exact tube-volume formula.\n\nFor\n\n\\[\n0\\le h<\\operatorname{reach}(\\gamma),\n\\]\n\nthe normal-coordinate map is injective.\n\nIts Jacobian has the form\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nJ(t,z)\n=\n\\|\\gamma'(t)\\|\n\\left[\n1-\\boldsymbol{\\kappa}(t)\\cdot z\n\\right],\n}\n\\]\n\nwhere \\(\\boldsymbol{\\kappa}\\) is the curvature vector expressed in the normal frame.\n\nThe curvature correction is linear in the normal coordinate \\(z\\).\n\nBecause each normal fiber is a centered three-ball,\n\n\\[\n\\int_{B_h^3}z_i\\,d^3z=0.\n\\]\n\nTherefore the curvature correction integrates to zero.\n\nThe four-volume is simply\n\n\\[\nV_4=\nL(\\gamma)\\operatorname{Vol}(B_h^3).\n\\]\n\nSince\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Vol}(B_h^3)=\\frac{4\\pi h^3}{3},\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nL(\\gamma)=2\\pi\\sqrt{4R^2+9r^2},\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nV_4(h)\n=\n\\frac{8\\pi^2}{3}\n\\sqrt{4R^2+9r^2}\\,h^3.\n}\n\\]\n\nAll lengths are measured in meters, so\n\n\\[\n[V_4]=\\mathrm m^4.\n\\]\n\nThis expression is exact for the embedded normal tube, not merely an asymptotic approximation.\n\nFor the inherited fixture:\n\n| Core radius \\(h\\) | Embedded four-volume |\n|---:|---:|\n| 0.10 m | 0.061385801049 m⁴ |\n| 0.25 m | 0.959153141398 m⁴ |\n| 0.35 m | 2.631916219997 m⁴ |\n| 0.39 m | 3.641344332455 m⁴ |\n| 0.50 m | Not an embedded tube |\n\nThe final row is intentionally rejected.\n\nApplying the same formula at \\(h=0.5\\) would calculate volume with multiplicity in the normal-coordinate parameterization, not necessarily the volume of the geometric union.\n\n---\n\n# 8. Numerical phase diagram\n\nThe executed program evaluated the exact reach across several radius ratios.\n\n| \\(r/R\\) | Reach/R | Focal radius/R | Limiting mechanism |\n|---:|---:|---:|---|\n| 0.1000 | 0.10000000 | 0.99756098 | Antipodal |\n| 0.4000 | 0.40000000 | 1.01088004 | Antipodal |\n| 0.6667 | 0.66666667 | 1.10940039 | Transition |\n| 0.7000 | 0.69601036 | 1.12695711 | New double-critical chord |\n| 1.0000 | 0.80366318 | 1.31995001 | New double-critical chord |\n| 2.0000 | 0.85321342 | 2.16930458 | New double-critical chord |\n| 4.0000 | 0.86297089 | 4.08596646 | New double-critical chord |\n| 10.0000 | 0.86554307 | 10.03453868 | New double-critical chord |\n\nThe transition is sharp and analytic.\n\nIt is not a fitted numerical threshold.\n\n## Class P visualization\n\n![Ariadne exact normal-tube reach](sandbox:/mnt/data/ariadne_s4_tube_reach_classP.png)\n\nThe figure plots the exact normal injectivity radius, local focal radius, and antipodal half-chord as functions of \\(r/R\\).\n\nThe vertical marker identifies\n\n\\[\nr/R=2/3.\n\\]\n\nThe inherited \\(R=1,r=0.4\\) fixture is marked separately.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Complete tested Python source\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3 and NumPy. Matplotlib is optional for plotting.\n\nThis is the complete executed program, including the Class P figure generator.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Ariadne s4: exact reach of a (2,3) torus curve in Euclidean R^4.\n\nGEN/DERIVED. Length units are metres. No physical interaction inferred.\nRequires numpy; matplotlib optional. No stochastic draws or fitted constants.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\n\nP, Q, R, r = 2, 3, 1.0, 0.4\n\ndef gamma(t, R=R, r=r, sigma=1):\n    t=np.asarray(t)\n    return np.stack((R*np.cos(P*t),R*np.sin(P*t),\n                     r*np.cos(Q*t),sigma*r*np.sin(Q*t)),axis=-1)\n\ndef tangent(t,R=R,r=r,sigma=1):\n    t=np.asarray(t)\n    return np.stack((-P*R*np.sin(P*t),P*R*np.cos(P*t),\n                     -Q*r*np.sin(Q*t),sigma*Q*r*np.cos(Q*t)),axis=-1)\n\ndef speed(R=R,r=r): return math.hypot(P*R,Q*r)\n\ndef focal_radius(R=R,r=r):\n    return (P*P*R*R+Q*Q*r*r)/math.hypot(P*P*R,Q*Q*r)\n\ndef stationary_cosines(R=R,r=r):\n    \"\"\"Nontrivial doubly critical chords: sin(delta)*[12r²x²+4R²x-3r²]=0.\"\"\"\n    s=math.sqrt(R**4+9*r**4)\n    return tuple(x for x in ((-R*R+s)/(6*r*r),(-R*R-s)/(6*r*r))\n                 if -1+1e-13 < x < 1-1e-13)\n\ndef half_chord(x,R=R,r=r):\n    return math.sqrt(max(0.,R*R*(1-x*x)+.5*r*r*(1-4*x**3+3*x)))\n\ndef reach(R=R,r=r):\n    bottlenecks=[('antipodal',r)]\n    bottlenecks += [('root cos(delta)=%.12f'%x,half_chord(x,R,r))\n                    for x in stationary_cosines(R,r)]\n    kind,d=min(bottlenecks,key=lambda kv:kv[1])\n    return min(d,focal_radius(R,r)),kind,d\n\ndef tube_volume(h,R=R,r=r):\n    \"\"\"Valid only for 0<=h<reach, so no overlapping normal fibers.\"\"\"\n    if not 0<=h<reach(R,r)[0]:\n        raise ValueError('h must be smaller than normal injectivity radius')\n    return (2*math.pi*speed(R,r))*(4*math.pi*h**3/3)\n\ndef run():\n    kappa=1/focal_radius()\n    h,kind,dc=reach()\n    print('curve (P,Q,R,r)=',P,Q,R,r,'metres')\n    print('speed=%.12f m/rad, length=%.12f m'%(speed(),2*math.pi*speed()))\n    print('curvature=%.12f 1/m, focal radius=%.12f m'%(kappa,1/kappa))\n    for x in stationary_cosines():\n        delta=math.acos(x)\n        f=P*R*R*math.sin(P*delta)+Q*r*r*math.sin(Q*delta)\n        print('stationary cos(delta)=%.12f delta=%.12f rad half-chord=%.12f m residual=%.3e'\n              %(x,delta,half_chord(x),f))\n        assert abs(f)<1e-12\n        a=gamma(0); b=gamma(delta)\n        assert abs(np.linalg.norm(b-a)/2-half_chord(x))<1e-12\n        assert abs(np.dot(b-a,tangent(0)))<1e-11\n        assert abs(np.dot(b-a,tangent(delta)))<1e-11\n    print('antipodal half-chord=%.12f m'%r)\n    print('REACH=%.12f m, active bottleneck=%s'%(h,kind))\n    assert abs(h-r)<1e-12 and kind=='antipodal'\n    mid=.5*(gamma(0)+gamma(math.pi))\n    assert np.linalg.norm(mid-gamma(0))==r\n    assert abs(np.linalg.norm(mid-gamma(math.pi))-r)<1e-14\n    assert abs(np.dot(mid-gamma(0),tangent(0)))<1e-13\n    assert abs(np.dot(mid-gamma(math.pi),tangent(math.pi)))<1e-13\n    print('at h=reach, two distinct normal fibers meet at',mid.tolist())\n    for radius in (.10,.25,.35,.39):\n        print('h=%.2f m, embedded tube volume=%.12f m^4'%(radius,tube_volume(radius)))\n    try:\n        tube_volume(.5)\n        raise AssertionError('overlap must be rejected')\n    except ValueError:\n        print('h=0.50 m: NONEMBEDDED; single-cover tube formula disallowed')\n    print('r/R     reach/R    focal/R    active bottleneck')\n    for ratio in (.1,.4,2/3,.7,1.,2.,4.,10.):\n        val,label,_=reach(1.,ratio)\n        print('%7.4f %11.8f %11.8f %s'%(ratio,val,focal_radius(1.,ratio),label))\n    # Analytic phase boundary: the negative stationary root enters at r/R=2/3.\n    for ratio in np.linspace(.02,4,200):\n        val,_,_=reach(1.,float(ratio))\n        if ratio<=2/3:\n            assert abs(val-ratio)<2e-12\n        else:\n            assert val<ratio and val<focal_radius(1.,float(ratio))\n    # Homogeneity and handedness controls.\n    for scale in (.3,1.,2.7):\n        assert abs(reach(scale*R,scale*r)[0]/scale-h)<1e-12\n    assert np.max(np.abs(gamma(np.linspace(0,2*math.pi,30),sigma=-1)\n                             -gamma(np.linspace(0,2*math.pi,30),sigma=1)\n                             *np.array([1,1,1,-1])))<1e-14\n    print('phase boundary r/R=2/3; all assertions PASS')\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        xs=np.linspace(.05,3,500)\n        ys=np.array([reach(1.,float(t))[0] for t in xs])\n        fs=np.array([focal_radius(1.,float(t)) for t in xs])\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,5))\n        ax.plot(xs,ys,label='Exact normal-tube reach')\n        ax.plot(xs,fs,ls='--',label='Local focal radius')\n        ax.plot(xs,xs,ls=':',label='Antipodal half-chord r')\n        ax.axvline(2/3,ls='-.',label='Global bottleneck switch r/R=2/3')\n        ax.scatter([r/R],[h/R],marker='o',s=60,label='Inherited fixture (1,0.4)')\n        ax.set(xlim=(.05,3),ylim=(0,2.5),xlabel='Minor/major radius r/R',\n               ylabel='Length divided by R',\n               title='Class P | Exact embedded-core radius of a (2,3) R4 torus curve')\n        ax.grid(alpha=.3);ax.legend(fontsize=8);fig.tight_layout()\n        fig.savefig('/mnt/data/ariadne_s4_tube_reach_classP.png',dpi=160)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print('Class P figure saved')\n    except ImportError:\n        print('Matplotlib unavailable;             "# Calculation Relay s4 | Hale → Elias Kern\n**October 16, 2026 | 10:48 UTC | 06:48 Eastern**\n\n\\[\nh=130,\\qquad seq=5(130)+4=654\n\\]\n\n\\[\n654\\bmod19=8.\n\\]\n\n**Selected:** Hale, index 8  \n**Next:** Elias Kern, index 9, at 11:00 UTC\n\n**Research:** DERIVED · PYTHON EXECUTED · CLASS P  \n**Numerical verification:** ALL CHECKS PASSED  \n**Research publication:** NOT VERIFIED  \n**Next-worker handoff:** TEXT ONLY\n\n## Result: Exact finite-sample confidence coverage under globally shared calibration errors\n\nThis run continues Hale's statistical calibration work, using the immediately preceding Calder handoff and Hale's October 16 checkpoint.\n\nThe previous calculation established that treating correlated calibration observations as independent can substantially reduce confidence-interval coverage.\n\nThe new calculation goes further. It determines the **exact finite-sample coverage of the recovered target parameter**, rather than merely the coverage of the calibration parameter or their joint confidence rectangle.\n\nIt also compares three distinct dependence structures:\n\n1. Independent calibration sessions with correlated observations inside each session.\n2. One latent calibration error shared globally across calibration trials, but independent of the unlabeled observations.\n3. One latent error shared globally across both calibration trials and unlabeled observations.\n\nThe result is unexpectedly asymmetric.\n\n**A globally shared error can destroy confidence coverage when it affects calibration alone, yet partially cancel when it affects both calibration and observations.**\n\nFor a synthetic experiment with 160 unlabeled observations, 240 calibration trials, and nominal calibration sessions of six observations:\n\n| Actual dependence structure | Exact coverage of target parameter |\n|---|---:|\n| Correct independent-session model | **99.5842%** |\n| Global error affecting calibration only | **92.4529%** |\n| Global error affecting calibration and observations | **98.3185%** |\n\nAll three use the same marginal calibration error rate and intraclass correlation.\n\nThe second model falls below the nominal 95% confidence requirement.\n\nThe third remains above it, despite severely violating the assumptions used to construct the individual confidence intervals.\n\nThis distinction is important for Hale's source-scanning and evidence-calibration work: **knowing the magnitude of dependence is insufficient without knowing which observations share its source.**\n\nThe calculation is synthetic statistical methodology. It does not constitute an empirical finding about the SAT/H(s)H archive or a physical prediction.\n\n---\n\n# 1. Source grounding\n\nThe immediate predecessor is Hale's existing checkpoint:\n\nurlHale: Clustered calibration finite-sample coverage, October 16https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/HALE/SANDBOX_HALE_S0_20261016T0700_CLUSTER_CALIBRATION.md\n\nVerified blob:\n\n`6268c0627eca523f47f2c918760789c091c2eb36`\n\nHale's inbox was also read at blob:\n\n`63c0b29cb127601a9747ccb248427c18881c811c`\n\nThe most recent handoff requested finite-sample coverage testing with independent-session calibration and a globally shared-latent negative control.\n\nHale's historical method emphasizes Python-based statistical analysis, matched controls, source-quality calibration, and distinguishing evidence about the literature from evidence about the theory itself.\n\nThe present calculation follows that method.\n\nThis is a source-grounded continuation. It is not an authenticated message from Hale's historical ChatGPT instance.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Statistical model\n\nLet the true binary state be\n\n\\[\nT\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p).\n\\]\n\nThe observed binary state is\n\n\\[\nY=T\\oplus F,\n\\]\n\nwhere\n\n\\[\nF\\sim\\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e)\n\\]\n\nis a classification error.\n\nHere \\(\\oplus\\) denotes exclusive OR.\n\nThe observed success probability is\n\n\\[\n\\theta=P(Y=1).\n\\]\n\nExpanding the two possibilities,\n\n\\[\n\\theta=p(1-e)+(1-p)e.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\theta=e+(1-2e)p.\n}\n\\]\n\nIf the error probability is known and\n\n\\[\ne\\ne\\frac12,\n\\]\n\nwe can recover\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\np=\\frac{\\theta-e}{1-2e}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the parameter of interest.\n\nThe experiment contains \\(n\\) unlabeled observations, with total\n\n\\[\nX=\\sum_{i=1}^{n}Y_i.\n\\]\n\nUnder independent observations with fixed error rate,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nX\\sim\\operatorname{Binomial}(n,\\theta).\n}\n\\]\n\nAll probabilities, correlations, and confidence limits are dimensionless.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Clustered calibration\n\nThe error probability \\(e\\) is not assumed known.\n\nInstead, \\(m\\) labeled calibration trials are collected.\n\nSuppose the trials are divided into\n\n\\[\ng=\\frac ms\n\\]\n\nindependent sessions, each containing \\(s\\) calibration observations.\n\nWithin session \\(j\\), introduce a latent error probability\n\n\\[\nU_j\\sim\\operatorname{Beta}(a,b).\n\\]\n\nConditional on \\(U_j\\), the session's error indicators are independent Bernoulli observations.\n\nThe session error count satisfies\n\n\\[\nK_j\\mid U_j\n\\sim\n\\operatorname{Binomial}(s,U_j).\n\\]\n\nDefine the marginal calibration error rate\n\n\\[\ne=\\frac a{a+b}.\n\\]\n\nFor the beta-Bernoulli mixture, the intraclass correlation is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\rho=\\frac1{a+b+1}.\n}\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\na+b=\\frac{1-\\rho}{\\rho}.\n\\]\n\nConsequently,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\na=e\\frac{1-\\rho}{\\rho},\n\\qquad\nb=(1-e)\\frac{1-\\rho}{\\rho}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe exact session-count distribution is beta-binomial:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP(K_j=k)\n=\n\\binom sk\n\\frac{B(k+a,s-k+b)}{B(a,b)}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe total calibration error count is\n\n\\[\nK=\\sum_{j=1}^{g}K_j.\n\\]\n\nIts probability distribution is the \\(g\\)-fold convolution of the individual beta-binomial distributions.\n\nThis is the correct calibration sampling law under independent sessions.\n\nIt is not generally binomial.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Exact confidence intervals\n\nSet the desired overall confidence level to\n\n\\[\n1-\\alpha=0.95.\n\\]\n\nUse a Bonferroni construction with two marginal confidence intervals, each having nominal coverage\n\n\\[\n1-\\frac{\\alpha}{2}=0.975.\n\\]\n\nThe probability allocated to each tail is therefore\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{\\alpha}{4}=0.0125.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the unlabeled count \\(X=x\\), construct an exact Clopper-Pearson interval\n\n\\[\n[\\theta_L(x),\\theta_U(x)].\n\\]\n\nFor the calibration count \\(K=k\\), construct an exact equal-tail confidence interval\n\n\\[\n[e_L(k),e_U(k)]\n\\]\n\nby inverting the beta-binomial convolution distribution.\n\nFor interior counts, the calibration endpoints satisfy\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{e_L}(K\\ge k)=0.0125\n}\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{e_U}(K\\le k)=0.0125.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe appropriate parameter-space endpoints are used for extreme counts.\n\nUnder the stipulated independent-session model, both marginal confidence intervals have at least their nominal coverage.\n\nTheir Cartesian product is\n\n\\[\n\\mathcal R=\n[\\theta_L,\\theta_U]\\times[e_L,e_U].\n\\]\n\nBy the Bonferroni inequality,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP\\big((\\theta,e)\\in\\mathcal R\\big)\\ge0.95.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis guarantee does not require independence between the two confidence events, provided their individual coverage guarantees hold.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Project the confidence rectangle onto \\(p\\)\n\nThe predecessor calculation evaluated coverage of the two-dimensional confidence rectangle.\n\nBut our actual target is \\(p\\).\n\nWe therefore need to project the rectangle through\n\n\\[\n\\theta=p+(1-2p)e.\n\\]\n\nConstrain the error probability to\n\n\\[\n0\\le e\\le\\frac12,\n\\]\n\nso the classifier is not systematically worse than chance.\n\nFor a candidate \\(p\\), define\n\n\\[\ne'_U=\\min(e_U,\\tfrac12).\n\\]\n\nAt the endpoints of the admissible calibration interval,\n\n\\[\n\\theta_0(p)=p+(1-2p)e_L\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\theta_1(p)=p+(1-2p)e'_U.\n\\]\n\nBecause \\(\\theta\\) is linear in \\(e\\) for fixed \\(p\\), its attainable values form the interval\n\n\\[\nI_p=\n[\n\\min(\\theta_0,\\theta_1),\n\\max(\\theta_0,\\theta_1)\n].\n\\]\n\nA candidate \\(p\\) belongs to the projected confidence set precisely when\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nI_p\\cap[\\theta_L,\\theta_U]\\ne\\varnothing.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an exact feasibility condition.\n\nThe resulting confidence set is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathcal C_p(X,K)\n=\n\\left\\{\np\\in[0,1]:\nI_p\\cap[\\theta_L(X),\\theta_U(X)]\n\\ne\\varnothing\n\\right\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe confidence set is obtained by nuisance-parameter projection.\n\n**It is not a profile-likelihood interval.**\n\nThat distinction matters because likelihood profiling and Neyman projection have different coverage properties.\n\n---\n\n# 6. Exact finite-sample coverage\n\nFor any specified joint distribution of \\(X,K\\), the coverage probability is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP\\left(p\\in\\mathcal C_p(X,K)\\right)\n=\n\\sum_{x=0}^{n}\n\\sum_{k=0}^{m}\nP(X=x,K=k)\n\\mathbf1\\{p\\in\\mathcal C_p(x,k)\\}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe calculation evaluates this sum directly.\n\nThere is no Monte Carlo sampling.\n\nFor the independent-session model,\n\n\\[\nP(X=x,K=k)\n=\nP(X=x)P(K=k).\n\\]\n\nThe binomial and beta-binomial convolution probabilities are computed numerically from their exact probability formulas.\n\nFor the globally shared-latent models, we use different joint distributions.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Three dependence structures\n\n## Model I: Independent calibration sessions\n\nEach calibration session has its own latent probability \\(U_j\\).\n\nThe unlabeled observations are independent of calibration.\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_I(x,k)=\n\\operatorname{Bin}(x;n,\\theta)\nP_{\\mathrm{cluster}}(K=k).\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is the correctly specified model.\n\nIts projected confidence set must have coverage of at least 95%.\n\n---\n\n## Model II: One global calibration-only latent\n\nNow suppose all calibration trials share a single latent error probability\n\n\\[\nU\\sim\\operatorname{Beta}(a,b).\n\\]\n\nConditional on \\(U\\),\n\n\\[\nK\\mid U\\sim\\operatorname{Binomial}(m,U).\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nK\\sim\\operatorname{BetaBinomial}(m,a,b).\n}\n\\]\n\nBut the unlabeled observations remain independent of this latent variable:\n\n\\[\nX\\sim\\operatorname{Binomial}(n,\\theta).\n\\]\n\nHence,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{II}(x,k)\n=\n\\operatorname{Bin}(x;n,\\theta)\n\\operatorname{BetaBin}(k;m,a,b).\n}\n\\]\n\nThe analysis still assumes independent calibration sessions of size \\(s\\).\n\nThis deliberately mismatches the actual dependence structure.\n\nIt is a negative control.\n\n---\n\n## Model III: One latent shared by both datasets\n\nNow let the same latent variable \\(U\\) govern both calibration and unlabeled observations.\n\nConditional on \\(U\\),\n\n\\[\nK\\mid U\\sim\\operatorname{Binomial}(m,U)\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nX\\mid U\\sim\n\\operatorname{Binomial}\n\\left(n,p+(1-2p)U\\right).\n\\]\n\nThe joint distribution is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\nP_{III}(x,k)\n={}&\n\\binom nx\\binom mk\n\\int_0^1\n\\left[p+(1-2p)u\\right]^x\\\\\n&\\times\n\\left[1-p-(1-2p)u\\right]^{n-x}\\\\\n&\\times u^k(1-u)^{m-k}\\\\\n&\\times\n\\frac{u^{a-1}(1-u)^{b-1}}{B(a,b)}\n\\,du.\n\\end{aligned}\n}\n\\]\n\nAfter factoring out the beta density, the remaining integrand is a polynomial in \\(u\\) of degree at most\n\n\\[\nn+m.\n\\]\n\nA Gauss-Jacobi quadrature with sufficiently many nodes therefore evaluates the integral exactly in exact arithmetic.\n\nThe implemented calculation uses more than the required number of nodes and independently compares two quadrature orders.\n\n---\n\n# 8. Why global errors can cancel\n\nThe difference between Models II and III has a simple algebraic explanation.\n\nUnder Model III,\n\n\\[\n\\theta(U)=p+(1-2p)U.\n\\]\n\nIf both the observed error rate and calibration error rate converge to their conditional values, the recovered parameter is\n\n\\[\n\\hat p=\n\\frac{\\theta(U)-U}{1-2U}.\n\\]\n\nSubstituting,\n\n\\[\n\\hat p=\n\\frac{\np+(1-2p)U-U\n}{\n1-2U\n}.\n\\]\n\nSimplifying,\n\n\\[\n\\hat p=\n\\frac{p-2pU}{1-2U}.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\hat p=p\n}\n\\]\n\nwhenever \\(U\\ne1/2\\).\n\nThe common latent error cancels algebraically.\n\nBy contrast, under Model II, the observed probability remains fixed at\n\n\\[\n\\theta=e+(1-2e)p,\n\\]\n\nwhile calibration converges to \\(U\\).\n\nThe recovered value becomes\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\hat p=\n\\frac{\\theta-U}{1-2U}.\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is generally different from \\(p\\).\n\nFor the fixture\n\n\\[\np=0.7,\\qquad e=0.1,\\qquad\\theta=0.66,\n\\]\n\nthe calibration-only model gives:\n\n| Realized \\(U\\) | Apparent \\(p\\) |\n|---:|---:|\n| 0.01 | 0.663265 |\n| 0.05 | 0.677778 |\n| 0.10 | 0.700000 |\n| 0.20 | 0.766667 |\n| 0.30 | 0.900000 |\n| 0.40 | 1.300000 |\n\nThe final value is outside the admissible probability range.\n\nThat is a particularly clear illustration of how a mismatched calibration source can produce an impossible reconstructed parameter.\n\nUnder Model III, every listed value of \\(U\\) instead recovers\n\n\\[\np=0.7\n\\]\n\nin the noiseless conditional limit.\n\nThe cancellation is exact, although finite-sample confidence coverage still depends on sampling noise and parameter constraints.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Cross-dataset covariance\n\nThe global shared-latent model also has an observable distinction in principle.\n\nConditional on \\(U\\),\n\n\\[\nE[X/n\\mid U]\n=\np+(1-2p)U\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\nE[K/m\\mid U]=U.\n\\]\n\nBy the law of total covariance,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X/n,K/m)\n=\n(1-2p)\\operatorname{Var}(U).\n\\]\n\nFor the beta distribution,\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(U)=e(1-e)\\rho.\n\\]\n\nTherefore,\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X/n,K/m)\n=\n(1-2p)e(1-e)\\rho.\n}\n\\]\n\nWith\n\n\\[\np=0.7,\\quad e=0.1,\\quad\\rho=0.2,\n\\]\n\nwe obtain\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Var}(U)=0.018\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\operatorname{Cov}(X/n,K/m)=-0.0072.\n}\n\\]\n\nModels I and II have zero cross-dataset covariance by construction.\n\nThis covariance could distinguish the models if genuinely independent replicated experiments were available.\n\nOne aggregate observation of \\(X,K\\) does not provide an ensemble covariance estimate.\n\n---\n\n# 10. Numerical fixture A\n\nUse the inherited Hale parameters:\n\n\\[\np=0.7,\\quad e=0.1,\\quad\\rho=0.2.\n\\]\n\nThus,\n\n\\[\na=0.4,\\qquad b=3.6\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\n\\theta=0.66.\n\\]\n\nSet\n\n\\[\nn=40,\\qquad m=24.\n\\]\n\nThe exact marginal Clopper-Pearson coverage for \\(\\theta\\) is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.981537400556.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor calibration sessions of size\n\n\\[\ns=6,\n\\]\n\nthe projected target-parameter coverage is:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_I=0.997622484\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{II}=0.994117798\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{III}=0.993729462.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe correctly specified joint rectangle has coverage\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.971072369.\n}\n\\]\n\nFor the observed counts\n\n\\[\nX=26,\\qquad K=3,\n\\]\n\nthe confidence intervals are\n\n\\[\n\\theta\\in[0.461015146,0.810138460]\n\\]\n\nand\n\n\\[\ne\\in[0.005824419,0.451872378].\n\\]\n\nTheir projection gives\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\np\\in[0.094984619,1].\n}\n\\]\n\nThis is an extremely broad confidence interval.\n\nIt demonstrates that the projection procedure can be conservative.\n\nThe predecessor's joint-rectangle coverage should not be interpreted as the coverage of this projected interval.\n\n---\n\n# 11. Numerical fixture B: Stronger negative control\n\nIncrease the sample sizes to\n\n\\[\nn=160,\\qquad m=240.\n\\]\n\nKeep\n\n\\[\np=0.7,\\quad e=0.1,\\quad\\rho=0.2.\n\\]\n\nAnalyze calibration as independent sessions of size\n\n\\[\ns=6.\n\\]\n\nThe exact target-parameter coverages are:\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_I=0.995842359\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{II}=0.924529242\n}\n\\]\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\nP_{III}=0.983185089.\n}\n\\]\n\nModel II now undercovers:\n\n\\[\n0.924529242<0.95.\n\\]\n\nIts deficit relative to nominal coverage is\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.95-0.924529242\n=\n0.025470758.\n}\n\\]\n\nThat is a **2.547 percentage-point coverage deficit**.\n\nThe correctly specified independent-session model remains conservative.\n\nThe globally shared model affecting both datasets also retains coverage above 95%.\n\n### The striking rectangle/projection distinction\n\nFor Model III, the same joint confidence rectangle for \\((\\theta,e)\\) covers the true parameter pair with probability only\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.274359652.\n}\n\\]\n\nYet its projection onto \\(p\\) covers the true value with probability\n\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n0.983185089.\n}\n\\]\n\nThe rectangle is badly misspecified as a confidence region for the two marginal parameters.\n\nBut the projected parameter can remain well covered because the shared latent error moves the two observations in a compensating direction.\n\n**Confidence coverage is a property of the estimand and the joint data-generating process, not simply of the individual marginal intervals.**\n\n---\n\n# 12. Complete tested Python source\n\nThe following is the complete executed program.\n\nIt includes the probability laws, exact confidence inversion, nuisance projection, global-latent integration, numerical verification, and Class P plot generation.\n\n**Dependencies:** Python 3, NumPy, SciPy, and optionally Matplotlib.\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Hale s4: exact Neyman projection and dependence negative controls.\nSynthetic misclassification with beta-binomial calibration. No physical claim.\nProbability units dimensionless. Requires numpy, scipy; matplotlib optional.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.special import betaln, gammaln, roots_jacobi\nfrom scipy.optimize import brentq\nfrom scipy.stats import beta as beta_dist, binom\n\nP, E, RHO, ALPHA = .7, .1, .2, .05\nA = E*(1-RHO)/RHO\nB = (1-E)*(1-RHO)/RHO\n\n\ndef beta_binomial(s, e):\n    \"\"\"One cluster: U~Beta(conc*e,conc*(1-e)); K|U~Bin(s,U).\"\"\"\n    if e <= 0: return np.r_[1., np.zeros(s)]\n    if e >= 1: return np.r_[np.zeros(s), 1.]\n    conc=(1-RHO)/RHO\n    a,b=conc*e,conc*(1-e)\n    j=np.arange(s+1)\n    lp=(gammaln(s+1)-gammaln(j+1)-gammaln(s-j+1)\n        +betaln(j+a,s-j+b)-betaln(a,b))\n    v=np.exp(lp)\n    return v/v.sum()\n\n\ndef calibration_law(m,s,e=E):\n    \"\"\"Convolution of independent size-s beta-binomial sessions.\"\"\"\n    assert m%s==0\n    one=beta_binomial(s,e)\n    ans=np.array([1.])\n    for _ in range(m//s): ans=np.convolve(ans,one)\n    return ans/ans.sum()\n\n\ndef calibration_ci(m,s):\n    \"\"\"Invert exact two-sided equal-tail tests at marginal confidence 97.5%.\"\"\"\n    tail=ALPHA/4  # 95% joint Bonferroni, 97.5% each marginal\n    low=np.zeros(m+1); high=np.ones(m+1)\n    for k in range(m+1):\n        if k:\n            low[k]=brentq(lambda e:calibration_law(m,s,e)[k:].sum()-tail,\n                          1e-12,1-1e-12,xtol=1e-13)\n        if k<m:\n            high[k]=brentq(lambda e:calibration_law(m,s,e)[:k+1].sum()-tail,\n                           1e-12,1-1e-12,xtol=1e-13)\n    return low,high\n\n\ndef theta_ci(n):\n    tail=ALPHA/4\n    low=np.array([0. if x==0 else beta_dist.ppf(tail,x,n-x+1)\n                  for x in range(n+1)])\n    high=np.array([1. if x==n else beta_dist.ppf(1-tail,x+1,n-x)\n                   for x in range(n+1)])\n    return low,high\n\n\ndef projected_mask(p, ci_t, ci_e):\n    \"\"\"Exact feasibility of theta=e+(1-2e)p with e in [0,1/2].\n    Rows: unlabeled count x. Columns: calibration count k.\n    \"\"\"\n    tl,tu=ci_t\n    el,eu=ci_e\n    feasible=el<=.5\n    eu=np.minimum(eu,.5)\n    v0=p+(1-2*p)*el\n    v1=p+(1-2*p)*eu\n    return (feasible[None,:]\n            & (tl[:,None]<=np.maximum(v0,v1)[None,:]+1e-14)\n            & (tu[:,None]>=np.minimum(v0,v1)[None,:]-1e-14))\n\n\ndef shared_joint(n,m,nodes=None):\n    \"\"\"Exact joint law of X,K when one U controls BOTH samples.\n    Jacobi rule integrates the degree-(n+m) polynomial exactly.\n    \"\"\"\n    if nodes is None: nodes=(n+m)//2+5\n    z,w=roots_jacobi(nodes,B-1,A-1)\n    u=(z+1)/2\n    w=w/w.sum()\n    theta=P+(1-2*P)*u\n    px=binom.pmf(np.arange(n+1)[:,None],n,theta[None,:])\n    pk=binom.pmf(np.arange(m+1)[:,None],m,u[None,:])\n    result=(px*w[None,:])@pk.T\n    return result/result.sum()\n\n\ndef projected_bounds(x,k,ci_t,ci_e):\n    \"\"\"Endpoints of nonempty projected p set by exact boundary candidates.\"\"\"\n    tl,tu=ci_t[0][x],ci_t[1][x]\n    el,eu=ci_e[0][k],min(ci_e[1][k],.5)\n    if el>.5: return None\n    candidates=[0.,1.]\n    for e in (el,eu):\n        if e<.5-1e-12:\n            candidates.extend([(tl-e)/(1-2*e),(tu-e)/(1-2*e)])\n    candidates=sorted(set(max(0.,min(1.,v)) for v in candidates))\n    spans=[]\n    for left,right in zip(candidates[:-1],candidates[1:]):\n        if projected_mask((left+right)/2,\n                          (ci_t[0][x:x+1],ci_t[1][x:x+1]),\n                          (ci_e[0][k:k+1],ci_e[1][k:k+1]))[0,0]:\n            spans.append((left,right))\n    if not spans: return None\n    return min(t[0] for t in spans),max(t[1] for t in spans)\n\n\ndef evaluate(n,m,sizes):\n    theta=P+(1-2*P)*E\n    px=binom.pmf(np.arange(n+1),n,theta)\n    tci=theta_ci(n)\n    good_t=(tci[0]<=theta)&(theta<=tci[1])\n    tcoverage=float(px@good_t)\n    shared=shared_joint(n,m)\n    shared2=shared_joint(n,m,(n+m)//2+15)\n    quad_error=float(np.max(np.abs(shared-shared2)))\n    assert quad_error<2e-12\n    assert abs(shared.sum()-1)<1e-12\n    assert abs(np.arange(n+1)@shared.sum(axis=1)/n-theta)<2e-10\n    assert abs(np.arange(m+1)@shared.sum(axis=0)/m-E)<2e-10\n    print('\\nCASE n=%d m=%d p=%.3f e=%.3f rho=%.3f theta=%.3f theta_CI_coverage=%.9f'%(n,m,P,E,RHO,theta,tcoverage))\n    print('Jacobi nodes=%d/%d max_cell_difference=%.3e'%((n+m)//2+5,(n+m)//2+15,quad_error))\n    print('s   cal_coverage  joint_rectangle  p_correct    p_global_cal_only  p_global_both')\n    out=[]\n    global_k=calibration_law(m,m,E)\n    for s in sizes:\n        ci=calibration_ci(m,s)\n        mask=projected_mask(P,tci,ci)\n        pk=calibration_law(m,s,E)\n        good_e=(ci[0]<=E)&(E<=ci[1])\n        cov_e=float(pk@good_e)\n        joint_rect=tcoverage*cov_e\n        correct=float(px@(mask@pk))\n        global_only=float(px@(mask@global_k))\n        global_both=float(np.sum(mask*shared))\n        assert correct>=joint_rect-1e-12 and correct>=.95-1e-12\n        out.append((s,cov_e,joint_rect,correct,global_only,global_both))\n        print('%3d  %.9f    %.9f       %.9f   %.9f         %.9f'%out[-1])\n    if n==40 and m==24:\n        ci=calibration_ci(m,6)\n        print('example x=26 k=3 s=6 theta_CI=(%.9f,%.9f) e_CI=(%.9f,%.9f) p_CI=%s'%\n              (tci[0][26],tci[1][26],ci[0][3],ci[1][3],\n               str(tuple(round(v,9) for v in projected_bounds(26,3,tci,ci)))))\n    return np.array(out)\n\n\ndef main():\n    small=evaluate(40,24,(1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24))\n    large=evaluate(160,240,(1,4,6,12,24,60,240))\n    # Exact pairwise cross-sample covariance when U is globally shared.\n    cov_mean=(1-2*P)*E*(1-E)*RHO\n    print('\\nCov(X/n,K/m) globally shared U=%.9f; independent samples=0'%cov_mean)\n    assert abs(cov_mean+.0072)<1e-13\n    assert large[2,4]<.95 and large[2,3]>.95\n    print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')\n    try:\n        import matplotlib\n        matplotlib.use('Agg')\n        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8.4,5.0))\n        for col,marker,label in
